full_output.paper_title: Low-level resistance of Staphylococcus aureus to thrombin-induced platelet microbicidal protein 1 in vitro associated with qacA gene carriage is independent of multidrug efflux pump activity.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the qacA gene as a mediator of low-level resistance to thrombin-induced platelet microbicidal protein 1 (tPMP-1) in Staphylococcus aureus, independent of multidrug efflux pump activity.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized cloning, susceptibility assays, and biochemical analyses to validate the role of qacA in tPMP-1 resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Crystal structure of the Mycobacterium fortuitum class A beta-lactamase: structural basis for broad substrate specificity.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the class A beta-lactamase from Mycobacterium fortuitum (MFO), highlighting its broad substrate specificity and structural features that contribute to its ability to hydrolyze various beta-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: X-ray crystallography was used to determine the structure of the MFO beta-lactamase, providing insights into its active site and substrate interactions.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of the lipopolysaccharide modifications controlled by the Salmonella PmrA/PmrB system mediating resistance to Fe(III) and Al(III).

pmrG.mechanism: dephosphorylation of the Hep(II) phosphate in the core region of the lipopolysaccharide
pmrG.validation_method: mutant analysis and phosphatase activity assay
pmrG.evidence_note: The PmrG protein is a phosphatase that targets the Hep(II) phosphate in the core region of the lipopolysaccharide.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the PmrA-regulated genes pmrC, pmrG, ugd, and the pbgPE operon as essential for Fe(III) and Al(III) resistance in Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium through modifications of the lipopolysaccharide.
full_output.methodology: Genetic analysis, mutant construction, plasmid complementation, and biochemical assays were used to identify and validate the roles of the genes in Fe(III) and Al(III) resistance.

sarA.notes: Disruption of sarA led to decreased resistance to erythromycin and kanamycin.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and antimicrobial susceptibility pattern of methicillin resistant Staphylococcus aureus isolates from Trinidad & Tobago.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that all MRSA isolates were resistant to ceftriaxone, erythromycin, gentamicin, and penicillin but were 100% sensitive to vancomycin, rifampin, and chloramphenicol.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed 1912 Staphylococcus aureus isolates using various methods including oxacillin disk diffusion, MRSA-Screen latex agglutination test, and E-test for methicillin resistance, along with antimicrobial susceptibility testing via the modified Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that a nonmedicated dietary supplement correlated with increased prevalence of streptomycin-sulfa-tetracycline-resistant (SSuT) Escherichia coli on a dairy farm, suggesting that environmental components other than antibiotics can select for resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed the prevalence of antimicrobial-resistant E. coli in calves before and after discontinuing a medicated dietary supplement, conducted growth experiments in LB broth, and performed statistical analyses.
full_output.sample_size: 2001 (n=18 calves), 2004 (n=30 calves), and 27 neonatal calves in reintroduction experiments

full_output.paper_title: Mutations Prevalent among Rifampin- and Isoniazid-Resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis Isolates from a Hospital in Vietnam.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in the rpoB gene associated with rifampin resistance and mutations in the katG and inhA genes associated with isoniazid resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates from Vietnam.
full_output.methodology: Sequencing of the rpoB, katG, and inhA genes in rifampin- and isoniazid-resistant M. tuberculosis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Evolution of Metallo-β-Lactamase-Producing Pseudomonas aeruginosa in a Nosocomial Setting of High-Level Endemicity.

blaVIM-1.validation_method: dot blot hybridization and PCR-RFLP analysis

blaVIM-2.validation_method: dot blot hybridization and PCR-RFLP analysis

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the molecular evolution of metallo-beta-lactamase-producing Pseudomonas aeruginosa strains, identifying bla VIM-1 and bla VIM-2 as the primary resistance genes responsible for carbapenem resistance in the hospital setting.
full_output.methodology: Molecular methods including dot blot hybridization, PCR-RFLP, and Southern blot analysis were used to characterize the resistance genes and their genetic environments.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of the TB-Biochip oligonucleotide microarray system for rapid detection of rifampin resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

full_output.methodology: The study used a combination of hybridization, sequencing, and PCR to evaluate the TB-Biochip system for detecting rifampin resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Serogroups, K1 antigen, and antimicrobial resistance patterns of Aeromonas spp. strains isolated from different sources in Mexico.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high levels of resistance to ampicillin and ampicillin/sulbactam in Aeromonas strains, with 100% resistance observed. Additionally, the K1 capsular antigen was prevalent in clinical isolates, suggesting potential roles in virulence.
full_output.methodology: The study used the Vitek AutoMicrobic system for antimicrobial susceptibility testing and serotyping methods to identify Aeromonas strains.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation of antibiotic-resistant bacteria from the air plume downwind of a swine confined or concentrated animal feeding operation.
full_output.key_findings: The study found higher levels of antibiotic-resistant bacteria, particularly Staphylococcus aureus, downwind of a swine confined animal feeding operation compared to upwind areas. These bacteria showed resistance to multiple antibiotic classes, including tetracycline, oxytetracycline, erythromycin, ampicillin, and penicillin.
full_output.methodology: The study used Andersen two-stage samplers to collect bacterial samples, followed by the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method to determine antibiotic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Naturally processed dermcidin-derived peptides do not permeabilize bacterial membranes and kill microorganisms irrespective of their charge.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that naturally processed dermcidin-derived peptides exhibit antimicrobial activity against various bacteria, including gram-positive and gram-negative organisms, without permeabilizing bacterial membranes. The peptides' activity is independent of their charge.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized antimicrobial assays, membrane permeability tests, and structural analysis to evaluate the activity of dermcidin-derived peptides.

full_output.paper_title: Population genetics study of isoniazid resistance mutations and evolution of multidrug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

full_output.paper_title: Evolution and global dissemination of macrolide-resistant group A streptococci.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple macrolide resistance genes (mef(A), erm(A), and erm(B)) in group A streptococci, highlighting the independent acquisition of resistance through horizontal gene transfer and the global dissemination of resistant clones.
full_output.methodology: The study uses multilocus sequence typing (MLST) and PCR to analyze the genetic diversity and resistance mechanisms of 212 macrolide-resistant group A streptococcal isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Multicity outbreak of carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii isolates producing the carbapenemase OXA-40.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the carbapenemase OXA-40 as the cause of carbapenem resistance in a multicity outbreak of Acinetobacter baumannii isolates.

full_output.paper_title: MarA-like regulator of multidrug resistance in Yersinia pestis.

marA47 Yp.mechanism: overexpression of AcrAB multidrug efflux pump

full_output.paper_title: Efficacy of cethromycin, a new ketolide, against Streptococcus pneumoniae susceptible or resistant to erythromycin in a murine pneumonia model.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that cethromycin is highly effective against both erythromycin-susceptible and -resistant strains of Streptococcus pneumoniae in a murine pneumonia model, showing superior in vivo activity compared to erythromycin.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the efficacy of cethromycin and erythromycin against Streptococcus pneumoniae strains in a murine pneumonia model through in vivo experiments, measuring survival rates, bacterial clearance, and pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic parameters.

full_output.paper_title: High-level mupirocin resistance within methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus pandemic lineages.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the ileS2 gene as responsible for high-level mupirocin resistance in methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) pandemic lineages, highlighting the role of conjugative plasmids in its dissemination.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection, plasmid analysis, and conjugation experiments were used to characterize the ileS2 gene and its role in mupirocin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical outcome and risk factors related to extended-spectrum beta-lactamase-producing Klebsiella spp. infection among hospitalized patients.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Klebsiella spp. as a significant cause of nosocomial infections, highlighting risk factors such as mechanical ventilation, central venous catheter use, and antimicrobial exposure, particularly fourth-generation cephalosporins and quinolones.
full_output.methodology: Cross-sectional and prospective cohort analyses of patients with Klebsiella spp. infections, including microbiological testing and statistical analysis of risk factors and clinical outcomes.

full_output.paper_title: Genome sequence alterations detected upon passage of Burkholderia mallei ATCC 23344 in culture and in mammalian hosts.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies genome sequence alterations in Burkholderia mallei ATCC 23344 upon passage in culture and in mammalian hosts, highlighting the impact of these variations on gene expression patterns.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic detection of carbapenem-susceptible metallo-beta-lactamase-producing gram-negative bacilli in the clinical laboratory.

full_output.paper_title: DNA methylase activity as a marker for the presence of a family of phage-like elements conferring efflux-mediated macrolide resistance in streptococci.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the dinuclear cobalt-beta-lactamase from Bacillus cereus (BcII) and demonstrates its ability to hydrolyze beta-lactam antibiotics, highlighting its catalytic efficiency and the role of cobalt ions in the enzymatic process.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of specific gene sequences conserved in contemporary epidemic strains of Salmonella enterica.

full_output.paper_title: VEB-1 Extended-spectrum beta-lactamase-producing Acinetobacter baumannii, France.

full_output.paper_title: Multiple genetic elements carry the tetracycline resistance gene tet(W) in the animal pathogen Arcanobacterium pyogenes.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in the gyrA and parC genes of Escherichia coli that confer resistance to quinolones such as nalidixic acid, norfloxacin, and ciprofloxacin.
full_output.methodology: The study used nucleotide sequencing to confirm mutations in the quinolone resistance-determining regions of gyrA and parC genes.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic and molecular analysis of penicillin-nonsusceptible Streptococcus pneumoniae isolates in Poland.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes penicillin-nonsusceptible Streptococcus pneumoniae isolates in Poland, identifying modifications in pbp1a, pbp2x, and pbp2b genes as key mechanisms of penicillin resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR-RFLP of pbp genes, MLST, and PFGE analysis were used to characterize the resistance mechanisms and genetic diversity of the isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the prevalence of extended-spectrum cephalosporin (ESC) and ciprofloxacin (CIP) resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates, with higher resistance rates observed in nosocomial infections compared to community-acquired ones.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of 377 patients with K. pneumoniae bacteremia, including antimicrobial susceptibility testing via disk diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular analysis of isoleucyl-tRNA synthetase mutations in clinical isolates of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus with low-level mupirocin resistance.

mutations_found.effect_on_function: mutation of this residue causes steric repulsion to mupirocin
K226T are on the outer surface adjacent to the tRNA molecule about 20 Å from the editing active site
F227L are on the outer surface adjacent to the tRNA molecule about 20 Å from the editing active site
V588 is located in a hydrophobic pocket that interacts directly with the fatty acid side chain of mupirocin, mutation of this residue causes steric repulsion to mupirocin
Q612H has potential to interact with mupirocin. Q612 sits close to the core of IleS Rossman fold motif, where it forms a water-bridged hydrogen bond with the side chain of D635
V767D lies in the interior surface of the cylindrical central helical domain of the IleS, distal to the tRNA binding site

ileS.notes: All mutations were identified in low-level mupirocin-resistant MRSA isolates.
ileS.evidence_note: The paper explicitly states that the mutations P187F, K226T, F227L, V588F, Q612H, and V767D are associated with low-level mupirocin resistance in MRSA isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies six missense mutations in the ileS gene (P187F, K226T, F227L, V588F, Q612H, and V767D) that are associated with low-level mupirocin resistance in MRSA isolates.
full_output.methodology: Sequencing of the ileS gene fragments and structural analysis of the mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic detection of methicillin resistance in Staphylococcus aureus by disk diffusion testing and Etest on Mueller-Hinton agar.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the effectiveness of cefoxitin disk diffusion and Etest for detecting methicillin resistance in Staphylococcus aureus, suggesting adjustments to CLSI breakpoints for improved accuracy.
full_output.methodology: The study used disk diffusion testing and Etest on Mueller-Hinton agar to evaluate methicillin resistance in S. aureus isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Bacterial identification, clinical significance, and antimicrobial susceptibilities of Acinetobacter ursingii and Acinetobacter schindleri, two frequently misidentified opportunistic pathogens.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the antimicrobial susceptibilities of Acinetobacter ursingii and Acinetobacter schindleri, highlighting their resistance patterns to various antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic identification, 16S rRNA gene sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were conducted.

full_output.paper_title: Acquired gentamicin resistance by permeability impairment in Enterococcus faecalis.

atp.notes: No mutations were found in the structural genes for the F o channel.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that acquired gentamicin resistance in Enterococcus faecalis is due to impaired permeability rather than traditional resistance mechanisms such as enzymatic modification or target alteration.
full_output.methodology: The study used gentamicin uptake studies, DNA sequencing, and real-time PCR to investigate the mechanism of resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study detected Mycobacterium tuberculosis in sputum samples from Suruí Indian subjects and identified one MTB genotype showing resistance to rifampicin and isoniazid.
full_output.methodology: PCR and culture analysis, drug resistance testing, genotyping techniques including MIRU-VNTR and spoligotyping.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of rifampin resistance patterns in Mycobacterium tuberculosis strains isolated in Iran by polymerase chain reaction-single-strand conformation polymorphism and direct sequencing methods.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in the rpoB gene of Mycobacterium tuberculosis strains that confer resistance to rifampin, with specific mutations at codons 511, 512, 516, 523, 526, and 531.
full_output.methodology: PCR-SSCP and direct sequencing were used to detect and characterize mutations in the rpoB gene of M. tuberculosis strains.

full_output.paper_title: Multidrug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis, Bangui, Central African Republic.

rpoB.notes: Mutations in rpoB are responsible for rifampin resistance.

mutT1.notes: Synonymous SNP in mutT1 is present in cluster E and F strains.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies rpoB mutations responsible for rifampin resistance in multidrug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis strains in Bangui, Central African Republic. A synonymous SNP in the mutT1 gene is also noted in cluster E and F strains.
full_output.methodology: Spoligotyping and sequencing of rpoB and mutT1 genes were used to analyze genetic diversity and resistance mechanisms in MDR M. tuberculosis strains.

full_output.paper_title: Fluoroquinolone-resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies two novel chromosomal mutations, S79Y in parC and Q118K in gyrA, which confer fluoroquinolone resistance in Streptococcus pneumoniae.
full_output.methodology: Sequencing of QRDRs and transformation experiments to validate resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: High-level vancomycin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus isolates associated with a polymicrobial biofilm.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies vanA, tet(S), and tet(U) as key genes contributing to vancomycin and tetracycline resistance in VRSA isolates, highlighting the role of plasmid-mediated gene transfer in the emergence of multidrug-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.methodology: PCR, plasmid analysis, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize resistance genes and mechanisms in VRSA isolates.
full_output.sample_size: Multiple isolates from a single patient and various body sites.

full_output.paper_title: In vivo gene expression analysis identifies genes required for enhanced colonization of the mouse urinary tract by uropathogenic Escherichia coli strain CFT073 dsdA.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies genes such as hlyA, papA, papH, ompF, dppA, and ibpB that are essential for the hypercolonization of the mouse urinary tract by uropathogenic E. coli strain CFT073 dsdA. These genes are up-regulated in the dsdA mutant and their deletion reduces the hypercolonization phenotype.
full_output.methodology: In vivo gene expression analysis using microarrays, mutant construction via λ-Red recombination, and competitive infection in a murine model of urinary tract infection.
full_output.sample_size: 18 mutants of CFT073 dsdA and wild type, 8 mutants of CFT073 and wild type

full_output.paper_title: A peptidoglycan hydrolase motif within the mycobacteriophage TM4 tape measure protein promotes efficient infection of stationary phase cells.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies MSMEG3721 and MSMEG0642 as peptidoglycan-degrading enzymes and demonstrates that the TM4 Tmp mt3 motif enhances phage infection of stationary phase cells by facilitating peptidoglycan hydrolysis.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized genetic manipulation, zymogram assays, and phage infection experiments to investigate the role of MSMEG3721, MSMEG0642, and TM4 Tmp mt3 in peptidoglycan degradation and phage infection.

full_output.paper_title: Complete and SOS-mediated response of Staphylococcus aureus to the antibiotic ciprofloxacin.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies SACOL1400 and SACOL1955 as Y-family polymerases involved in induced mutation in Staphylococcus aureus in response to ciprofloxacin. These genes are up-regulated and contribute to the SOS response and mutation under antibiotic stress.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptional profiling using DNA microarrays and RT-PCR to analyze gene expression changes in Staphylococcus aureus in response to ciprofloxacin.

full_output.paper_title: M.SpyI, a DNA Methyltransferase Encoded on a mefA Chimeric Element, Modifies the Genome of Streptococcus pyogenes.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies M.SpyI, a DNA methyltransferase encoded on the mefA chimeric element Φ10394.4, which methylates genomic DNA of Streptococcus pyogenes, leading to resistance against SmaI restriction.
full_output.methodology: Cloning, expression, and activity assays of the spyIM gene in E. coli, along with bisulfite modification analysis of genomic DNA.

full_output.paper_title: Occurrence of virulence and antimicrobial resistance genes in Escherichia coli isolates from different aquatic ecosystems within the St. Clair River and Detroit River areas.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of antimicrobial resistance genes such as blaTEM, tet(A), tet(B), and sulII in Escherichia coli isolates from various aquatic ecosystems in the St. Clair River and Detroit River areas.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized DNA microarray technology to detect virulence and antimicrobial resistance genes in E. coli isolates from surface water samples.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of CTX-M-Type Extended-Spectrum-β-Lactamase Genes Using Real-Time PCR and Pyrosequencing
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes CTX-M-type extended-spectrum beta-lactamase genes using real-time PCR and pyrosequencing, highlighting the predominance of bla CTX-M-15 in ESBL-producing E. coli isolates.
full_output.methodology: Real-time PCR and pyrosequencing were used to detect and differentiate CTX-M-type beta-lactamase genes in clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: SGI1-K, a variant of the SGI1 genomic island carrying a mercury resistance region, in Salmonella enterica serovar Kentucky.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the aacCA5 and aadA7 gene cassette array in SGI1-K, which confers resistance to gentamicin, streptomycin, and spectinomycin in Salmonella enterica serovar Kentucky.
full_output.methodology: PCR mapping, DNA sequencing, and Southern hybridization were used to characterize the genetic elements and resistance mechanisms in the Salmonella strain.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of multidrug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several novel mutations in genes associated with drug resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis, including rpoB, katG, embB, pncA, rpsL, rrs, and gyrA, which contribute to resistance against rifampin, isoniazid, ethambutol, pyrazinamide, streptomycin, and fluoroquinolones.

full_output.paper_title: Catalase (KatA) and Alkyl Hydroperoxide Reductase (AhpC) Have Compensatory Roles in Peroxide Stress Resistance and Are Required for Survival, Persistence, and Nasal Colonization in Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: KatA and AhpC have compensatory roles in peroxide stress resistance and are essential for survival, persistence, and nasal colonization in Staphylococcus aureus.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in the parC, parE, and gyrA genes that confer fluoroquinolone resistance in Streptococcus pneumoniae, with varying fitness costs associated with each mutation.

full_output.paper_title: Increase in multidrug transport activity is associated with oocyte maturation in sea stars.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies ABCB proteins, specifically P-gp, as playing a role in multidrug resistance during oocyte maturation in sea stars.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic-Resistant Invasive Pneumococcal Clones in Italy

mutations_found.validated_by: sequencing of the PBP2B transpeptidase domain

pbp2b.notes: The T445A mutation in pbp2b was associated with reduced susceptibility to penicillin.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antibiotic-resistant invasive pneumococcal clones in Italy, including those with mutations in pbp2b and pbp2x genes associated with penicillin resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used antibiotic susceptibility testing, serotyping, pbp2b and pbp2x gene restriction profiling, PFGE, and MLST to characterize the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Lateral gene transfer in vitro in the intracellular pathogen Chlamydia trachomatis.

mutations_found.validated_by: sequencing of DNA from polyclonal doubly resistant isolates

full_output.paper_title: Inhibitory Impact of Bifidobacteria on the Transfer of β-Lactam Resistance among Enterobacteriaceae in the Gnotobiotic Mouse Digestive Tract
full_output.key_findings: Bifidobacteria inhibit the transfer of beta-lactam resistance genes (blaSHV-5 and blaCTX-M-15) between Enterobacteriaceae in gnotobiotic mice, suggesting a potential role in controlling antibiotic resistance dissemination.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial resistance and their genetic location in MRSA isolated in Kuwait hospitals, 1994-2004.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high-level mupirocin resistance encoded by the mupH gene on a 38-kb plasmid in MRSA isolates from Kuwait hospitals.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis and evaluation of isosteres of N-methyl indolo[3,2-b]-quinoline (cryptolepine) as new antiinfective agents.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that phenothiazines synergistically interact with various antimicrobial agents against Burkholderia pseudomallei, enhancing their antimicrobial potency by inhibiting efflux pumps.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro effects of antimicrobial agents on planktonic and biofilm forms of Staphylococcus lugdunensis clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Cloning and characterization of the pyrrolomycin biosynthetic gene clusters from Actinosporangium vitaminophilum ATCC 31673 and Streptomyces sp. strain UC 11065.

full_output.methodology: Cloning, sequencing, and disruption experiments were used to identify and validate the biosynthetic gene clusters.

full_output.paper_title: Cold shock domain proteins and glycine-rich RNA-binding proteins from Arabidopsis thaliana can promote the cold adaptation process in Escherichia coli.

full_output.paper_title: Catalases are NAD(P)H-dependent tellurite reductases.

full_output.methodology: Gene cloning, expression in E. coli, enzyme activity assays, and resistance testing.

full_output.paper_title: Development of signature-tagged mutagenesis in Burkholderia pseudomallei to identify genes important in survival and pathogenesis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the aroB gene in Burkholderia pseudomallei, which is involved in the shikimate pathway and essential for the biosynthesis of aromatic compounds. Mutations in aroB led to auxotrophy and reduced virulence, making it a potential vaccine candidate.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies acrAB gene amplification as a significant mechanism for multidrug resistance in E. coli, demonstrating that genetic amplifications can lead to transient but clinically relevant resistance.

ermA.source: Phenotypic and Genotypic Characterization of Streptococcus pyogenes Isolates Displaying the MLSB Phenotype of Macrolide Resistance in Spain, 1999 to 2005
ermA.evidence_note: The paper states that isolates harboring the ermA gene showed moderate erythromycin resistance (MIC 50, 4 μg/ml) and were susceptible to clindamycin and telithromycin.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of resistance genes ermB, ermA, mef, and tetM in MLSB-resistant Streptococcus pyogenes isolates in Spain, highlighting the emergence of clones such as emm11/T11/ST403 and emm28/T28/ST52 associated with these resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and molecular typing methods including emm typing, T typing, and multilocus sequence typing (MLST) were used to analyze resistance genes and clones.

full_output.paper_title: Staphylococcus aureus Strains Isolated from Bloodstream Infections Changed Significantly in 2006
full_output.key_findings: The study reports a significant increase in the incidence of Staphylococcus aureus bloodstream infections (BSI) in 2006, particularly involving methicillin-sensitive S. aureus (MSSA) and nonmultiresistant methicillin-resistant S. aureus (NORSA) strains. It highlights the emergence of tst gene-positive MSSA strains and the potential role of fluoroquinolone use in the acquisition of resistance and virulence genes.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the analysis of 358 S. aureus strains isolated from BSI cases over three years (2004-2006), including antimicrobial susceptibility testing, molecular typing, and virulence gene detection.

full_output.paper_title: Analysis of sof Gene Diversity Using BLAST Miner

pbp2x.mechanism: chromosomal mutation leading to penicillin resistance

full_output.key_findings: The study introduces BLAST Miner, a tool for analyzing highly recombined genes, focusing on the structural features of pbp2x and sof alleles. It identifies modules within these genes that reveal insights into recombination and genetic organization.
full_output.methodology: The study uses a BLAST-based method called BLAST Miner to analyze sequence data and identify modules within genes, focusing on pbp2x and sof alleles.

full_output.paper_title: N-Thiolated beta-lactams: Studies on the mode of action and identification of a primary cellular target in Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified that N-thiolated beta-lactams inhibit fatty acid biosynthesis in Staphylococcus aureus by forming alkyl-CoA mixed disulfides, targeting coenzyme A (CoA) as a primary cellular target.
full_output.methodology: The study used antimicrobial susceptibility testing, MIC assays, and metabolic studies to identify the mechanism of action of N-thiolated beta-lactams.

full_output.paper_title: Products of the Escherichia coli acid fitness island attenuate metabolite stress at extremely low pH and mediate a cell density-dependent acid resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies hdeA, slp, and yhiF as critical genes in E. coli's acid resistance mechanism, protecting against organic acid metabolites under extreme low pH conditions.
full_output.methodology: Gene knockout and complementation experiments, acid resistance assays, and mutant analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Development and persistence of antimicrobial resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa: a longitudinal observation in mechanically ventilated patients.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the role of ampC β-lactamase, oprD porin, and mexC efflux pump in the development of antimicrobial resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Resistance to β-lactams and fluoroquinolones was associated with increased expression of ampC and mexC, respectively, while imipenem resistance was linked to decreased oprD expression.
full_output.methodology: The study used quantitative real-time PCR to analyze gene expression and disk diffusion for susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: rpoN Gene of Pseudomonas aeruginosa Alters Its Susceptibility to Quinolones and Carbapenems
full_output.key_findings: The rpoN gene of Pseudomonas aeruginosa was found to alter susceptibility to quinolones and carbapenems, likely through increased pyoverdine production and vqsR gene expression.
full_output.methodology: Construction of rpoN mutant, complementation studies, MIC and MBC determination, qRT-PCR, and flow cytometry.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic elements carrying erm(B) in Streptococcus pyogenes and association with tet(M) tetracycline resistance gene.

erm(B).mechanism: ribosome modification-mediated resistance to macrolide, lincosamide, and streptogramin B (MLS) antibiotics
erm(B).validation_method: experimental validation through PCR and sequencing

tet(M).validation_method: experimental validation through PCR and sequencing

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes genetic elements carrying the erm(B) gene, which confers resistance to macrolides, lincosamides, and streptogramin B, and its association with the tet(M) gene, which confers tetracycline resistance in Streptococcus pyogenes.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, PFGE, and conjugation experiments were used to analyze the genetic elements and their resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic susceptibility of Bifidobacterium thermophilum and Bifidobacterium pseudolongum isolates from animal sources.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of tetracycline resistance genes tet(O) and tet(W), as well as the erythromycin resistance gene erm(X), in Bifidobacterium thermophilum and Bifidobacterium pseudolongum isolates from animal sources.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing and PCR screening for resistance genes.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the antibiotic resistance profiles of 60 Shigella strains (30 S. flexneri and 30 S. sonnei) isolated from bacillary dysentery cases in Southeast Brazil, highlighting multidrug resistance to ampicillin, chloramphenicol, streptomycin, sulfamethoxazole, and tetracycline.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic resistance was determined using the diffusion disk method, and molecular techniques such as ERIC-PCR, REP-PCR, and DRE-PCR were used for strain typing.

full_output.paper_title: National survey on the susceptibility of Bacteroides fragilis group: report and analysis of trends in the United States from 1997 to 2004.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports on the susceptibility trends of Bacteroides fragilis group species to various antibiotics from 1997 to 2004, highlighting decreasing geometric mean MICs for certain antibiotics and increasing resistance rates to others such as clindamycin and moxifloxacin.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed 5,225 isolates using agar dilution method for MIC determination and assessed susceptibility trends over time.

full_output.paper_title: Nonsense-mediated mRNA decay affects nonsense transcript levels and governs response of cystic fibrosis patients to gentamicin.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that nonsense-mediated mRNA decay (NMD) influences the levels of nonsense transcripts, which in turn affects the response of cystic fibrosis patients to gentamicin treatment.
full_output.methodology: The study used RNA analysis, real-time PCR, and functional assays to investigate the role of NMD in the response to gentamicin in cystic fibrosis patients.

full_output.paper_title: Clonal population structure and specific genotypes of multidrug-resistant Campylobacter coli from Turkeys.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies specific clonal groups of multidrug-resistant Campylobacter coli from turkeys, highlighting the clonal population structure and the association between genotypes and multidrug resistance profiles.
full_output.methodology: Multilocus sequence typing (MLST), fla typing, and pulsed-field gel electrophoresis (PFGE) were used to analyze the population structure and resistance profiles of Campylobacter coli strains.

full_output.paper_title: Fluoroquinolone resistance in Streptococcus pneumoniae: area under the concentration-time curve/MIC ratio and resistance development with gatifloxacin, gemifloxacin, levofloxacin, and moxifloxacin.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies specific mutations in the parC, parE, and gyrA genes that confer fluoroquinolone resistance in Streptococcus pneumoniae, highlighting the role of these genetic changes in resistance development.
full_output.methodology: The study used an in vitro pharmacodynamic model to examine resistance development in Streptococcus pneumoniae isolates, with sequence analysis to identify mutations.

full_output.paper_title: In vitro activities of oral cephem and telithromycin against clinical isolates of major respiratory pathogens in Japan.

ermA.validation_method: PCR detection of gene presence and correlation with antibiotic susceptibility

ermC.validation_method: PCR detection of gene presence and correlation with antibiotic susceptibility

ermB.validation_method: PCR detection of gene presence and correlation with antibiotic susceptibility

mefA.validation_method: PCR detection of gene presence and correlation with antibiotic susceptibility
mefA.evidence_note: The paper states that 'Macrolide resistance in S. pneumoniae is conferred by 23S ribosome methylation by ErmB and/or drug efflux systems by MefA'.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of macrolide resistance genes (ermA, ermC, ermB, mefA) in clinical isolates of respiratory pathogens in Japan, which correlated with reduced susceptibility to macrolides and telithromycin.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of resistance genes and broth microdilution for antibiotic susceptibility testing.
full_output.sample_size: 43 MSSA, 49 S. pyogenes, 149 S. pneumoniae, 49 H. influenzae

full_output.paper_title: Bacterial toxicity of potassium tellurite: unveiling an ancient enigma.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that potassium tellurite toxicity in E. coli involves superoxide formation, which is derived from enzymatic TeO3^2- reduction. The ibpA, sodA, sodB, and soxS genes are involved in the resistance to oxidative stress induced by superoxide.
full_output.methodology: Biochemical, genetic, enzymatic and molecular approaches were used to analyze the mechanisms of potassium tellurite toxicity in E. coli.

full_output.paper_title: Multiple staphylococcal cassette chromosomes and allelic variants of cassette chromosome recombinases in Staphylococcus aureus and coagulase-negative staphylococci from Norway.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies two new allelic variants of ccrC, ccrC6 and ccrC7, in Staphylococcus aureus and coagulase-negative staphylococci, highlighting the diversity of SCC mec elements.
full_output.methodology: PCR, inverse PCR, DNA sequencing, and Southern blot hybridization were used to analyze SCC mec elements and their variants.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation and characterization of bacteria capable of tolerating the extreme conditions of clean room environments.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies various extremotolerant bacteria isolated from clean room environments, highlighting their ability to survive extreme conditions such as high salinity, pH extremes, and temperature variations. Key isolates include Bacillus species, Oceanobacillus, and Exiguobacterium, which exhibit robust survival traits under harsh conditions.
full_output.methodology: The research employed a combination of culture-dependent and -independent methods, including ATP-based bioluminescence assays and quantitative PCR, to characterize microbial populations in clean room environments.
full_output.sample_size: Multiple clean room facilities across the United States

full_output.paper_title: Horizontal gene transfer of ftsI, encoding penicillin-binding protein 3, in Haemophilus influenzae.

ftsI.validation_method: DNA sequencing of the ftsI gene, susceptibility testing, and genotyping by PFGE

mutations_found.protein_change: substitutions at positions 526 (Asn→Lys), 517 (Arg→His), 377 (Met→Ile), 385 (Ser→Thr), and 389 (Leu→Phe) in the PBP 3 protein
mutations_found.validated_by: DNA sequencing of the ftsI gene, susceptibility testing, and genotyping by PFGE

ftsI.notes: Mutations promoted from gene entry 'ftsI' (model emitted mutations_found inside genes).

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies horizontal gene transfer of the ftsI gene, which encodes penicillin-binding protein 3, in Haemophilus influenzae. Mutations in the ftsI gene lead to β-lactam resistance, including ampicillin and cefdinir resistance.
full_output.methodology: DNA sequencing, susceptibility testing, PFGE, and in vitro gene transfer experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus colonization in veterinary personnel.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that 6.5% of veterinary conference attendees were colonized with methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), with a higher prevalence among those working with large animals. Two predominant MRSA clones, CMRSA-5 and CMRSA-2, were identified, with CMRSA-5 being more common in large-animal personnel.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed nasal swabs from attendees using microbiological techniques including enrichment broth, selective agar, and molecular typing methods such as PFGE.

full_output.paper_title: Association between methicillin susceptibility and biofilm regulation in Staphylococcus aureus isolates from device-related infections.

sarA.notes: Mutation of sarA abolished biofilm in seven MRSA and eight MSSA isolates.

agr.notes: Mutation of agr in 13 MRSA and 8 MSSA isolates substantially increased biofilm (more than twofold) in only 5 of 21 (23%) isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that biofilm development in MRSA is ica independent and involves a protein adhesin(s) regulated by SarA and Agr, whereas SarA-regulated PIA/PNAG plays a more important role in MSSA biofilm development.
full_output.methodology: The study used genetic manipulation, biofilm assays, and molecular techniques to analyze the role of ica, sarA, and agr in biofilm development.

full_output.paper_title: Association of the diplotype configuration at the N-acetyltransferase 2 gene with adverse events with co-trimoxazole in Japanese patients with systemic lupus erythematosus.
full_output.key_findings: The NAT2*4 haplotype is associated with reduced risk of adverse events with co-trimoxazole in Japanese patients with SLE.
full_output.methodology: Genotyping of NAT2 gene SNPs and haplotype analysis using TaqMan and PENHAPLO software.

full_output.paper_title: Elongation factor Tu3 (EF-Tu3) from the kirromycin producer Streptomyces ramocissimus Is resistant to three classes of EF-Tu-specific inhibitors.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies tuf3 as a gene encoding EF-Tu3, which exhibits resistance to three classes of EF-Tu-specific inhibitors: kirromycin, pulvomycin, and GE2270A.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized in vitro translation assays and antibiotic resistance testing to characterize the function and resistance properties of EF-Tu3.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of class 1 integrons in commensal Escherichia coli from pigs and pig farmers in Thailand.
full_output.key_findings: Class 1 integrons were prevalent in commensal E. coli isolates from pigs and pig farmers in Thailand, with many isolates showing multidrug resistance to various antibiotics including sulfonamides, tetracyclines, chloramphenicol, aminoglycosides, and fluoroquinolones.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of class 1 integrons and antimicrobial susceptibility testing of E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Enterococci from Appenzeller and Schabziger raw milk cheese: antibiotic resistance, virulence factors, and persistence of particular strains in the products.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various erythromycin and tetracycline resistance genes in enterococci isolated from raw milk cheeses, including ereA, ereB, mphA, ermA, ermB, ermC, mrsA/mrsB, mefA/mefE, tetM, and tetL. These genes contribute to resistance against erythromycin and tetracycline in Enterococcus species.
full_output.methodology: PCR was used to detect the presence of antibiotic resistance genes in selected enterococcal strains.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of the epidemic European fusidic acid-resistant impetigo clone of Staphylococcus aureus.

fusB.mechanism: confers resistance to fusidic acid by protecting the staphylococcal translation apparatus from inhibition
fusB.validation_method: experimental validation through mapping of the chromosomal location of fusB and confirmation via Southern hybridization

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the epidemic European fusidic acid-resistant impetigo clone of Staphylococcus aureus, identifying the fusB gene as the determinant of fusidic acid resistance. The gene was found to be located on the chromosome and associated with a novel genomic island, SaRI fusB.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized molecular typing methods, PCR, plasmid purification, DNA sequencing, and antibiotic susceptibility testing to characterize the EEFIC and identify the fusB gene.

full_output.paper_title: Error-prone DNA repair system in enteroaggregative Escherichia coli identified by subtractive hybridization.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the impB gene, which encodes an error-prone DNA repair protein, in enteroaggregative Escherichia coli strain 60A. This gene contributes to UV resistance and mutagenesis.
full_output.methodology: Subtractive hybridization, mutant construction, complementation, and UV survival assays.

full_output.paper_title: Single-dose oral amoxicillin or linezolid for prophylaxis of experimental endocarditis due to vancomycin-susceptible and vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecalis.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the effectiveness of single-dose oral amoxicillin and linezolid for prophylaxis against experimental endocarditis caused by vancomycin-susceptible and vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecalis. Amoxicillin provided 100% protection against all tested isolates, while linezolid required multiple doses for full protection against the vancomycin-resistant isolate.
full_output.methodology: The study used rat models with catheter-induced aortic vegetations to simulate human pharmacokinetics and assess the efficacy of amoxicillin and linezolid in preventing endocarditis.

full_output.paper_title: Rapid detection of clarithromycin-resistant Helicobacter pylori in patients with dyspepsia by fluorescent in situ hybridization (FISH) compared with the E-test.

mutations_found.validated_by: fluorescent in situ hybridization (FISH) and E-test

23S_rRNA.notes: Mutations in 23S rRNA confer resistance to clarithromycin

full_output.paper_title: The transition metal gallium disrupts Pseudomonas aeruginosa iron metabolism and has antimicrobial and antibiofilm activity.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that gallium (Ga) disrupts Pseudomonas aeruginosa iron metabolism, leading to antimicrobial and antibiofilm activity. Ga inhibits bacterial growth, prevents biofilm formation, and kills both planktonic and biofilm bacteria. The mechanism involves interference with iron-dependent processes and repression of the iron-regulated transcriptional regulator pvdS.
full_output.methodology: The study used in vitro experiments, biofilm assays, and animal infection models to evaluate the antimicrobial and antibiofilm effects of gallium.

full_output.paper_title: Identification and characterization of genes encoding a putative ABC-type transporter essential for utilization of gamma-hexachlorocyclohexane in Sphingobium japonicum UT26.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes the linKLMN genes encoding a putative ABC-type transporter essential for the utilization of gamma-hexachlorocyclohexane (gamma-HCH) in Sphingobium japonicum UT26. The ABC transporter is involved in the tolerance to the toxic metabolite 2,5-dichlorophenol (2,5-DCP) and regulates membrane permeability to hydrophobic compounds.
full_output.methodology: The study used transposon mutagenesis, gene deletion, complementation, and biochemical assays to characterize the linKLMN genes and their role in gamma-HCH utilization.

full_output.paper_title: High-level gentamicin resistance mediated by a Tn4001-like transposon in seven nonclonal hospital isolates of Streptococcus pasteurianus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the aac(6')-Ie-aph(2")-Ia gene as the cause of high-level gentamicin resistance in seven nonclonal hospital isolates of Streptococcus pasteurianus, which is mediated by a Tn4001-like transposon.
full_output.methodology: PCR, nucleotide sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize the resistance gene.

full_output.paper_title: Secondary acylation of Klebsiella pneumoniae lipopolysaccharide contributes to sensitivity to antibacterial peptides.

mutations_found.protein_change: deletion of 142 bp and insertion of cat gene
mutations_found.confers_resistance_to: polymyxin B, colistin, polymyxin E, C18G

lpxM.notes: The lpxM gene was disrupted by removing an internal 142 bp and adding a cat gene, leading to increased sensitivity to antimicrobial peptides.

full_output.key_findings: Disruption of the lpxM gene in Klebsiella pneumoniae leads to increased sensitivity to antimicrobial peptides such as polymyxin B, colistin, polymyxin E, and C18G due to increased outer membrane permeability.
full_output.methodology: Gene disruption, MIC testing, SDS-PAGE, and TLC analysis were used to study the role of lpxM in lipid A acylation and antimicrobial peptide sensitivity.

full_output.paper_title: Multidrug-resistant Salmonella enterica serovar paratyphi A harbors IncHI1 plasmids similar to those found in serovar typhi.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple antibiotic resistance genes, including blaTEM-1, sul2, strAB, cat, tet, and dfrA7, carried on IncHI1 plasmids in multidrug-resistant Salmonella enterica serovar paratyphi A, highlighting the role of these plasmids in the spread of multidrug resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing of the plasmid pAKU_1 and comparative analysis with other IncHI1 plasmids.
full_output.sample_size: 81 serovar Paratyphi A isolates from Pakistan

full_output.paper_title: External guide sequences targeting the aac(6')-Ib mRNA induce inhibition of amikacin resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that external guide sequences (EGSs) targeting the aac(6')-Ib mRNA can inhibit amikacin resistance by reducing the expression of the resistance gene.
full_output.methodology: The study used EGSs to target the aac(6')-Ib mRNA, leading to RNase P-mediated cleavage and reduced resistance in E. coli.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation and molecular characterization of antibiotic-resistant lactic acid bacteria from poultry and swine meat products.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified tetracycline resistance genes (tet(M)), erythromycin resistance genes (erm(B)), and penicillin resistance gene (blaZ) in lactic acid bacteria isolated from poultry and swine meat products.
full_output.methodology: PCR, MIC determination, and genetic fingerprinting were used to identify and characterize antibiotic-resistant lactic acid bacteria.

full_output.paper_title: Microcin J25 has dual and independent mechanisms of action in Escherichia coli: RNA polymerase inhibition and increased superoxide production.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that Microcin J25 (MccJ25) has two distinct mechanisms of action in Escherichia coli: inhibition of RNA polymerase (RNAP) and increased superoxide production, leading to respiratory chain damage.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized bacterial culture techniques, genetic manipulation, and enzymatic activity assays to investigate the mechanisms of MccJ25.

full_output.paper_title: Efficacy of tachyplesin III, colistin, and imipenem against a multiresistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa strain.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the efficacy of tachyplesin III, colistin, and imipenem against a multiresistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa strain, demonstrating synergistic effects and improved outcomes in both in vitro and in vivo models.
full_output.methodology: The study conducted in vitro MIC determination, time-kill assays, and in vivo sepsis modeling in mice to assess the efficacy of the antimicrobial agents.

full_output.paper_title: Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolates with reduced susceptibility to cefixime and ceftriaxone: association with genetic polymorphisms in penA, mtrR, porB1b, and ponA.

mtrR.encodes: transcriptional repressor of the mtr locus

mutations_found.nucleotide_change: insertion of a single codon (GAC) encoding an aspartic acid residue (D345a)

full_output.key_findings: The study identified genetic polymorphisms in penA, mtrR, porB1b, and ponA associated with reduced susceptibility to cefixime and ceftriaxone in Neisseria gonorrhoeae isolates.
full_output.methodology: Sequencing of penA, mtrR, porB1b, and ponA alleles, along with MIC testing for cefixime, ceftriaxone, and penicillin G.

full_output.paper_title: Multicopy blaOXA-58 gene as a source of high-level resistance to carbapenems in Acinetobacter baumannii.

blaOXA-58.validation_method: cloning in E. coli + MIC testing

full_output.key_findings: The multicopy blaOXA-58 gene was identified as a source of high-level resistance to carbapenems in Acinetobacter baumannii, with increased resistance levels correlated with the number of gene copies.
full_output.methodology: Cloning, sequencing, and MIC testing were used to characterize the blaOXA-58 gene and its impact on carbapenem resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Isoniazid induces its own resistance in nonreplicating Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

katG.notes: Mutations in katG were found in three of eight INH-resistant isolates.

inhA.notes: No mutations in the inhA gene or its promoter were identified in any strains.

ndh.notes: No mutations in the ndh gene were identified in any strains.

full_output.key_findings: Isoniazid (INH) can induce its own resistance in nonreplicating Mycobacterium tuberculosis persisters. Mutations in the katG gene were found in some INH-resistant isolates, suggesting a genetic basis for this resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the in vitro activity of ceftobiprole against Enterococcus faecalis, including β-lactamase-producing and vancomycin-resistant isolates, demonstrating its effectiveness and synergistic potential with aminoglycosides.
full_output.methodology: MIC determinations, time-kill and synergism studies were conducted.

full_output.paper_title: A copper-activated two-component system interacts with zinc and imipenem resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

oprD.notes: Mutations in the promoter region of oprD lead to reduced expression and imipenem resistance.
oprD.evidence_note: The paper states that mutations in the promoter region of oprD lead to reduced expression and imipenem resistance. The organism observed is Pseudomonas aeruginosa. The effect on function is reduced expression. The mutation type is promoter mutation.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the copR and czcRS genes as regulators involved in copper and zinc resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and shows that the oprD gene is repressed by these regulators, leading to imipenem resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used qRT-PCR, Western blot analysis, and mutagenesis to investigate the roles of copR, czcRS, and oprD in metal and antibiotic resistance.

full_output.paper_title: pmrA(Con) confers pmrHFIJKL-dependent EGTA and polymyxin resistance on msbB Salmonella by decorating lipid A with phosphoethanolamine.
full_output.key_findings: The pmrA(Con) mutation confers EGTA and polymyxin resistance on msbB Salmonella by modifying lipid A with phosphoethanolamine and aminoarabinose.

full_output.paper_title: Enterobacteriaceae bloodstream infections: presence of integrons, risk factors, and outcome.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various gene cassettes within integrons in Enterobacteriaceae, including those conferring resistance to trimethoprim, sulfonamides, aminoglycosides, chloramphenicol, and beta-lactams.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR, sequencing, and pulsed-field gel electrophoresis to analyze integrons and their gene cassettes in Enterobacteriaceae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Investigation of the regioselectivity for the staudinger reaction and its application for the synthesis of aminoglycosides with N-1 modification.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the regioselectivity of the Staudinger reaction for synthesizing aminoglycosides with N-1 modification, focusing on enhancing antibacterial activity against drug-resistant bacteria.
full_output.methodology: Chemical synthesis and NMR spectroscopy were used to characterize the synthesized aminoglycosides and their antibacterial activities.

full_output.paper_title: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus infections of the eye and orbit (an American Ophthalmological Society thesis).
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the increasing prevalence of community-acquired methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (CA-MRSA) infections in the eye and orbit, emphasizing the need for ophthalmologists to recognize and manage these infections effectively.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective review of patients with MRSA infections in the Parkland Health and Hospital System from 2000 to 2004.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of direct detection of Mycobacterium tuberculosis rifampin resistance by a nitrate reductase assay applied to sputum samples in Cotonou, Benin.

rpoB.notes: The isolate with discordant result had a deletion of codon 518 of the rpoB gene.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated a nitrate reductase assay (NRA) for detecting rifampin resistance in Mycobacterium tuberculosis. One isolate showed a discrepancy between NRA and the reference method, which was confirmed by rpoB gene sequencing revealing a deletion in codon 518.
full_output.methodology: NRA was performed on sputum samples, and results were compared with the indirect proportion method. Sequencing of the rpoB gene was conducted for the discordant isolate.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of community-associated MRSA (CA-MRSA) in Northern Ireland.
full_output.key_findings: The paper reports the emergence of community-associated MRSA (CA-MRSA) in Northern Ireland, highlighting the presence of the Panton-Valentine Leukocidin (PVL) gene and the SCCmec IV subtype in the isolate.
full_output.methodology: Molecular work-up and PCR techniques were used to characterize the MRSA isolate.

full_output.paper_title: Campylobacter antimicrobial drug resistance among humans, broiler chickens, and pigs, France.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports increasing resistance to nalidixic acid and tetracycline/doxycycline in Campylobacter isolates from humans, broilers, and pigs in France between 1986 and 2004. Resistance to ciprofloxacin was also observed, particularly in C. coli isolates from broilers and pigs.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed antimicrobial resistance patterns in Campylobacter isolates from human, broiler, and pig sources using agar diffusion and agar dilution methods.
full_output.sample_size: 5,685 human Campylobacter isolates, 544 C. jejuni and 374 C. coli isolates from poultry, and 871 C. coli isolates from pigs

full_output.paper_title: Differential regulation of ponA and pilMNOPQ expression by the MtrR transcriptional regulatory protein in Neisseria gonorrhoeae.

full_output.paper_title: Genomics of glycopeptidolipid biosynthesis in Mycobacterium abscessus and M. chelonae.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of macrolide resistance genes mef(A) and erm(B), and the tetracycline resistance gene tetM in invasive Streptococcus pyogenes isolates from Italy.

full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the replication of colonic Crohn's disease mucosal Escherichia coli isolates within macrophages and their susceptibility to antibiotics. It found that these isolates can replicate within macrophage vacuoles and are susceptible to several antibiotics including ciprofloxacin, clarithromycin, rifampin, sulfamethoxazole, tetracycline, and trimethoprim.
full_output.methodology: The study used macrophage cell cultures and antibiotic susceptibility testing to evaluate the replication and antibiotic effectiveness against E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Staphylococcus aureus clinical isolate with high-level methicillin resistance with an lytH mutation caused by IS1182 insertion.

lytH.mechanism: inactivation by IS1182 insertion leads to increased methicillin resistance

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that inactivation of the lytH gene by IS1182 insertion contributes to high-level methicillin resistance in Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.methodology: Mutant construction, PCR, and MIC testing were used to validate the role of lytH in methicillin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic and biochemical characterization of CAD-1, a chromosomally encoded new class A penicillinase from Carnobacterium divergens.

blaCAD-1.validation_method: cloning in E. coli + susceptibility testing

full_output.key_findings: The study identified CAD-1, a chromosomally encoded class A beta-lactamase from Carnobacterium divergens, which confers resistance to penicillins.
full_output.methodology: Cloning, sequencing, and susceptibility testing in E. coli.

full_output.paper_title: Development of multiplex assay for rapid characterization of Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

rpoB.notes: Mutation in rpoB codon 176 (C->T) leads to rifampin resistance.

katG.notes: Mutation in katG codon 315 (A->T) leads to isoniazid resistance.

inhA.notes: Mutation in inhA promoter region (-15 C->T) leads to isoniazid resistance.

embB.notes: Mutation in embB codon 306 (G->A) leads to ethambutol resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study developed a multiplex assay based on MLPA for the rapid detection of drug resistance mutations and genotyping of Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Key mutations identified include rpoB (C->T at codon 176), katG (A->T at codon 315), inhA (C->T at -15), and embB (G->A at codon 306), which confer resistance to rifampin, isoniazid, isoniazid, and ethambutol, respectively.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized MLPA, sequencing, and spoligotyping to validate the assay and identify drug resistance mutations in M. tuberculosis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Treatment with tigecycline of recurrent urosepsis caused by extended-spectrum-beta-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The case report discusses the successful treatment of recurrent urosepsis caused by an extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Escherichia coli with tigecycline after failed treatment with meropenem.
full_output.methodology: Clinical case report with antimicrobial susceptibility testing and treatment outcomes.

full_output.paper_title: Genotypic characteristics of Staphylococcus aureus isolates from a multinational trial of complicated skin and skin structure infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various virulence genes in Staphylococcus aureus isolates from a multinational trial, highlighting differences in gene distribution between US and South African isolates, particularly noting the significance of the pvl gene in association with better cure rates.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized PCR assays and PFGE to analyze the presence of virulence genes and genetic diversity among S. aureus isolates from patients with complicated skin and skin structure infections.

full_output.paper_title: Recombineering with tolC as a selectable/counter-selectable marker: remodeling the rRNA operons of Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates the use of tolC as a selectable/counter-selectable marker for genetic engineering in E. coli, enabling the deletion and replacement of genes including rRNA operons.
full_output.methodology: Lambda recombineering and PCR-based methods were used to manipulate the E. coli genome, utilizing tolC as a marker for selection and counter-selection.

full_output.paper_title: Novel characteristics of community-acquired methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus strains belonging to multilocus sequence type 59 in Taiwan.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a multidrug-resistant PVL+ CA-MRSA ST59 strain in Taiwan with a novel SCC mec type VII, carrying resistance genes such as tetK, cat, aadE, aph(3')-IIIa, ermB, blaZ, and cadDX.
full_output.methodology: Molecular typing, PCR, plasmid analysis, and susceptibility testing were used to characterize the AMR genes and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Quantitative determination by real-time PCR of four vaginal Lactobacillus species, Gardnerella vaginalis and Atopobium vaginae indicates an inverse relationship between L. gasseri and L. iners.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified an inverse relationship between Lactobacillus gasseri and Lactobacillus iners in vaginal microflora, with L. gasseri showing higher concentrations in grade II and lower in grade III, while L. iners was more prevalent in grade III and absent in grades Ia and II. Additionally, the study provided MIC values for clindamycin for L. gasseri and L. iners.
full_output.methodology: Real-time PCR and agar dilution method for determining MIC values.

full_output.paper_title: Altered utilization of N-Acetyl-D-galactosamine by Escherichia coli O157:H7 from the 2006 spinach outbreak.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a point mutation in the agaF gene of E. coli O157:H7 from the 2006 spinach outbreak, resulting in a Gly91Ser substitution that causes an inability to utilize N-acetyl-D-galactosamine (Aga).
full_output.methodology: The study used phenotypic microarray analysis, sequencing, and complementation experiments to identify and validate the mutation in agaF.

bcrC.validation_method: transcriptional fusion and heat induction experiments

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies bcrC and mreBH as targets of the alternative sigma factor SigI in Bacillus subtilis, demonstrating their regulation by SigI and involvement in stress responses.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptional fusion experiments, primer extension analysis, and heat induction studies were used to validate the regulation of bcrC and mreBH by SigI.

full_output.paper_title: Acinetobacter septicus sp. nov. association with a nosocomial outbreak of bacteremia in a neonatal intensive care unit.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel Acinetobacter species, Acinetobacter septicus sp. nov., associated with a nosocomial outbreak of bacteremia in a neonatal intensive care unit. The isolates were found to be distinct from other Acinetobacter species based on 16S rRNA and rpoB gene sequencing and DNA-DNA hybridization.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized 16S rRNA and rpoB gene sequencing, PFGE, and DNA-DNA hybridization to characterize the novel Acinetobacter species.

full_output.paper_title: Fitness of Streptococcus pneumoniae fluoroquinolone-resistant strains with topoisomerase IV recombinant genes.

parC.notes: Mutations in parC contribute to fluoroquinolone resistance in Streptococcus pneumoniae.

parE.notes: Mutation in parE contributes to fluoroquinolone resistance in Streptococcus pneumoniae.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in parC, parE, and gyrA that contribute to fluoroquinolone resistance in Streptococcus pneumoniae.
full_output.methodology: Genetic transformation, MIC testing, and RT-PCR were used to analyze mutations in topoisomerase IV and DNA gyrase genes.

full_output.paper_title: Epidemiology and clinical outcomes of community-acquired pneumonia in adult patients in Asian countries: a prospective study by the Asian network for surveillance of resistant pathogens.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that 56.1% of pneumococcal isolates were resistant to erythromycin and 52.6% were not susceptible to penicillin. Resistance rates to cefuroxime and ceftriaxone were 47.4% and 7.0%, respectively.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the broth microdilution method.

full_output.paper_title: Convergent use of RhoGAP toxins by eukaryotic parasites and bacterial pathogens.

LbGAP.mechanism: GAP activity towards Rac1 and Cdc42
LbGAP.validation_method: in vitro GAP assays, yeast two-hybrid analysis, GST pull-down assay

full_output.key_findings: The cfr gene, encoding a 23S rRNA methyltransferase, mediates linezolid resistance in a clinical MRSA isolate (CM-05) and is rarely found in clinical isolates of Colombian MRSA.
full_output.methodology: PCR, susceptibility testing, PFGE, and molecular typing were used to characterize the cfr gene and its impact on linezolid resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Functional Overlap but Lack of Complete Cross-Complementation of Streptococcus mutans and Escherichia coli YidC Orthologs.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that E. coli YidC can partially rescue the stress-sensitive phenotype of S. mutans lacking yidC2, and S. mutans YidC1 and YidC2 can complement growth defects in E. coli. However, there are differences in their functional abilities depending on the growth conditions and species background.
full_output.methodology: The study used genetic complementation, Western blot analysis, and membrane vesicle assays to evaluate the functional roles of YidC orthologs in S. mutans and E. coli.

full_output.paper_title: Diversity of Tn1546 and Its Role in the Dissemination of Vancomycin-Resistant Enterococci in Portugal.

SpeB, a cysteine proteinase, hydrolyzes and inactivates EndoS, thereby regulating its activity.
full_output.methodology: Site-directed mutagenesis, chemical modification, Western blot analysis, and enzyme activity assays were used to characterize the role of specific amino acids in EndoS activity.

full_output.paper_title: The resuscitation-promoting factors of Mycobacterium tuberculosis are required for virulence and resuscitation from dormancy but are collectively dispensable for growth in vitro.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that the rpfA-E genes are collectively dispensable for growth of Mycobacterium tuberculosis in vitro, but they are essential for virulence and resuscitation from dormancy. Mutants lacking rpfB and rpfE exhibit hypersensitivity to SDS and reduced growth in mice.
full_output.methodology: Genetic deletion mutagenesis, complementation experiments, and growth assays were performed to analyze the role of rpfA-E genes in M. tuberculosis.

full_output.paper_title: Trends in antibacterial resistance among Streptococcus pneumoniae isolated in the USA: update from PROTEKT US Years 1-4.

full_output.methodology: Polymerase chain reaction and minimum inhibitory concentration testing were used to determine macrolide resistance mechanisms and susceptibility patterns.

full_output.paper_title: Demonstration of allelic exchange in the slow-growing bacterium Mycobacterium avium subsp. paratuberculosis, and generation of mutants with deletions at the pknG, relA, and lsr2 loci.

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates the successful generation of targeted gene deletions in Mycobacterium avium subsp. paratuberculosis, including deletions in the pknG, relA, and lsr2 genes, using an optimized allelic exchange system.

full_output.paper_title: Protein kinases Fpk1p and Fpk2p are novel regulators of phospholipid asymmetry.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Fpk1p and Fpk2p as novel regulators of phospholipid asymmetry, highlighting their role in the function and regulation of Lem3p-Dnf1p and Lem3p-Dnf2p, which are involved in phospholipid translocation across the plasma membrane.
full_output.methodology: Genetic screening, mutant analysis, fluorescence microscopy, and biochemical assays were used to investigate the role of Fpk1p and Fpk2p in phospholipid asymmetry.

full_output.paper_title: The Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae PhoPQ two-component system is required for AvrXA21 activity, hrpG expression, and virulence.
full_output.key_findings: The PhoPQ two-component system is required for AvrXA21 activity and virulence in Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae. Mutations in phoP and phoQ lead to reduced virulence and altered gene expression in response to Mg2+ and Ca2+ concentrations.
full_output.methodology: Mutant construction, complementation, RT-PCR, and growth assays.

full_output.paper_title: Utilization of lactoferrin-bound and transferrin-bound iron by Campylobacter jejuni.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Cj0178 as a critical outer membrane receptor for the utilization of iron bound to transferrin and lactoferrin by Campylobacter jejuni, demonstrating its role in iron acquisition through mutant analysis and radiolabelled iron uptake experiments.
full_output.methodology: Mutant construction, radiolabelled iron uptake assays, and growth experiments in defined media.

full_output.paper_title: Variation in the group B Streptococcus CsrRS regulon and effects on pathogenicity.

csrR.notes: csrR mutants show altered gene expression

csrS.notes: csrS mutants show altered gene expression

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the CsrRS regulon in GBS strains 2603 and 515, revealing a core group of 39 genes regulated by CsrRS, including virulence factors like β-hemolysin, CAMP factor, and C5a peptidase. Mutations in csrR and csrS lead to differential gene regulation and affect virulence in murine models.
full_output.methodology: Genomic microarray analysis, qRT-PCR, EMSA, and mouse virulence studies were used to analyze gene regulation and virulence effects of csrR and csrS mutants.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of secretion-defective sublines of Pseudomonas aeruginosa PAO1 resulting from spontaneous mutations in the vfr global regulatory gene.

full_output.paper_title: A functional genomic yeast screen to identify pathogenic bacterial proteins.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several translocated Shigella proteins that inhibit yeast growth, indicating their potential role in pathogenesis. It also discovers IpaJ as a new substrate of the Shigella type III secretion system.
full_output.methodology: A quantitative yeast growth assay was developed to evaluate the effects of bacterial proteins on yeast growth, identifying translocated proteins based on growth inhibition.

full_output.paper_title: The periplasmic disulfide oxidoreductase DsbA contributes to Haemophilus influenzae pathogenesis.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that the periplasmic disulfide oxidoreductase DsbA is required for Haemophilus influenzae pathogenesis, particularly in bloodstream infections. DsbA is necessary for the proper folding and function of HbpA, a heme transport protein, which plays a crucial role in heme acquisition and bacterial survival in vivo.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized genetic manipulation, Western blotting, and murine and infant rat infection models to investigate the role of DsbA in H. influenzae pathogenesis.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies linezolid-resistant enterococci (LRE) as an emerging hospital problem, highlighting the role of linezolid exposure and patient-to-patient transmission in outbreaks. It also notes the association between prior MRSA infection and LRE development.

full_output.paper_title: Defensin susceptibility and colonization in the mouse model of AJ100, a polymyxin B-resistant, Brucella abortus RB51 isolate.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the polymyxin B resistance in Brucella abortus AJ100 and its susceptibility to defensins, indicating that the susceptibility profile to defensins may predict attenuation better than susceptibility to polymyxin B.
full_output.methodology: MIC values determined by Etest and drop assay for susceptibility to defensins.

full_output.paper_title: Human multidrug-resistant Salmonella Newport infections, Wisconsin, 2003-2005.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the blaCMY-2 gene as a key factor in ceftriaxone resistance among multidrug-resistant Salmonella Newport isolates in Wisconsin, highlighting its potential for spread via plasmid transfer.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of antimicrobial susceptibility testing data and epidemiological surveys.

full_output.paper_title: Evolution of a family of metazoan active-site-serine enzymes from penicillin-binding proteins: a novel facet of the bacterial legacy.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies LACTB and its paralogs as metazoan homologs of bacterial penicillin-binding proteins and β-lactamases, suggesting an evolutionary origin from α-proteobacteria. LACTB and related proteins are active-site-serine enzymes with potential roles in metabolic signaling and peptidoglycan degradation.
full_output.methodology: Phylogenetic analysis, structural comparison, and sequence alignment of LACTB family proteins from various metazoan and bacterial species.

full_output.paper_title: Capsular antigen fraction 1 and Pla modulate the susceptibility of Yersinia pestis to pulmonary antimicrobial peptides such as cathelicidin.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Pla as a protease that degrades cathelicidin LL-37, contributing to Yersinia pestis resistance to antimicrobial peptides. F1 protein inhibits Pla activity, making Y. pestis more susceptible to LL-37.
full_output.methodology: Mutant construction, plasmid complementation, and antimicrobial assays were used to validate the role of Pla and F1 in resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance and heat sensitivity of oxacillin-resistant, mecA-positive Staphylococcus spp. from unpasteurized milk.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mecA as a gene responsible for oxacillin resistance in Staphylococcus spp. from unpasteurized milk, along with qacA/B genes contributing to benzalkonium chloride resistance.
full_output.methodology: Isolation of Staphylococcus spp. from unpasteurized milk samples and determination of antimicrobial resistance profiles.

full_output.paper_title: Capacity of human nisin- and pediocin-producing lactic Acid bacteria to reduce intestinal colonization by vancomycin-resistant enterococci.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified nisZ and pedA genes in Lactococcus lactis MM19 and Pediococcus acidilactici MM33, which encode nisin and pediocin, respectively, showing activity against vancomycin-resistant enterococci.
full_output.methodology: PCR and DNA sequencing were used to identify bacteriocin genes, and in vitro assays assessed antimicrobial activity.

full_output.paper_title: Packaging of live Legionella pneumophila into pellets expelled by Tetrahymena spp. does not require bacterial replication and depends on a Dot/Icm-mediated survival mechanism.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the Dot/Icm system as crucial for Legionella pneumophila to resist digestion by Tetrahymena, enabling the formation of pellets containing live bacteria without replication.
