full_output.paper_title: Treatment of otitis media by transtympanic delivery of antibiotics.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a hydrogel drug delivery system for the treatment of otitis media, which effectively eradicated infections caused by nontypable Haemophilus influenzae (NTHi) in chinchillas. The system allowed for localized, sustained delivery of ciprofloxacin, reducing systemic exposure and improving treatment outcomes.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a hydrogel formulation containing ciprofloxacin and chemical permeation enhancers (CPEs) to achieve localized antibiotic delivery. The effectiveness of the formulation was evaluated through in vitro, ex vivo, and in vivo experiments, including assessments of drug release, permeation across the tympanic membrane, and therapeutic efficacy in a chinchilla model of otitis media.

full_output.methodology: Epidemiologic and laboratory investigations, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and product traceback analyses were conducted.

full_output.paper_title: Virulence and Genomic Feature of Multidrug Resistant Campylobacter jejuni Isolated from Broiler Chicken.

gyrA.evidence_note: The T86I mutation in the gyrA gene contributes to high-level resistance to fluoroquinolones.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple AMR genes and mutations in Campylobacter jejuni 1655, including gyrA T86I mutation, 23S rRNA A2075G mutation, tetO, aphA, and aadE genes, contributing to resistance against fluoroquinolones, macrolides, tetracycline, and aminoglycosides.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify AMR genes and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization and Comparative Overview of Complete Sequences of the First Plasmids of Pandoraea across Clinical and Non-clinical Strains.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes plasmids from various Pandoraea strains, identifying several antibiotic resistance genes including beta-lactamases, tetracycline resistance genes, aminoglycoside resistance genes, fluoroquinolone resistance genes, macrolide resistance genes, chloramphenicol resistance genes, and lincomamide resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to identify and characterize plasmid-encoded antibiotic resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Escherichia coli Probiotic Strain ED1a in Pigs Has a Limited Impact on the Gut Carriage of Extended-Spectrum-β-Lactamase-Producing E. coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the impact of E. coli probiotic strain ED1a on the gut carriage of extended-spectrum-beta-lactamase-producing E. coli. It found that ED1a had a limited effect on reducing the fecal excretion of ESCR E. coli and that the bla CTX-M-1 gene was frequently transferred to other E. coli strains in the microbiota.
full_output.methodology: The study used qPCR, culture, and fecal sampling to analyze the presence and resistance of E. coli strains in pigs.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Bases Determining Daptomycin Resistance-Mediated Resensitization to β-Lactams (Seesaw Effect) in Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mprF mutations and the role of PrsA in the seesaw effect, where DAP resistance leads to increased β-lactam sensitivity in MRSA.
full_output.methodology: Genetic analysis, MIC testing, Western blot, and RNA-Seq.

full_output.paper_title: Mechanism of Gene Regulation by a Staphylococcus aureus Toxin.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies PmtR as a GntR-type transcriptional regulator that negatively regulates the pmt operon, which encodes an ABC transporter responsible for PSM export. PSMs, in turn, disrupt the PmtR-pmt promoter complex, leading to pmt transcription and PSM secretion.
full_output.methodology: Genetic deletion, complementation, qRT-PCR, microarray analysis, and EMSA were used to investigate the regulatory relationship between PmtR and the pmt operon.

full_output.paper_title: Simultaneous Deletion of the 9GL and UK Genes from the African Swine Fever Virus Georgia 2007 Isolate Offers Increased Safety and Protection against Homologous Challenge.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that simultaneous deletion of the 9GL and UK genes from the African Swine Fever Virus Georgia 2007 isolate leads to increased safety and protection against homologous challenge in swine.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized molecular cloning techniques to create a double-gene-deletion recombinant virus, followed by in vitro and in vivo evaluations of its virulence and protective efficacy.

full_output.paper_title: Structure of the bacterial plant-ferredoxin receptor FusA
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies FusA as a novel TonB-dependent receptor involved in iron acquisition from plant ferredoxin in Pectobacterium spp. FusA was shown to bind ferredoxin through specific extracellular loops, and its structure was determined using X-ray crystallography.
full_output.methodology: Structural biology techniques including X-ray crystallography, NMR spectroscopy, and bioinformatics analyses were employed to characterize FusA and its interactions with ferredoxin.

full_output.paper_title: Vibrio vulnificus Type 6 Secretion System 1 Contains Anti-Bacterial Properties.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies two novel type 6 secretion systems (T6SS1 and T6SS2) in Vibrio vulnificus, with T6SS1 exhibiting anti-bacterial properties through intra-species and inter-species killing mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, co-culture assays, western blot analysis, and mutagenesis studies.

full_output.paper_title: Genotypic and Phenotypic Characterization of Stenotrophomonas maltophilia Strains from a Pediatric Tertiary Care Hospital in Serbia.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that all Stenotrophomonas maltophilia isolates were uniformly sensitive to the tested antimicrobial agents, including trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole, chloramphenicol, ciprofloxacin, levofloxacin, and tetracycline. No AMR genes were experimentally validated in this study.
full_output.methodology: The study used 16S rRNA gene sequencing, PFGE, MLST, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, biofilm formation assays, and PCR-based screening for genes associated with biofilm formation.

full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the molecular basis of antimicrobial resistance in various bacteria, highlighting the role of specific genes such as vanA, vanB, and others in glycopeptide resistance, as well as mutations in gyrA contributing to fluoroquinolone resistance. It also emphasizes the impact of antimicrobial use in food animals on the development of resistance in human pathogens.
full_output.methodology: Review of existing literature and analysis of resistance mechanisms in bacteria.

full_output.paper_title: Characteristics of gram-negative urinary tract infections caused by extended spectrum beta lactamases: pivmecillinam as a treatment option within South Dublin, Ireland.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the efficacy of pivmecillinam as a treatment for urinary tract infections caused by extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Enterobacteriaceae. It found that pivmecillinam had good in vitro activity against ESBL-producing E. coli and Klebsiella, with only 5.26% of isolates resistant to pivmecillinam.
full_output.methodology: The study used E-test and checkerboard techniques to determine minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) and evaluate synergistic effects of pivmecillinam and co-amoxiclav against ESBL-producing isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Impact of High Diversity of Achromobacter Populations within Cystic Fibrosis Sputum Samples on Antimicrobial Susceptibility Testing.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the high within-sample and within-morphotype diversity of antimicrobial resistance in Achromobacter species strains isolated from cystic fibrosis sputum samples, indicating that antimicrobial susceptibility testing based on a single colony may not accurately reflect the overall resistance profile of the population.
full_output.methodology: The study used pulsed-field gel electrophoresis (PFGE) and disk diffusion assays to analyze genomic and antimicrobial resistance diversity in Achromobacter strains from cystic fibrosis sputum samples.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of an Escherichia coli Sequence Type 167 Strain with Two Tandem Copies of blaNDM-1 in the Chromosome.

blaNDM-1.validation_method: genomic sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing

full_output.key_findings: The study reports the first clinical strain of Escherichia coli sequence type 167 (ST167) with two tandem chromosomal copies of blaNDM-1, demonstrating the vertical spreading pattern of the gene.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and PFGE analysis were used to characterize the strain and its resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Extensively Drug-Resistant Tuberculosis: Report and Literature Review on Two Cases Requiring Prolonged Treatment.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the treatment of two cases of extensively drug-resistant tuberculosis (XDR-TB) with prolonged individualized therapy, highlighting the challenges and outcomes of managing such cases.
full_output.methodology: The paper presents a case report analyzing the treatment and outcomes of two siblings with XDR-TB, focusing on the use of individualized treatment regimens and surgical interventions.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies eugenol and its derivatives as effective inhibitors of biofilm formation and virulence in Escherichia coli O157:H7, without affecting planktonic cell growth.
full_output.methodology: The study used a combination of biochemical assays, molecular biology techniques, and microbiological analyses to evaluate the effects of essential oils and eugenol on biofilm formation and virulence in E. coli O157:H7.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of a two-component Class IIb bacteriocin in Streptococcus pyogenes by recombinase-based in vivo expression technology.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes the spbM and spbN genes, which encode a functional Class IIb two-peptide bacteriocin in Streptococcus pyogenes. These genes are induced in vivo and exhibit antimicrobial activity against various bacterial strains.
full_output.methodology: Recombinant expression of spbM and spbN peptides, antimicrobial activity testing, and qRT-PCR analysis.

full_output.paper_title: A prospective study of treatment of carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae infections and risk factors associated with outcome.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the bla KPC gene as the primary carbapenemase in carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae (CRE) isolates, highlighting its prevalence and association with high mortality rates in patients with CRE infections.
full_output.methodology: PCR and susceptibility testing were used to detect carbapenemase genes and assess antimicrobial resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Finished Genome Sequence of the Highly Multidrug-Resistant Human Urine Isolate Citrobacter freundii Strain SL151.
full_output.key_findings: The genome of the multidrug-resistant Citrobacter freundii strain SL151 reveals several resistance genes including blaCMY-79, qnrB, aac(3)-III, blaTEM-1, blaCTX-M-15, qnrS1, sul2, catA1, strA, strB, aadA16, aac(6')-Ib-cr, arr-3, dfrA27, and qnrB6, highlighting the complex plasmid-mediated accumulation of antimicrobial resistance determinants.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing using the Pacific Biosciences RS II platform followed by genomic analysis and annotation.

full_output.paper_title: Interfering TAL effectors of Xanthomonas oryzae neutralize R-gene-mediated plant disease resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Tal3a and Tal3b as interfering TAL effectors (iTALEs) that interfere with Xa1-mediated resistance in rice, allowing Xanthomonas oryzae to overcome plant disease resistance.
full_output.methodology: Mutant strain generation, complementation experiments, and PCR-based detection of iTALE genes.

full_output.paper_title: The endotracheal tube microbiome associated with Pseudomonas aeruginosa or Staphylococcus epidermidis.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed the endotracheal tube (ETT) microbiome and found that the presence of Pseudomonas aeruginosa was associated with worse patient outcomes, while the presence of Candida species was more common in ETTs with Staphylococcus epidermidis. The microbial composition of the ETT was found to correlate with patient prognosis.
full_output.methodology: The study used 16S rRNA and ITS-II sequencing to analyze the ETT microbiome, along with culture-based methods and histological analysis.

full_output.paper_title: A Mutational Hotspot and Strong Selection Contribute to the Order of Mutations Selected for during Escherichia coli Adaptation to the Gut.

gatC.validation_method: whole genome sequencing and mutation analysis

mutations_found.validated_by: whole genome sequencing and mutation analysis

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several mutational targets involved in E. coli adaptation to the gut, including arcA, dcuB, focA, and srlR, which are associated with respiratory flexibility and metabolism. These mutations primarily affect gene regulation rather than direct antimicrobial resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, gene expression analysis, and in vivo competitive fitness assays were used to identify and validate the mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Plasmid-Mediated Quinolone-Resistance (qnr) Genes in Clinical Isolates of Escherichia coli Collected from Several Hospitals of Qazvin and Zanjan Provinces, Iran.

qnrS1.evidence_note: The paper states that four (2.9%) of the 136 quinolone-nonsusceptible E. coli isolates carried qnrS1.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the qnrS1 gene as a plasmid-mediated quinolone resistance gene in 2.9% of quinolone-nonsusceptible E. coli isolates from Qazvin and Zanjan Provinces, Iran.
full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing were used to detect qnrA, qnrB, and qnrS genes in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Extracellular Nucleases of Streptococcus equi subsp. zooepidemicus Degrade Neutrophil Extracellular Traps and Impair Macrophage Activity of the Host.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies two extracellular nucleases, ENuc (encoded by SESEC_RS04165) and 5Nuc (encoded by SESEC_RS05720), which degrade neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) and impair macrophage phagocytosis, contributing to the virulence of Streptococcus equi subsp. zooepidemicus.
full_output.methodology: The study used qRT-PCR, gene deletion mutants, and biochemical assays to characterize the functions of ENuc and 5Nuc in degrading NETs and affecting macrophage activity.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several Dictyostelium discoideum mutants that affect the interaction with yeast cells, particularly highlighting the roles of autophagy-related genes (atg1, atg6, atg5, atg7, atg8) and other regulatory genes (kil1, kil2, rdeA, phg1A, sibA, wshA, dymA) in modulating yeast growth. Mutations in these genes resulted in altered yeast growth patterns, suggesting their involvement in the host-pathogen interaction.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized mutant analysis, amoebae plate tests, and phagocytosis assays to investigate the interaction between Dictyostelium discoideum and yeast cells.

full_output.paper_title: Non-classical transpeptidases yield insight into new antibacterials.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies l,d-transpeptidases Ldt Mt1 and Ldt Mt2 as novel targets for (carba)penems, showing that these enzymes are effectively inhibited by faropenem, doripenem, biapenem, and tebipenem, leading to potent anti-TB activity.
full_output.methodology: Biochemical and biophysical approaches, including UPLC-MS, ITC, and crystallography, were used to characterize the interactions between (carba)penems and l,d-transpeptidases.

full_output.paper_title: Triethylene Glycol Up-Regulates Virulence-Associated Genes and Proteins in Streptococcus mutans.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that triethylene glycol (TEG) up-regulates virulence-associated genes and proteins in Streptococcus mutans, particularly gtfB, gtfC, gbpB, comC, comD, comE, and atpH, which are involved in biofilm formation, acid tolerance, and stress response.
full_output.methodology: Quantitative real-time PCR, proteomics analysis, and glucosyltransferase enzyme activity measurements were used to analyze the effects of TEG on S. mutans gene expression and protein abundance.

full_output.paper_title: Large scale analysis of amino acid substitutions in bacterial proteomics.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a method for identifying single amino acid polymorphisms (SAPs) in bacterial proteomics without relying on genomic databases. It highlights the importance of SAPs in understanding bacterial diversity and provides insights into the effectiveness of various algorithms for SAP detection.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized mass spectrometry data and developed an algorithm called 'speptide' to identify SAPs by comparing MS/MS spectra against a spectral library. The method involved training and validating the algorithm using data from multiple bacterial strains.
full_output.sample_size: Multiple bacterial strains from different species

full_output.paper_title: Substantial Targeting Advantage Achieved by Pulmonary Administration of Colistin Methanesulfonate in a Large-Animal Model.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the pharmacokinetics of colistin methanesulfonate (CMS) and colistin in a large-animal model, demonstrating that pulmonary administration provides higher concentrations in epithelial lining fluid (ELF) with minimal systemic exposure, offering a significant targeting advantage over intravenous administration.
full_output.methodology: Pharmacokinetic analysis of CMS and colistin in plasma and ELF following intravenous and pulmonary administration in sheep.

full_output.paper_title: Optimization of Synergistic Combination Regimens against Carbapenem- and Aminoglycoside-Resistant Clinical Pseudomonas aeruginosa Isolates via Mechanism-Based Pharmacokinetic/Pharmacodynamic Modeling.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified that imipenem combined with aminoglycosides (tobramycin or amikacin) effectively enhances bacterial killing and suppresses resistance in carbapenem- and aminoglycoside-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates. The mechanism involves aminoglycosides enhancing imipenem's target site concentration through outer membrane permeabilization.
full_output.methodology: The study employed mechanism-based pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic modeling, time-kill experiments, and Monte Carlo simulations to evaluate the efficacy of imipenem in combination with aminoglycosides against resistant P. aeruginosa isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Differential Penicillin-Binding Protein 5 (PBP5) Levels in the Enterococcus faecium Clades with Different Levels of Ampicillin Resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that PBP5 levels are differentially regulated in Enterococcus faecium clades, contributing to varying levels of ampicillin resistance. Higher PBP5 levels correlate with increased ampicillin resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used Western blotting, Northern blotting, and genetic analysis to examine PBP5 levels and their association with ampicillin resistance in different E. faecium clades.

full_output.paper_title: Establishing Antibacterial Multilayer Films on the Surface of Direct Metal Laser Sintered Titanium Primed with Phase-Transited Lysozyme.
full_output.key_findings: The study established antibacterial multilayer films on direct metal laser sintered titanium surfaces primed with phase-transited lysozyme, demonstrating effective inhibition of bacterial biofilm formation by minocycline-loaded hyaluronic acid/chitosan multilayers.
full_output.methodology: Surface characterization, nano-indentation, contact angle measurements, in vitro release profile analysis, and antibacterial assays using CFU counting and CLSM.

full_output.paper_title: A TolC-Like Protein of Actinobacillus pleuropneumoniae Is Involved in Antibiotic Resistance and Biofilm Formation.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies TolC1 as a critical component of the multidrug efflux machinery in Actinobacillus pleuropneumoniae, contributing to antibiotic resistance in both planktonic and biofilm cells. Deletion of tolC1 leads to increased susceptibility to various antibiotics and non-antibiotic antimicrobials.
full_output.methodology: Construction of mutants, MIC-P and MBC-B assays, Western blotting, and biofilm formation assays.

full_output.paper_title: The Antimicrobial Susceptibility of Klebsiella pneumoniae from Community Settings in Taiwan, a Trend Analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the emergence and increasing prevalence of ESBL and AmpC β-lactamase-producing K. pneumoniae isolates in community settings in Taiwan, highlighting the rise in resistance to third-generation cephalosporins and fluoroquinolones.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR for detection of ESBL and AmpC β-lactamase genes, and molecular typing techniques such as MLST and PFGE.

full_output.paper_title: High-Throughput Parallel Sequencing to Measure Fitness of Leptospira interrogans Transposon Insertion Mutants during Acute Infection.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of Ly2 members as antimicrobial peptides from zebrafish Danio rerio.
