full_output.methodology: Experimental evolution, genomic sequencing, and real-time PCR were used to analyze the genetic changes associated with colistin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: OXA-181-Like Carbapenemases in Klebsiella pneumoniae ST14, ST15, ST23, ST48, and ST231 from Septicemic Neonates: Coexistence with NDM-5, Resistome, Transmissibility, and Genome Diversity.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies bla OXA-181 and bla OXA-232 as OXA-48-like carbapenemases in Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from septicemic neonates, alongside bla NDM-5, highlighting their coexistence and transmissibility.
full_output.methodology: PCR, WGS, and susceptibility testing were used to characterize the AMR genes and mutations in the study.

full_output.paper_title: A Novel N4-Like Bacteriophage Isolated from a Wastewater Source in South India with Activity against Several Multidrug-Resistant Clinical Pseudomonas aeruginosa Isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel N4-like bacteriophage, AM.P2, which effectively lyses multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa strains, showing potential for phage therapy applications.
full_output.methodology: The phage was isolated from wastewater, characterized through genomic sequencing, and tested for its antibacterial activity against clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Genes Influencing Phage Host Range in Staphylococcus aureus on a Species-Wide Scale.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several genes influencing phage host range in Staphylococcus aureus, including trpA, phoR, isdB, sodM, fmtC, and relA, through genome-wide association studies and molecular genetic experiments.
full_output.methodology: High-throughput host range assay, genome-wide association studies (GWAS), and molecular genetic experiments including transposon knockout and complementation assays.

full_output.paper_title: First line treatment selection modifies disease course and long-term clinical outcomes in Mycobacterium avium complex pulmonary disease.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that standard regimens (RFP + EB + CAM) were more effective than alternative regimens in achieving sputum conversion, reducing treatment failure, and preventing the emergence of CAM resistance in patients with MAC-PD.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective cohort study analyzing the outcomes of patients with MAC-PD treated with standard or alternative regimens.

full_output.paper_title: Identification and characterization of resistance and pathogenicity of Enterococcus spp. in samples of donor breast milk.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified efa A and ace genes as virulence factors in Enterococcus spp. isolates from breast milk samples, along with tetracycline resistance in 63% of isolates.
full_output.methodology: PCR and disk diffusion susceptibility tests were used to identify resistance and virulence genes in Enterococcus spp. isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Single-molecule nanopore sequencing reveals extreme target copy number heterogeneity in arylomycin-resistant mutants.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies lepB gene amplification as a mechanism of arylomycin resistance in Escherichia coli and Acinetobacter baumannii, demonstrating that increased copy numbers of lepB lead to reduced susceptibility to arylomycin.
full_output.methodology: Nanopore sequencing and Illumina whole-genome sequencing were used to analyze copy number variations and mutations in arylomycin-resistant mutants.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified high rates of antimicrobial resistance in neonatal hospital-acquired bloodstream infections, with significant resistance observed in Klebsiella species, Serratia marcescens, and Acinetobacter baumannii. Extended-spectrum beta-lactamase production was common in Klebsiella species, methicillin resistance in Staphylococcus aureus, and extensive drug resistance in Acinetobacter species. The in vitro activity of piperacillin-tazobactam and amikacin decreased over time.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of neonatal hospital-acquired bloodstream infections from 2009 to 2018, including phenotypic susceptibility testing and review of clinical and laboratory data.

full_output.paper_title: How Insertion of a Single Tryptophan in the N-Terminus of a Cecropin A-Melittin Hybrid Peptide Changes Its Antimicrobial and Biophysical Profile.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the antimicrobial peptide W-BP100, which shows enhanced antibacterial activity against Gram-positive bacteria compared to its parent peptide BP100. W-BP100 exhibits a higher partition constant towards anionic membranes and induces membrane saturation, indicating its potential as a more effective antimicrobial agent.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the synthesis and characterization of W-BP100, evaluation of its antibacterial activity via MIC and MBC assays, and analysis of its interactions with model membranes using biophysical techniques such as fluorescence spectroscopy and DLS.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence, predictors, and mortality of bloodstream infections due to methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus in patients with malignancy: systemic review and meta-analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) accounts for a significant proportion of bloodstream infections (BSIs) in cancer patients, with a global prevalence of 3% among all BSIs and 44% among S. aureus bacteremia. The study highlights the importance of considering local microbiology and antibiotic-sensitivity patterns in treating BSIs in cancer patients.
full_output.methodology: Systematic review and meta-analysis of studies published from 2000 to 2020, focusing on the prevalence, predictors, and mortality of MRSA bacteremia in cancer patients.

full_output.key_findings: The study found high resistance rates to fluoroquinolones (93.3%) and nalidixic acid (93.3%) among Salmonella enterica isolates, while most isolates remained susceptible to first-line antibiotics like cephalosporins and macrolides.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the disk diffusion method and MIC determination by agar dilution.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic adaptation of Pseudomonas strains to acidity and antibiotics in hydrothermal vents at Kolumbo submarine volcano, Greece.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies 37 unique gene clusters associated with antimicrobial and multidrug resistance in the 'High Tolerance' group of Pseudomonas strains, highlighting the genetic basis of their enhanced co-tolerance to antibiotics and acidity in the Kolumbo volcano's acidic seawater environment.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing of 21 Pseudomonas strains isolated from different depths of the Kolumbo volcano, followed by pangenome analysis and functional enrichment comparisons between high and low tolerance groups.

full_output.paper_title: Lactobacillus reuteri AN417 cell-free culture supernatant as a novel antibacterial agent targeting oral pathogenic bacteria.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in E. coli isolates from broiler chicken farms in Shandong, China, including aadA, aacC4, aacC2, aphA3, bla CTX-M, bla SHV, tetA, tetB, sul1, sul2, sul3, and mcr-1. full_output.methodology: Synthesis of tetracyclic compounds and evaluation of their anti-TB activity against Mtb H37Rv, along with thermal stability analysis using nanoDSF.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and antimicrobial resistance of Salmonella enterica subspecies enterica serovar Enteritidis isolated from broiler chickens in Shandong Province, China, 2013-2018.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that Salmonella Enteritidis isolates from broiler chickens in Shandong Province, China, exhibited high resistance rates to piperacillin (96.1%), ampicillin (95.3%), nitrofurantoin (82.8%), and tetracycline (72.7%). Multidrug-resistant strains were prevalent, with the most common resistance pattern being AM-PIP-TE-FT.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was conducted using VITEK 2 AST-GN65 cards, and serotyping was performed using the Kauffman-White method.

full_output.paper_title: Research Note: Epidemiological cutoff values and acquired resistance mechanisms of three veterinary antibiotics against Escherichia coli from chicken respiratory tract infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study established epidemiological cutoff values (ECVs) for florfenicol, apramycin, and danofloxacin against E. coli from chicken respiratory tract infections. It identified resistance genes including floR, aac(3)-IV, and qnrS, which conferred resistance to these antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR, and DNA sequence analysis were used to determine resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Resistance Determinants in Livestock and Human Resistomes: A Comparative Analysis
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies country-independent and country-specific AMR determinants associated with different reservoirs, highlighting the potential of metagenomics in AMR source-attribution. It shows that human resistomes are more similar to pig and veal calves' resistomes than to those of broilers and turkeys.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic shotgun sequencing and Random Forests classification were used to analyze AMR determinants in fecal samples from various animal reservoirs and humans.

full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, plasmid assembly, and comparative analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus epidermidis Lineages in the Nasal and Skin Microbiota of Patients Planned for Arthroplasty Surgery.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus epidermidis (MRSE) lineages, including multidrug-resistant (MDRSE) strains, in the nasal and skin microbiota of patients before hospital admission for arthroplasty surgery. Key AMR genes identified include qacA (chlorhexidine tolerance), aac(6')-aph(2'') (aminoglycoside resistance), and ermC (macrolide-lincosamide resistance).

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and antimicrobial resistance profiles of Salmonella species and Escherichia coli isolates from poultry feeds in Ruiru Sub-County, Kenya.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of beta-lactamase (TEM, SHV), aminoglycoside (strB), and sulfonamide (Dfr) resistance genes in Escherichia coli and Salmonella sp. isolates from poultry feeds in Kenya.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR amplification, and gel electrophoresis were used to detect resistance genes in bacterial isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Three-dimensional low shear culture of Mycobacterium bovis BCG induces biofilm formation and antimicrobial drug tolerance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies genes such as sigE, BCG_0559c, esxJ, esxM, and PE19 that are upregulated in biofilm-grown Mycobacterium bovis BCG, indicating their involvement in biofilm formation and drug tolerance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptomic profiling and antimicrobial drug efficacy assays were used to characterize the genes and their roles in biofilm formation and drug tolerance.

full_output.paper_title: Acquisition and carriage of multidrug-resistant organisms in dogs and cats presented to small animal practices and clinics in Switzerland.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of multidrug-resistant organisms (MDRO) in dogs and cats in Switzerland, with a focus on carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales. Key AMR genes characterized include bla OXA-181, bla OXA-48, and bla NDM-5, which confer resistance to carbapenems.
full_output.methodology: The study involved sampling of oronasal and rectal swabs from dogs and cats, followed by isolation, identification, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing of the isolates. Molecular techniques such as PCR and sequencing were used to detect AMR genes.

full_output.paper_title: Treatment of Community-Acquired Pneumonia: A Focus on Lefamulin.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses lefamulin, a pleuromutilin antibiotic, which shows effectiveness against various pathogens causing community-acquired bacterial pneumonia (CABP), including methicillin-susceptible and resistant strains of Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, Mycoplasma pneumoniae, and others. It highlights lefamulin's unique mechanism of action and its potential as an alternative to existing treatments due to its lower likelihood of resistance development.
full_output.methodology: The paper reviews clinical pharmacology, pharmacokinetics, efficacy, and safety of lefamulin through a systematic literature review and analysis of phase 3 clinical trials.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of efflux pump activity and biofilm formation in multidrug resistant clinical isolates of Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolated from a Federal Medical Center in Nigeria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of efflux pump genes (mexA, mexB, oprM) and biofilm-related genes (pslA, pslD) in multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from Nigeria, highlighting their roles in antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize AMR genes and resistance profiles in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Surface-bound reactive oxygen species generating nanozymes for selective antibacterial action.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that nanozymes generating surface-bound reactive oxygen species (ROS), particularly AgPd 0.38, selectively kill bacteria over mammalian cells. These nanozymes efficiently eliminate antibiotic-resistant bacteria and delay the onset of bacterial resistance emergence. Additionally, when used as a coating additive, AgPd 0.38 inhibits biofilm formation and suppresses infection-related immune responses in mouse models.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized transmission electron microscopy (TEM), fluorescence spectroscopy, and in vitro antibacterial assays to characterize the properties and effectiveness of AgPd 0.38 nanozymes.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial FANA oligonucleotides as a novel approach for managing the Huanglongbing pathosystem.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that FANA antisense oligonucleotides targeting the gyrA gene of Wolbachia wDi and the LigA gene of Candidatus Liberibacter asiaticus can effectively silence these genes, leading to reduced bacterial titer and transmission.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized FANA antisense oligonucleotides to target specific genes in bacterial endosymbionts and pathogens, employing qPCR and viability assays to validate gene silencing and bacterial titer reduction.

full_output.paper_title: Implanted Port Catheter System Infection Caused by Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus pseudintermedius ST71-SCCmec type III.

full_output.key_findings: The study reports a case of implanted port catheter system infection caused by methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus pseudintermedius ST71-SCC mec III, identifying several AMR genes and mutations including aac(6')-aph(2''), ant(6')-Ia, aph(3')-III, sat4A, mecA, blaZ, erm(B), dfrG, GyrA Ser84Leu, and GrlA Ser80Ile.

full_output.paper_title: Induction of the Stringent Response Underlies the Antimicrobial Action of Aliphatic Isothiocyanates.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that aliphatic isothiocyanates (ITCs) inhibit bacterial growth by inducing the stringent response, leading to the accumulation of (p)ppGpp. Specific amino acids like glycine and methionine reverse the antimicrobial effects of ITCs, suggesting that ITCs interfere with amino acid metabolism.
full_output.methodology: The study used disc diffusion assays, microdilution methods, and time-kill assays to evaluate the antimicrobial effects of ITCs. Additionally, (p)ppGpp levels were measured to assess the induction of the stringent response.

full_output.paper_title: A Virulence Associated Siderophore Importer Reduces Antimicrobial Susceptibility of Klebsiella pneumoniae.

ybtPQ.validation_method: disk diffusion assay and MIC assay
ybtPQ.genetic_context: encoded in the yersiniabactin cluster in a prevalent mobile genetic element ICEKp
ybtPQ.evidence_note: The mechanism was dependent on the yersiniabactin importer YbtPQ and may involve antimicrobial efflux, since it was affected by the inhibitor reserpine.

full_output.key_findings: The yersiniabactin importer YbtPQ reduces antimicrobial susceptibility in Klebsiella pneumoniae and Escherichia coli by enhancing antimicrobial efflux, as evidenced by increased minimum inhibitory concentrations and zone of inhibition assays.

full_output.paper_title: Integrated Metabolomics and Targeted Gene Transcription Analysis Reveal Global Bacterial Antimonite Resistance Mechanisms.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies genes involved in antimonite resistance and oxidation in Agrobacterium tumefaciens GW4, including anoA, aioA, katA, and phoBR, which are upregulated in response to Sb(III) exposure.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and antimicrobial resistance of Salmonella isolates from goose farms in Northeast China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antimicrobial resistance genes in Salmonella isolates from goose farms in Northeast China, including blaTEM-1, cmlA, aac(6')-Ib-cr, sul1, sul2, sul3, mcr-1.1, tetB, qnrB, and floR, which confer resistance to various antibiotics such as amoxicillin, chloramphenicol, gentamicin, kanamycin, tetracycline, florfenicol, and colistin.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR and antimicrobial susceptibility testing to detect and characterize antimicrobial resistance genes in Salmonella isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Wildlife as Sentinels of Antimicrobial Resistance in Germany?
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various AMR genes, including bla CTX-M-1, bla CTX-M-15, bla CTX-M-14-like, bla CMY-2-like, and bla TEM-1, in Escherichia coli isolates from wild boars, roe deer, and wild ducks and geese in Germany. These genes conferred resistance to beta-lactam antibiotics such as cefotaxime, ceftazidime, and ampicillin.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the collection and analysis of fecal samples from wild boars, roe deer, and wild ducks and geese, followed by microbial isolation, identification, and antimicrobial resistance testing using broth microdilution and molecular methods.

full_output.key_findings: The Xpert MRSA/SA BC assay effectively identifies methicillin-resistant and methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus and coagulase-negative staphylococci, enabling faster antimicrobial stewardship decisions.
full_output.methodology: Prospective observational study comparing Xpert MRSA/SA BC assay with culture-based methods.

full_output.paper_title: Purification and characterization of bacteriocins-like inhibitory substances from food isolated Enterococcus faecalis OS13 with activity against nosocomial enterococci.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified and characterized two bacteriocin-like inhibitory substances, enterocin OS13α and OS13β, produced by the food-isolated Enterococcus faecalis OS13, which exhibit antimicrobial activity against vancomycin-resistant and multidrug-resistant enterococci.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the purification and characterization of bacteriocin-like inhibitory substances from Enterococcus faecalis OS13, followed by activity testing against various bacterial strains.

full_output.paper_title: A single system detects and protects the beneficial oral bacterium Streptococcus sp. A12 from a spectrum of antimicrobial peptides.

full_output.paper_title: Pseudomonas aeruginosa device associated - healthcare associated infections and its multidrug resistance at intensive care unit of University Hospital: polish, 8.5-year, prospective, single-centre study.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed Pseudomonas aeruginosa device-associated healthcare-associated infections (DA-HAIs) in an ICU, highlighting increasing multidrug resistance (MDR) and resistance to various antibiotics, including a notable 100% susceptibility to colistin.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed microbiological data from DA-HAIs in an ICU over 8.5 years, including susceptibility testing of P. aeruginosa isolates to various antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Microbiota restoration reduces antibiotic-resistant bacteria gut colonization in patients with recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection from the open-label PUNCH CD study.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that microbiota-based therapeutics like RBX2660 can reduce the abundance of antibiotic-resistant bacteria and antibiotic resistance genes in the gut microbiome of patients with recurrent Clostridioides difficile infection.
full_output.methodology: The study used 16S rRNA gene sequencing, whole metagenome shotgun sequencing, and selective bacterial culturing followed by genome sequencing to analyze the gut microbiota and resistome of patients treated with RBX2660.

full_output.paper_title: Nybomycin inhibits both types of E. coli DNA gyrase - fluoroquinolone-sensitive and fluoroquinolone-resistant.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in the gyrA gene (S83L and D87Y) that confer fluoroquinolone resistance in E. coli. These mutations were validated through genomic sequencing and MIC testing.

full_output.paper_title: Tracking the Emergence of Azithromycin Resistance in Multiple Genotypes of Typhoidal Salmonella.
Multiple copies of the oxytetracycline gene cluster in selected Streptomyces rimosus strains can provide significantly increased titers.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the oxytetracycline gene cluster (otc) in Streptomyces rimosus and identifies several genes involved in oxytetracycline resistance, including otrA, otrB, otcR, oxyTA1, and otcG. The research demonstrates that introducing multiple copies of the otc gene cluster significantly increases oxytetracycline production in selected strains.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized transformation-associated recombination (TAR) cloning, deletion and complementation experiments, and RT-qPCR analysis to investigate the role of the otc gene cluster in oxytetracycline production.

full_output.key_findings: PathoFact is a pipeline for the prediction of virulence factors, bacterial toxins, and antimicrobial resistance genes in metagenomic data with high accuracy and specificity.
full_output.methodology: PathoFact integrates three workflows for the prediction of virulence factors, bacterial toxins, and antimicrobial resistance genes using HMM profiles, random forest models, and signal peptide prediction.

full_output.paper_title: HutW from Vibrio cholerae Is an Anaerobic Heme-Degrading Enzyme with Unique Functional Properties.
full_output.key_findings: HutW from Vibrio cholerae is a radical S-adenosylmethionine (SAM) methyl transferase involved in anaerobic heme degradation. It binds ferrous heme with a Kd of 3.6 ± 0.9 μM and catalyzes the ring-opening of heme, producing a linear tetrapyrrole. HutW can utilize NADPH as an electron donor, demonstrating a unique mechanism compared to other heme-degrading enzymes.
full_output.methodology: Expression, purification, and biochemical characterization of HutW, including UV-vis spectroscopy, EPR, HPLC, and IM-MS analyses.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic islands mediate environmental adaptation and the spread of antibiotic resistance in multiresistant Enterococci - evidence from genomic sequences.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified seven antibiotic-resistant genomic islands (ARGIs) carrying multiple antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in six Enterococcus strains, highlighting the role of genomic islands in the spread of antibiotic resistance among Enterococcus species.
full_output.methodology: Genomic island prediction, ARGs prediction, clustering analysis, and network mapping were used to analyze the spread of antibiotic resistance genes in Enterococcus.

full_output.paper_title: Extensive antimicrobial resistance and plasmid-carrying resistance genes in mcr-1-positive E. coli sampled in swine, in Guangxi, South China.

full_output.paper_title: New combination approaches to combat methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA).
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several saponins from Zygophyllum album, including quinovic acid, quinovic acid 3β-O-β-D-quinovopyranoside, zygophylloside C, zygophylloside G, zygophylloside K, and ursolic acid, which showed antibacterial activity against MRSA. full_output.paper_title: Detection of diverse carbapenem and multidrug resistance genes and high-risk strain types among carbapenem non-susceptible clinical isolates of target gram-negative bacteria in Kenya.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance in commensal Escherichia coli and Enterococcus spp. is influenced by production system, antimicrobial use, and biosecurity measures on Spanish pig farms.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that the production system significantly influences antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in commensal E. coli and Enterococcus spp. on Spanish pig farms, with organic-extensive systems showing lower AMR levels compared to intensive systems. AMR was associated with antimicrobial use (AMU) and biosecurity measures.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed AMR in E. coli and Enterococcus spp. isolates from 37 Spanish pig farms using antimicrobial susceptibility testing and statistical analysis to assess the impact of production system, AMU, and biosecurity measures on AMR.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified a diverse slurry virome with potential to alter the metabolism and virulence of veterinary pathogens, including putative antimicrobial resistance genes and diversity-generating retroelements.
full_output.methodology: Hybrid sequencing and bioinformatics analyses were used to characterize the virome of agricultural slurry.

full_output.paper_title: RipA Modulates Host Immune Responses and Inhibits Autophagy in Macrophages
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies RipA, a secretory protein of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, as a key player in modulating host immune responses and inhibiting autophagy in macrophages. RipA activates TLR4, leading to the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines and the enhancement of macrophage activation. Additionally, RipA inhibits autophagy by activating the PI3K-AKT-mTORC1 signaling pathway and reducing the levels of autophagy-related proteins such as LC3BII and Rab7.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized in-silico analyses, in-vitro mammalian cell transfection experiments, and recombinant M. smegmatis to investigate the role of RipA in host immune responses and autophagy inhibition.

full_output.paper_title: Pyridoxal-5'-phosphate-dependent enzyme GenB3 Catalyzes C-3',4'-dideoxygenation in gentamicin biosynthesis.
full_output.key_findings: GenP and GenB3 are involved in the C-3',4'-dideoxygenation process in gentamicin biosynthesis. GenB3 is the first reported PLP-dependent enzyme catalyzing dideoxygenation in aminoglycoside biosynthesis.
full_output.methodology: Gene disruption, enzyme activity assays, HPLC-ELSD, MS, and NMR analyses were used to characterize the function of GenP and GenB3.

full_output.paper_title: Genome analyses of 174 strains of Mycobacterium tuberculosis provide insight into the evolution of drug resistance and reveal potential drug targets.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed 174 Mycobacterium tuberculosis strains to understand drug resistance mechanisms and identify potential drug targets. Key findings include the identification of mutations in rpsL, gidB, pncA, ahpC, embB, and other genes associated with resistance to streptomycin, pyrazinamide, isoniazid, and ethambutol. Additionally, the gene kasA was identified as a potential drug target due to its stability and interaction with host proteins.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, dN/dS ratio analysis, sequence similarity networks, and protein-protein interaction analysis were used to study drug resistance mechanisms in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

full_output.paper_title: Institutional outbreak involving multiple clades of IMP-producing Enterobacter cloacae complex sequence type 78 at a cancer center in Tokyo, Japan.

sul1.evidence_note: The presence of sul1 in the In316-like structure suggests its role in sulfonamide resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple clades of IMP-producing Enterobacter cloacae complex sequence type 78 (ST78) strains causing an institutional outbreak. These strains carried blaIMP-1 and blaIMP-11 genes on IncHI2 and IncL/M plasmids, along with various other resistance genes such as aac(6')-IIc, qnrB6, fosA, sul1, and tet(B).
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and conjugation experiments were used to analyze the outbreak.

full_output.paper_title: Efficacy of Topical Vancomycin- and Gentamicin-Loaded Calcium Sulfate Beads or Systemic Antibiotics in Eradicating Polymicrobial Biofilms Isolated from Diabetic Foot Infections within an In Vitro Wound Model.
full_output.key_findings: Vancomycin- and gentamicin-loaded calcium sulfate beads effectively reduced polymicrobial biofilm bioburden in an in vitro model of diabetic foot infections, outperforming systemic antibiotic therapy.
full_output.methodology: In vitro collagen wound models were used to assess the efficacy of antibiotic-loaded calcium sulfate beads against polymicrobial biofilms.

full_output.paper_title: Methylation analysis of Klebsiella pneumoniae from Portuguese hospitals.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies bla CTX-M-15 and bla KPC-3 as key resistance genes in Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from Portuguese hospitals, along with fosA contributing to fosfomycin resistance. Methylation analysis reveals unique patterns around these genes.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing using PacBio RSII, methylation analysis via SMRT, and bioinformatic pipelines for assembly and annotation.

full_output.paper_title: Allosteric communication in class A β-lactamases occurs via cooperative coupling of loop dynamics.

TEM-1.notes: mutations in TEM-1 affecting allosteric communication

KPC-2.notes: mutations in KPC-2 affecting allosteric communication
KPC-2.evidence_note: The paper discusses mutations in KPC-2 that affect allosteric communication, but does not explicitly state that these mutations confer resistance to specific drugs.

full_output.key_findings: The study reveals that allosteric communication in class A β-lactamases, such as TEM-1 and KPC-2, occurs through cooperative coupling of loop dynamics, which influences their catalytic activity and resistance to β-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Equilibrium and nonequilibrium molecular dynamics simulations were used to investigate the conformational changes and communication pathways in TEM-1 and KPC-2 β-lactamases.

full_output.paper_title: Inhibition of bacterial and human zinc-metalloproteases by bisphosphonate- and catechol-containing compounds.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the inhibitory effects of catechol-containing and bisphosphonate-containing compounds on bacterial and human zinc-metalloproteases, identifying compounds that effectively inhibited proteases such as TLN, PLN, ALN, MMP-9, and MMP-14. Key findings include the identification of BF471 as a potent inhibitor of TLN, PLN, and ALN, and RC2 as a strong inhibitor of TLN and PLN compared to human MMPs.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized enzyme inhibition assays, kinetic analysis, and molecular docking to evaluate the inhibitory effects of various compounds on proteases.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular survey of mcr1 and mcr2 plasmid mediated colistin resistance genes in Escherichia coli isolates of animal origin in Iran.

mcr-1.mechanism: modification of lipopolysaccharide by adding phosphoethanolamine

mcr-2.mechanism: modification of lipopolysaccharide by adding phosphoethanolamine

full_output.key_findings: The study found no mcr-1 or mcr-2 positive E. coli isolates among the 607 tested isolates from animal origins in Iran, indicating that these genes were not widespread in the animal population at least until 2016.
full_output.methodology: PCR-based detection of mcr-1 and mcr-2 genes in E. coli isolates from various animal sources.

full_output.paper_title: Translation error clusters induced by aminoglycoside antibiotics.

EF-Tu.notes: Error cluster D208E-F211L induced by Streptomycin.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies error clusters in proteins induced by aminoglycoside antibiotics, showing that these clusters contribute to proteotoxic stress and bacterial cell death.
full_output.methodology: Quantitative mass spectrometry and PRM analysis were used to identify and validate translation error clusters in E. coli.

full_output.paper_title: OMN6 a novel bioengineered peptide for the treatment of multidrug resistant Gram negative bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: OMN6 is a novel bioengineered cyclic peptide with potent antimicrobial activity against multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria, including Acinetobacter baumannii, with no resistance development observed.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis, stability, and antimicrobial activity testing of OMN6 against various bacterial strains.

full_output.paper_title: Piggybacking on Niche Adaptation Improves the Maintenance of Multidrug-Resistance Plasmids.

arcA.encodes: aerobic respiration control protein; DNA-binding transcriptional regulator
arcA.notes: Mutations in arcA were found in multiple evolved populations and contributed to reduced plasmid cost.

arcB.encodes: aerobic respiration control sensor protein; histidine kinase
arcB.notes: Mutations in arcB were found in multiple evolved populations and contributed to reduced plasmid cost.

cpdA.notes: Mutations in cpdA were found in multiple evolved populations and contributed to reduced plasmid cost.

crp.encodes: cAMP receptor protein; DNA-binding transcriptional regulator
crp.notes: Mutations in crp were found in multiple evolved populations and contributed to reduced plasmid cost.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in the CCR and ArcAB regulatory systems that mitigate the fitness costs of plasmid carriage in E. coli, facilitating plasmid maintenance through pleiotropic effects.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, competition experiments, and mutagenesis studies were conducted to analyze plasmid cost mitigation.

full_output.paper_title: ESBL-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae in a University hospital: Molecular features, diffusion of epidemic clones and evaluation of cross-transmission.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several ESBL genes, including CTX-M-15, CTX-M-3, CTX-M-14, CTX-M-9, SHV-2, TEM-like, SHV-11, and SHV-12, in ESBL-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates. These genes were associated with resistance to various antibiotics, including cephalosporins, fluoroquinolones, and sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim. The study also highlighted the prevalence of specific clones, such as ST405 and ST307, which contributed to the spread of these resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: Molecular genotyping, PCR, and antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to characterize the ESBL-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: A decade of neonatal sepsis caused by gram-negative bacilli-a retrospective matched cohort study.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that the incidence of neonatal gram-negative bacilli (GNB) sepsis was 0.35/1000 live births, with a low prevalence of antibiotic resistance. Resistance was observed in 7/107 GNB isolates, with all being susceptible to carbapenems.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective matched cohort study analyzing clinical data and antibiotic resistance patterns of GNB isolates from neonates.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Susceptibility Profiles To Predict the Presence of Carbapenemase Genes among Carbapenem-Resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa Isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies bla VIM, bla KPC, bla IMP, and bla NDM as carbapenemase genes associated with carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa (CRPA) isolates. These genes were detected in CRPA isolates and were linked to reduced susceptibility to carbapenems.
full_output.methodology: Genotypic detection of carbapenemase genes via real-time PCR and phenotypic carbapenemase production testing using the modified carbapenem inactivation method (mCIM).

full_output.paper_title: Multiresistant Bacterial Pathogens Causing Bacterial Pneumonia and Analyses of Potential Risk Factors from Northeast Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high prevalence of bacterial pneumonia with significant resistance to ampicillin, penicillin, and amoxicillin-clavulanate. Klebsiella pneumoniae and Staphylococcus aureus showed high multidrug resistance.
full_output.methodology: Cross-sectional study involving sputum specimen culture and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Drug screening to identify compounds to act as co-therapies for the treatment of Burkholderia species.
full_output.key_findings: Chloroxine was identified as a compound that enhances the efficacy of ceftazidime against Burkholderia species, reducing culturable cell numbers by two orders of magnitude.
full_output.methodology: High-throughput screening of compounds using a cell viability assay with Burkholderia thailandensis as a surrogate model.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Resistance in Salmonella and E. coli Isolated from Broiler Chicken Barns

qacEΔ1.validation_method: PCR detection of gene in E. coli isolates

sugE(p).validation_method: PCR detection of the gene in E. coli isolates

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the qacEΔ1 gene as a factor associated with resistance to quaternary ammonium compounds in E. coli isolates from commercial broiler chicken barns.
full_output.methodology: PCR was used to detect the presence of qacEΔ1 and sugE(p) genes in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic use for inpatient newborn care with suspected infection: EN-BIRTH multi-country validation study.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights significant gaps in the documentation and appropriate use of antibiotics for newborns with suspected infections, emphasizing the need for improved laboratory diagnostics and antibiotic stewardship in healthcare settings.
full_output.methodology: The study employed a multi-country validation approach, comparing antibiotic coverage data from hospital inpatient case notes with exit surveys of mothers to evaluate the accuracy of reported antibiotic use.

full_output.paper_title: Coagulase-negative staphylococci release a purine analog that inhibits Staphylococcus aureus virulence.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a 6-TG biosynthetic gene cluster in Staphylococcus chromogenes ATCC43764 and other coagulase-negative staphylococci, demonstrating that 6-TG inhibits S. aureus growth by targeting purine biosynthesis and reducing toxin production.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, gene cloning, and functional assays in S. aureus.

full_output.paper_title: Bacteria-specific pro-photosensitizer kills multidrug-resistant Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: Thymol acts as a bacteria-specific pro-photosensitizer that is converted into thymoquinone and thymohydroquinone upon blue-light activation, leading to effective killing of multidrug-resistant Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.methodology: Photo-oxidation analysis, bactericidal activity assays, and ROS production measurements.

full_output.paper_title: Improved diagnostic prediction of the pathogenicity of bloodstream isolates of Staphylococcus epidermidis.

mecA.mechanism: confers resistance to a large class of antibiotics
mecA.evidence_note: MecA is the most common virulence factor reported, especially in reference to methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA). Encoding an alternative penicillin-binding protein, mecA confers resistance to a large class of antibiotics.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mecA as a significant virulence factor in Staphylococcus epidermidis, showing its association with oxacillin resistance and pathogenicity.
full_output.methodology: PCR and phenotypic resistance testing were used to assess the presence of virulence genes and antibiotic resistance in S. epidermidis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial activities evaluation and phytochemical screening of some selected medicinal plants: A possible alternative in the treatment of multidrug-resistant microbes.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antimicrobial activities of various medicinal plant extracts against multidrug-resistant microbes, identifying several plants with significant antibacterial and antifungal effects.
full_output.methodology: In vitro experiments were conducted to assess the antimicrobial effects of plant extracts using disc diffusion and broth micro-dilution methods.

full_output.paper_title: Feasibility and potential significance of rapid in vitro qualitative phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing of gram-negative bacilli with the ProMax system.
full_output.key_findings: The ProMax system was evaluated for rapid antimicrobial susceptibility testing of gram-negative bacilli, showing high categorical agreement with disk diffusion for ciprofloxacin and gentamicin, but lower agreement for meropenem, particularly for certain species.
full_output.methodology: The ProMax system uses electrochemical sensor chips and 16S rRNA quantification for rapid AST, comparing results to disk diffusion.

full_output.paper_title: Optimal empiric treatment for KPC-2-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae infections in critically ill patients with normal or decreased renal function using Monte Carlo simulation.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the efficacy of fosfomycin (FOS), tigecycline (TGC), and colistin methanesulfonate (CMS) in combination against KPC-2-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae, highlighting the need for high-dose regimens to achieve optimal antimicrobial coverage.
full_output.methodology: Population pharmacokinetic models and Monte Carlo simulation were used to assess the probability of target attainment and cumulative fraction of response for various antibiotic regimens.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic characteristics of mcr-1 and bla(CTX-M-type) in a single multidrug-resistant Escherichia coli ST93 from chicken in China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified mcr-1, bla CTX-M-55, and bla CTX-M-14 genes in a multidrug-resistant E. coli ST93 isolate from a chicken in China, highlighting their role in resistance to colistin and cefotaxime.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, plasmid analysis, and conjugation assays were used to characterize the resistance genes and their transmission.

full_output.paper_title: The Antimicrobial Peptide Melectin Shows Both Antimicrobial and Antitumor Activity via Membrane Interference and DNA Binding.
full_output.key_findings: Melectin shows potent antibacterial activity against both drug-sensitive and drug-resistant bacterial strains, as well as antitumor activity. It acts through membrane interference and DNA binding mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antibacterial and antitumor activities of Melectin using radial diffusion assays, MIC determination, killing kinetics, PI uptake assays, membrane permeability measurements, calcein release from liposomes, DNA binding assays, and MTT assays for antitumor activity.

full_output.paper_title: Stenotrophomonas maltophilia: An emerging opportunistic nosocomial pathogen in a tertiary care hospital in Al Batinah North Governorate, Oman.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that Stenotrophomonas maltophilia exhibited high susceptibility to minocycline (97%), trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (93%), and levofloxacin (92%), but only 50% susceptibility to ceftazidime.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing was performed using Kirby-Bauer’s disc diffusion method and Epsilometer test.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of Carbapenem-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae Co-Harboring blaKPC-Carrying Plasmid and pLVPK-Like Virulence Plasmid in Bloodstream Infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae co-harboring blaKPC-2-carrying plasmid and pLVPK-like virulence plasmid, highlighting their multidrug resistance, enhanced virulence, and transferability.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, S1-PFGE, conjugation assays, and Galleria mellonella infection model.

full_output.paper_title: Host-defense peptides reduce bacterial load and stabilize weight loss post-infection
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that host-defense peptides IDR-1018, DJK-5, and IDR-1002 effectively reduce bacterial load in the nasal cavity and improve mouse welfare during infections with S. aureus USA300 and P. aeruginosa LESB58/LESB65. These peptides show varying degrees of efficacy, with IDR-1018 and DJK-5 exhibiting greater antibacterial activity compared to IDR-1002.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized bioluminescent and chemiluminescent imaging techniques to monitor bacterial load and inflammatory responses in a murine model of acute and long-term intranasal infections. Peptides were administered to assess their impact on bacterial burden and host immune responses.
full_output.sample_size: n=8 for acute infection experiments, n≥6 for long-term infection experiments

full_output.paper_title: Genetic Characterization of AmpC and Extended-Spectrum Beta-Lactamase Phenotypes in Escherichia coli and Salmonella From Alberta Broiler Chickens.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla CMY-2 and bla TEM genes in E. coli and Salmonella isolates from Alberta broiler chickens, contributing to beta-lactam resistance. Additionally, aadA, aadA1a, and aadA2 genes were found to confer resistance to streptomycin.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, conjugation experiments, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize AMR genes and their resistance profiles.

tetQ.validation_method: virome sequencing and phage contig analysis

full_output.key_findings: The study identified tetracycline resistance genes tetQ and tetW, which were found on phage contigs and associated with antibiotic-specific resistance gene homologs (AsRGs) that persisted in the gut microbiome after antibiotic treatment.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic, metatranscriptomic, and virome sequencing were used to analyze the gut microbiome and resistome of healthy individuals following antibiotic treatment.

full_output.paper_title: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus pseudintermedius synthesizes deoxyadenosine to cause persistent infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies AdsA and NucB as critical enzymes in Staphylococcus pseudintermedius that facilitate the synthesis of cytotoxic deoxyadenosine, contributing to persistent infection and abscess formation.
full_output.methodology: Genetic manipulation, biochemical assays, and animal infection models were used to characterize the roles of AdsA and NucB in S. pseudintermedius pathogenesis.
full_output.sample_size: Multiple isolates from a global collection

full_output.paper_title: Armeniaspirol A: a novel anti-Helicobacter pylori agent.
full_output.key_findings: Armeniaspirol A (ARM1) exhibits potent antibacterial activity against Helicobacter pylori, including multidrug-resistant strains, with MIC values ranging from 4 to 16 μg/ml. It disrupts bacterial cell membranes, inhibits biofilm formation, and effectively eliminates preformed biofilms. ARM1 shows greater efficacy than metronidazole in acidic conditions and has low toxicity.
full_output.methodology: Antibacterial activity was assessed using MIC determination, time-kill kinetics, membrane permeability assays, biofilm inhibition, and in vivo efficacy studies in a mouse model.

full_output.paper_title: Predicting antimicrobial mechanism-of-action from transcriptomes: A generalizable explainable artificial intelligence approach.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a machine learning approach to predict the mechanism of action (MOA) of antibiotics using transcriptomic data. It introduces the CoHEC model, which accurately identifies the MOA of both known and novel compounds, including darobactin, a newly discovered antibiotic with a novel MOA.
full_output.methodology: The study employs a hierarchical ensemble of classifiers (HEC) model optimized with a feature selection algorithm called Clairvoyance, using transcriptomic data from Escherichia coli challenged with antibiotics to predict their MOA.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic diversity of Japanese quail cathelicidins.

mutations_found.effect_on_function: predicted to have possibly damaging effects on protein function

CjCATH2.evidence_note: The paper reports that the I145F substitution in CjCATH2 was predicted to have possibly damaging effects on protein function and that synthetic CjCATH2 peptides exhibited greater antibacterial activity against E. coli than chicken CATH2 peptides.

mutations_found.effect_on_function: predicted to have possibly damaging effects on protein function

full_output.key_findings: The study identified amino acid substitutions in Japanese quail cathelicidins (CjCATH2 and CjCATHB1) that affect their antimicrobial activity against E. coli. Specifically, the I145F and Q148H substitutions in CjCATH2 and the P245H substitution in CjCATHB1 were found to influence the peptides' effectiveness.
full_output.methodology: Sequencing of CjCATH genes, synthesis of peptides, and antimicrobial activity assays against E. coli.

full_output.paper_title: Activity of β-Lactam Antibiotics against Metallo-β-Lactamase-Producing Enterobacterales in Animal Infection Models: a Current State of Affairs.
full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the activity of β-lactam antibiotics against metallo-β-lactamase (MBL)-producing Enterobacterales in animal infection models, highlighting discrepancies between in vitro and in vivo resistance profiles and the potential impact of zinc concentrations on MBL activity.
full_output.methodology: The paper is a review analyzing data from animal infection model studies evaluating β-lactam antibiotics against MBL-producing Enterobacterales.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies tetracycline resistance in Salmonella serovar Reading, highlighting the presence of antimicrobial resistance in low-abundance serovars within multiserovar populations.
full_output.methodology: CRISPR-SeroSeq and qPCR were used to detect and characterize antimicrobial resistance in Salmonella serovars.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of extended spectrum beta-lactamase genes in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolated from patients in rural Eastern Cape Province, South Africa.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaTEM, blaSHV, and blaCTX-M genes as the primary contributors to extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from the Eastern Cape Province, South Africa. Additionally, blaIMP was detected in a small percentage of isolates.
full_output.methodology: Real-time PCR was used to detect ESBL and MBL genes in P. aeruginosa isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Mycobacterium abscessus Strain Morphotype Determines Phage Susceptibility, the Repertoire of Therapeutically Useful Phages, and Phage Resistance.

mutations_found.validated_by: Mutant GD19_RM3 (Fig. 4F) has a frameshift mutation (4-bp deletion) in rpoZ coding for the RNA polymerase omega subunit, and is the sole sequence difference from GD19; rpoZ is clearly not essential for M. abscessus growth, as reported for M. smegmatis (37). Deletion of rpoZ in M. smegmatis does not alter the GPL profile but it reduces both sliding motility and biofilm formation, and has a notable reduction in short-chain mycolates on the cell surface (37). Similar surface changes in GD19_RM3 may be responsible for the inability of phage Muddy to infect.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in mps1, mps2, and mmpL4b that contribute to the rough colony morphotype in Mycobacterium abscessus, which affects phage susceptibility. Additionally, mutations in rpoZ, uvsD2, and uvrD2 are linked to phage resistance.
full_output.methodology: Sequencing of clinical isolates, comparison of smooth and rough variants, and assessment of phage susceptibility.

full_output.paper_title: Characterisation of twelve newly synthesised N-(substituted phenyl)-2-chloroacetamides with QSAR analysis and antimicrobial activity tests.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antimicrobial activity of twelve newly synthesized N-(substituted phenyl)-2-chloroacetamides against various bacterial and fungal strains, identifying compounds with potent activity against Gram-positive bacteria and yeasts.
full_output.methodology: The compounds were synthesized, characterized using spectroscopic techniques, and tested for antimicrobial activity via broth microdilution method.

full_output.paper_title: Modular Design of Membrane-Active Antibiotics: From Macromolecular Antimicrobials to Small Scorpionlike Peptidomimetics.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports on the development of a new class of small amphiphilic scorpionlike peptidomimetics with potent antimicrobial activity against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria. These compounds show high efficacy, low resistance development, and good biocompatibility.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the synthesis and evaluation of peptidomimetics for antimicrobial activity, including MIC testing, time-kill kinetics, biofilm inhibition, and in vivo efficacy in a mouse model.

full_output.paper_title: Analysis of Yersinia pseudotuberculosis Isolates Recovered from Deceased Mammals of a German Zoo Animal Collection.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes eight Y. pseudotuberculosis isolates from deceased zoo mammals, highlighting differences in virulence gene content and mobile genetic elements, with some isolates showing resistance to colistin.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, PFGE, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to analyze the isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that third-generation cephalosporins (3GC) and piperacillin/tazobactam (TZP) had distinct impacts on the microbiota of critically ill patients, with 3GC leading to increased abundance of Enterobacteriaceae and Enterococcaceae in certain body sites, while TZP was associated with an increase in commensal bacteria. No significant changes in antibiotic resistance were observed.
full_output.methodology: The study used 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing to analyze microbiota diversity and composition in endotracheal, perineal, and faecal samples from patients exposed to 3GC, TZP, or no β-lactams.

full_output.methodology: The study conducted antimicrobial susceptibility testing using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method on 221 bacterial isolates from urine samples.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of Microbiome Etiology Associated With Drug Resistance in Pleural Empyema.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in the pleural effusion microbiome of empyema patients, highlighting the association between microbial diversity and the abundance of ARGs. Key ARGs included tetQ, tetC, Gob-7, axyY, aadA14, mprf, erm46, and others, which conferred resistance to tetracycline, beta-lactam, aminoglycoside, MLS, and multidrug classes.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic analysis using Illumina sequencing to characterize the microbiome and resistome of pleural effusion samples from 45 empyema patients.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and Antimicrobial Resistance of Salmonella Isolated From Dead-in-Shell Chicken Embryos in Shandong, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla TEM, bla PSE, and qnrS as the main antimicrobial resistance genes in Salmonella isolates from dead-in-shell chicken embryos in Shandong, China, with bla TEM being the most common beta-lactamase gene and qnrS showing high prevalence.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify antimicrobial resistance genes and determine resistance profiles.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation and Characterization of Klebsiella Phages for Phage Therapy.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the isolation and characterization of 30 novel Klebsiella phages, highlighting their diversity, host ranges, and potential for phage therapy. None of the characterized phages were able to suppress the growth of Klebsiella for more than 12 hours, suggesting the need for phage cocktails for effective treatment.
full_output.methodology: The phages were isolated from various water sources, characterized through genome sequencing, and tested for host range and virulence.

full_output.paper_title: Research Note: Detection of antibiotic-resistance genes in commercial poultry and turkey flocks from Italy.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antibiotic-resistance genes in poultry and turkey flocks in Italy, including tetracycline, aminoglycoside, lincomycin, chloramphenicol, and vancomycin resistance genes. Notably, no colistin or carbapenem resistance genes were detected.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification and sequencing were used to detect antibiotic-resistance genes in environmental samples from poultry and turkey flocks.

full_output.paper_title: Outcome of Different Sequencing and Assembly Approaches on the Detection of Plasmids and Localization of Antimicrobial Resistance Genes in Commensal Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes qnrS1 and other antimicrobial resistance genes in commensal E. coli isolates using various sequencing and assembly approaches, highlighting the importance of hybrid assemblies for accurate detection and characterization of plasmid-borne resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, de novo assembly, and in silico analysis were used to identify and characterize antimicrobial resistance genes in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Spectroscopic Study of the Molecular Structure of the New Hybrid with a Potential Two-Way Antibacterial Effect.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the structure of a new ciprofloxacin-bismuth-chlorhexidine composite, focusing on the coordination of ciprofloxacin and chlorhexidine with bismuth(III) through various spectroscopic techniques.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized UV-VIS, FTIR, and NMR spectroscopy to analyze the structure of the ciprofloxacin-bismuth-chlorhexidine composite.

full_output.methodology: PCR and phenotypic susceptibility testing were used to identify AMR genes and resistance profiles in S. aureus isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of a Broad Host Range Bacteriophage KPP-5 Targeting Multidrug-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the KPP-5 phage, a podovirus with a broad host range against multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae. The phage genome lacks virulence and drug resistance genes, indicating its potential as a safe biocontrol agent.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, bioinformatics analysis, and experimental validation of phage properties.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Activity of Pyrazinamide Coordination Frameworks Synthesized by Mechanochemistry.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the synthesis and antimicrobial activity of pyrazinamide coordination frameworks with zinc, manganese, and silver. Silver-based compounds showed significantly enhanced antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli, Staphylococcus aureus, and Mycobacterium smegmatis compared to free pyrazinamide.
full_output.methodology: Mechanochemical synthesis, structural characterization by PXRD and SCXRD, and antimicrobial activity testing against selected bacterial strains.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of Macrolide-Resistant Mycoplasma pneumoniae during an Outbreak in a Primary School: Clinical Characterization of Hospitalized Children.

full_output.paper_title: Occurrence and Antimicrobial Resistance of Arcobacter spp. Recovered from Aquatic Environments.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of Extended-Spectrum β-Lactamase-Producing and AmpC β-Lactamase-Producing Enterobacterales Isolated from Companion Animals in Korea.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Basis of AmpC β-Lactamase Induction by Avibactam in Pseudomonas aeruginosa: PBP Occupancy, Live Cell Binding Dynamics and Impact on Resistant Clinical Isolates Harboring PDC-X Variants.

It identified specific mutations in AmpC (E247K and DelG229-E247) that reduced susceptibility to avibactam and increased resistance to ceftolozane and ceftazidime.

full_output.paper_title: Influence of Human Eating Habits on Antimicrobial Resistance Phenomenon: Aspects of Clinical Resistome of Gut Microbiota in Omnivores, Ovolactovegetarians, and Strict Vegetarians.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various antimicrobial resistance genes (ARG) in the gut microbiota of individuals with different eating habits, including tetracycline, beta-lactam, macrolide, aminoglycoside, sulfonamide, quinolone, and integron-related genes. No significant differences were observed in the distribution of ARG among omnivores, ovolactovegetarians, and strict vegetarians.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic DNA was extracted from fecal samples, and PCR screening was performed to detect 37 ARG. The study compared the presence of these genes among different dietary groups.

full_output.paper_title: Healthcare-Associated Laboratory-Confirmed Bloodstream Infections-Species Diversity and Resistance Mechanisms, a Four-Year Retrospective Laboratory-Based Study in the South of Poland.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a high prevalence of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and enterococci with high-level aminoglycoside resistance (HLAR) in intensive care units (ICUs) and surgical units. Carbapenem-resistant non-fermentative bacilli, such as Acinetobacter baumannii and Pseudomonas aeruginosa, were also prevalent in ICUs.
full_output.methodology: The study used MALDI-TOF for bacterial identification and EUCAST guidelines for resistance testing.

full_output.paper_title: Nasopharyngeal Carriage of Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) among Sickle Cell Disease (SCD) Children in the Pneumococcal Conjugate Vaccine Era.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of mecA, pvl, and tsst-1 genes in cefoxitin-resistant S. aureus isolates from SCD children, highlighting the prevalence of methicillin-resistant and virulent S. aureus strains in the nasopharynx.
full_output.methodology: Bacteriological culture, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and PCR for gene detection.

full_output.paper_title: Amphipathic Peptide Antibiotics with Potent Activity against Multidrug-Resistant Pathogens.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies WW307, an amphipathic peptide antibiotic, with potent activity against multidrug-resistant (MDR) pathogens, including those carrying bla NDM, mcr-1, and tet(X) genes. WW307 exhibits broad-spectrum antibacterial activity, effectively eradicating biofilms and showing minimal hemolytic activity.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antibacterial activity of WW307 through MIC determination, time-kill assays, biofilm inhibition, and mechanistic studies involving membrane permeability, membrane potential, and ROS production.

full_output.paper_title: Silver Nanoparticles from Oregano Leaves' Extracts as Antimicrobial Components for Non-Infected Hydrogel Contact Lenses.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the antimicrobial activity of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) synthesized from oregano leaves' extract (ORLE) against various bacterial strains including Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Escherichia coli, Staphylococcus epidermidis, and Staphylococcus aureus. The results showed that AgNPs(ORLE) exhibited significant antimicrobial effects, reducing bacterial viability and inhibiting biofilm formation.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized agar disc-diffusion, minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC), and biofilm elimination assays to evaluate the antimicrobial activity of AgNPs(ORLE) and ORLE against bacterial strains.

full_output.paper_title: Production of Membrane Vesicles in Listeria monocytogenes Cultured with or without Sub-Inhibitory Concentrations of Antibiotics and Their Innate Immune Responses In Vitro.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the production of membrane vesicles (MVs) in Listeria monocytogenes under sub-inhibitory concentrations of antibiotics and their effects on host cells. It found that sub-inhibitory concentrations of ampicillin (AMP), gentamicin (GEN), and trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole (SXT) increased MV production, and these MVs induced cytotoxicity and pro-inflammatory responses in Caco-2 cells.
full_output.methodology: The study used bacterial culture, MV isolation, nano particle tracking analysis (NTA), cell viability assays, and quantitative real-time PCR (qPCR) to analyze MV production and their effects on host cells.

full_output.paper_title: WGS of Commensal Neisseria Reveals Acquisition of a New Ribosomal Protection Protein (MsrD) as a Possible Explanation for High Level Azithromycin Resistance in Belgium.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the msr(D) gene, a ribosomal protection protein, as a novel mechanism for high-level azithromycin resistance in nonpathogenic Neisseria, particularly in Neisseria subflava. Additionally, the tetM gene was found in some Neisseria isolates, contributing to tetracycline resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and genotypic MIC prediction models were used to identify AMR genes and mutations in Neisseria isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Activity of Selected Medicinal Plants from a Sub-Saharan African Country against Bacterial Pathogens from Post-Operative Wound Infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antimicrobial activity of ethanolic and aqueous extracts of five medicinal plants against multidrug-resistant (MD-R) bacterial pathogens isolated from post-operative wounds.
full_output.methodology: The study used agar well diffusion method to evaluate the antimicrobial activity of plant extracts against reference strains and clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Resistance Genes and Diversity of Clones among ESBL- and Acquired AmpC-Producing Escherichia coli Isolated from Fecal Samples of Healthy and Sick Cats in Portugal.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various ESBL and qAmpC genes in E. coli isolates from cats, highlighting the presence of bla CTX-M-1, bla CTX-M-15, bla CTX-M-55, bla CTX-M-27, bla CTX-M-9, bla TEM, bla SHV-28, and bla CMY-2, along with other resistance genes such as tet(A), tet(B), sul1, sul2, aac(6')-Ib-cr, and armA.
full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing were used to identify antimicrobial resistance genes in E. coli isolates from fecal samples of cats.

full_output.paper_title: Culture-Independent Genotyping, Virulence and Antimicrobial Resistance Gene Identification of Staphylococcus aureus from Orthopaedic Implant-Associated Infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaZ and tetK as genes conferring resistance to penicillin and tetracycline, respectively, in Staphylococcus aureus from orthopaedic implant-associated infections using nanopore shotgun metagenomic sequencing.
full_output.methodology: Nanopore shotgun metagenomic sequencing and ResFinder analysis for AMR gene detection.

full_output.paper_title: Phytochemical Profiling of Lavandula coronopifolia Poir. Aerial Parts Extract and Its Larvicidal, Antibacterial, and Antibiofilm Activity Against Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the larvicidal, antibacterial, and antibiofilm activity of Lavandula coronopifolia aerial parts extract against Culex pipiens larvae and Pseudomonas aeruginosa. full_output.methodology: The study utilized HPLC-MS/MS for phytochemical profiling, larvicidal assays, and microbiological tests including MIC, MBC, and biofilm inhibition assays.

full_output.paper_title: Beneficial Impacts of Incorporating the Non-Natural Amino Acid Azulenyl-Alanine into the Trp-Rich Antimicrobial Peptide buCATHL4B.

full_output.paper_title: Variability in Bacteriophage and Antibiotic Sensitivity in Serial Pseudomonas aeruginosa Isolates from Cystic Fibrosis Airway Cultures over 12 Months.
full_output.key_findings: The study found variability in bacteriophage and antibiotic sensitivity among serial Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from cystic fibrosis patients over 12 months, highlighting the importance of current isolate testing for phage therapy selection.
full_output.methodology: The study used plaque and antibiotic disc diffusion assays to evaluate bacteriophage and antibiotic sensitivity in 102 Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from 24 cystic fibrosis patients.

full_output.paper_title: A Degeneration Gradient of Poplar Trees Contributes to the Taxonomic, Functional, and Resistome Diversity of Bacterial Communities in Rhizosphere Soils.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in the rhizosphere soils of poplar trees, highlighting the diversity of resistance mechanisms such as antibiotic efflux, target alteration, and target protection. Key ARGs included macB, streptomyces_cinnamoneus_EF-Tu, tetA48, mfd, patA, sav1866, Streptomyces_rishiriensis_parY, TaeA, arlR, and evgs, which conferred resistance to macrolides, tetracycline, and fluoroquinolones.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to characterize the microbial communities and their resistance genes in the rhizosphere soils of poplar trees.

full_output.paper_title: Mycobacterium tuberculosis Load in Host Cells and the Antibacterial Activity of Alveolar Macrophages Are Linked and Differentially Regulated in Various Lung Lesions of Patients with Pulmonary Tuberculosis.

full_output.methodology: Genetic analysis of Mtb DNA from resected lung tissues of patients with pulmonary tuberculosis.

full_output.paper_title: Spa typing of Staphylococcus aureus Isolated from Clinical Specimens from Outpatients in Iraq.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified 65 Staphylococcus aureus isolates, with 62 (95.4%) showing resistance to oxacillin and methicillin. full_output.methodology: PCR and spa typing were used to identify and characterize S. aureus isolates, along with antibiotic susceptibility testing.

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the presence of bla CTX-M-14 and bla CTX-M-15 genes in Escherichia coli isolates, indicating resistance to cefoxitin.

full_output.paper_title: Bacillus subtilis revives conventional antibiotics against Staphylococcus aureus osteomyelitis.

full_output.methodology: Experiments included MIC determination, time-kill assays, qRT-PCR, TEM, and in vivo mouse models.

full_output.paper_title: Epidemiology and Transmission of Carbapenemase-Producing Enterobacteriaceae in a Health Care Network of an Acute-Care Hospital and Its Affiliated Intermediate- and Long-Term-Care Facilities in Singapore.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several carbapenemase genes, including bla_IMI, bla_NDM-1, and bla_KPC-2, in Enterobacteriaceae isolates from an acute-care hospital and its affiliated intermediate- and long-term-care facilities in Singapore. These genes were associated with carbapenem resistance and were found in various bacterial species such as Enterobacter cloacae and Escherichia coli.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and multilocus sequence typing were used to analyze the genetic characteristics and transmission patterns of carbapenemase-producing Enterobacteriaceae.

full_output.paper_title: Microbiological Characterization of VNRX-5236, a Broad-Spectrum β-Lactamase Inhibitor for Rescue of the Orally Bioavailable Cephalosporin Ceftibuten as a Carbapenem-Sparing Agent against Strains of Enterobacterales Expressing Extended-Spectrum β-Lactamases and Serine Carbapenemases.

full_output.paper_title: Staphylococcus aureus Peptide Methionine Sulfoxide Reductases Protect from Human Whole-Blood Killing.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that methionine sulfoxide reductases (Msr) in Staphylococcus aureus protect against oxidative stress, particularly from hypochlorous acid (HOCl), and that the absence of all four Msr enzymes (Δ msr) leads to increased susceptibility to HOCl and human whole-blood killing.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized genetic deletion mutants, Msr activity assays, and growth curve analysis to investigate the role of Msr enzymes in S. aureus resistance to oxidative stress.

full_output.paper_title: Outer membrane and phospholipid composition of the target membrane affect the antimicrobial potential of first- and second-generation lipophosphonoxins.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates how the outer membrane and phospholipid composition of bacterial cells affect the antimicrobial activity of lipophosphonoxins (LPPOs). It shows that LPPO I is ineffective against Gram-negative bacteria like E. coli due to the barrier function of the outer membrane and lipopolysaccharides (LPS), whereas LPPO II exhibits broader activity. The effectiveness of LPPOs is also influenced by the phospholipid composition of the target membrane.
full_output.methodology: The study uses model membranes, live bacterial cells (Bacillus subtilis and Escherichia coli), and various biophysical techniques to analyze LPPO-induced membrane permeabilization and pore formation.

full_output.paper_title: Structural Basis of Metallo-β-lactamase Inhibition by N-Sulfamoylpyrrole-2-carboxylates.

blaNDM-1.validation_method: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing in combination with meropenem

full_output.key_findings: The study reports on the synthesis and mechanism of inhibition of N-sulfamoylpyrrole-2-carboxylates (NSPCs) which are potent inhibitors of clinically relevant B1 subclass metallo-β-lactamases, including NDM-1. The NSPCs restore meropenem efficacy in clinically derived E. coli and K. pneumoniae strains expressing blaNDM-1.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis of NSPCs, enzyme inhibition assays, crystallographic analysis, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.methodology: Genetic suppressor screens, whole genome sequencing, and biochemical assays were used to identify and characterize the PdtaS/PdtaR system.

full_output.methodology: Domain swapping, site-directed mutagenesis, and functional assays were used to identify and validate key residue changes in Tet(X) that contribute to tigecycline resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial activity and mechanism of plant flavonoids to gram-positive bacteria predicted from their lipophilicities.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified that the antibacterial activity of flavonoids against gram-positive bacteria correlates strongly with their lipophilicity, particularly ACD/LogP and LogD 7.40 values. The research established regression equations to predict MIC values based on these physicochemical parameters, highlighting the importance of lipophilicity in determining the effectiveness of flavonoids against Staphylococcus aureus and Bacillus subtilis.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized regression analysis on physicochemical parameters and antimicrobial activity data of 66 flavonoids to establish predictive models for MIC values against gram-positive bacteria.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of Hypervirulent Carbapenem-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae Coharboring a bla(NDM-1)-Carrying Virulent Plasmid and a bla(KPC-2)-Carrying Plasmid in an Egyptian Hospital.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the coexistence of a bla(NDM-1)-carrying virulent plasmid and a bla(KPC-2)-carrying plasmid in a hypervirulent carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae isolate, highlighting the complex genetic mechanisms underlying multidrug resistance and virulence in this pathogen.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, plasmid analysis, and bioinformatics tools were used to characterize the resistance and virulence genes in the isolate.

full_output.paper_title: Epidemiology of Multidrug-Resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa in the Middle East and North Africa Region.

Pseudomonas aeruginosa.notes: Mutations in oprD gene lead to reduced expression of the outer membrane porin, contributing to carbapenem resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple AMR genes and mutations associated with multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa in the MENA region, including bla VIM, bla IMP, bla NDM, bla GES, bla VEB, ampC, and efflux pump genes such as mexAB-oprM, mexCD-oprJ, mexEF-oprN, and mexXY.
