full_output.paper_title: Sewage sludge fertilization affects microbial community structure and its resistome in agricultural soils.
full_output.key_findings: Sewage sludge fertilization increases the diversity and abundance of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in agricultural soils, particularly those conferring resistance to fluoroquinolones, tetracyclines, macrolides, and sulfonamides.
full_output.methodology: High-throughput shotgun metagenomics was used to analyze the microbial communities and ARGs in soils fertilized with sewage sludge.

full_output.key_findings: Erythromycin disrupts Acinetobacter baumannii biofilms by destroying the quorum sensing system, as evidenced by the downregulation of abaI and abaR mRNA expression.
full_output.methodology: Fluorescence quantitative PCR and biofilm formation assays were used to evaluate the effect of erythromycin on the quorum sensing system of A. baumannii.

full_output.key_findings: The case report describes a patient with multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa septic arthritis, highlighting the challenges in treating such infections with limited antimicrobial options.
full_output.methodology: The study involved susceptibility testing of the P. aeruginosa isolate and treatment with a combination of colistin and piperacillin/tazobactam.

full_output.paper_title: Proven anti-virulence therapies in combating methicillin- and vancomycin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several virulence genes in MRSA and VRSA strains, including enterotoxins, hemolysins, and adhesion toxins, which are downregulated by anti-virulence compounds like ibuprofen, suggesting potential therapeutic applications.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic, molecular docking, and genetic studies were used to screen for anti-virulence activities of compounds such as coumarin, simvastatin, and ibuprofen.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified Aerococcus urinaeequi, Staphylococcus auricularis, and Staphylococcus haemolyticus as potential probiotics that may antagonize E. coli in the bovine udder microbiome.
full_output.methodology: 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing and metagenomic sequencing were used to analyze the milk microbiome composition and identify potential commensal bacteria that could outcompete E. coli.

full_output.paper_title: Lipidomic analyses reveal distinctive variations in homeoviscous adaptation among clinical strains of Acinetobacter baumannii, providing insights from an environmental adaptation perspective.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified genomic insertions containing genes involved in fatty acid desaturation, including fabA, fabB, and fabG, in ABVal2 and ABVal3. These genes are part of the FASII pathway and may contribute to the unique lipid profiles observed in these strains.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis, lipidomic profiling, and motility and biofilm assays were used to investigate the lipid composition and physiological adaptations of Acinetobacter baumannii strains.

full_output.paper_title: The microbial etiology and resistance patterns of cosmetic tourism-related infections in Ireland.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various bacterial species causing infections in cosmetic tourism patients, including multidrug-resistant organisms such as Vancomycin Resistant Enterococcus (VRE) and Extended Spectrum Beta Lactamase (ESBL) producers. Resistance to commonly prescribed antibiotics like co-amoxiclav and piperacillin-tazobactam was noted.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective-prospective cohort study analyzing microbial cultures and antimicrobial susceptibility results from patients with cosmetic tourism-related infections.

Key findings include resistance-conferring variants in hprrna23s, hprrna16s, pbp1, rdxa, frxa, frxb, gyra, and gyrb, along with caga positivity.
full_output.methodology: Next-generation sequencing (NGS) was used to analyze H. pylori and host genes involved in antibiotic resistance and PPI metabolism.

full_output.paper_title: Activity of Fluoroquinolones and Proton Pump Inhibitors against Resistant Oral Bacterial Biofilms, in silico and in vitro Analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the efficacy of fluoroquinolones and proton pump inhibitors against resistant oral bacterial biofilms. Omeprazole showed significant antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus, while fluoroquinolones were active against both S. epidermidis and S. aureus. Combination therapies showed enhanced antibiofilm and antiquorum sensing activities.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized molecular docking, MIC assays, antibiofilm assays, and time-kill kinetic studies to evaluate the efficacy of fluoroquinolones and proton pump inhibitors against oral bacterial biofilms.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular epidemiology of Streptococcus pneumoniae isolates causing invasive and noninvasive infection in Ethiopia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various serotypes and sequence types (STs) of Streptococcus pneumoniae, highlighting the presence of novel STs and diverse serotypes in Ethiopia. It also noted resistance patterns to antibiotics such as penicillin G and erythromycin among specific serotypes.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to analyze the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Distribution of chaperone-usher fimbriae and curli fimbriae among uropathogenic Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes various fimbrial adhesin genes (fimH, csgA, mrkD, foc, and papGII) in uropathogenic Escherichia coli (UPEC) strains, highlighting their prevalence and association with antimicrobial resistance patterns.
full_output.methodology: PCR and molecular screening techniques were used to identify fimbrial adhesin genes in UPEC isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the arsRBC operon as crucial for arsenic resistance in E. coli, demonstrating that ArsR, ArsB, and ArsC contribute to resistance against arsenite through distinct mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Differential proteomics and ICP-MS were used to analyze changes in metalloproteins and intracellular metal concentrations under arsenite stress.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial Activity of Novel Agent N-2-Hydroxypropyl Trimethyl Ammonium Chloride Chitosan against Streptococcus mutans.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the antibacterial activity of N-2-HACC against S. mutans, showing that it disrupts cell membrane integrity, increases cell wall permeability, interferes with bacterial protein and nucleic acid synthesis, perturbs glycolysis and the TCA cycle, and inhibits biofilm formation.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antibacterial effects of N-2-HACC through various assays including MIC determination, SEM observations, AKP activity measurement, conductivity, nucleic acid leakage, metabolic activity, and biofilm formation inhibition.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Resistance, Multilocus Sequence, and spa Typing of Staphylococcus aureus Isolated from Retail Raw Meat Products.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in S. aureus isolates from retail raw meat products, including blaZ, sulI, grlA, norA, tetK, chlA, tetM, aacA-aphD, and ermA. These genes conferred resistance to various antibiotics such as penicillin, sulfamethoxazole, fluoroquinolones, tetracycline, chloramphenicol, gentamicin, and macrolides. Additionally, 26% of the isolates were multidrug-resistant.
full_output.methodology: PCR and MIC testing were used to detect AMR genes and determine antimicrobial resistance profiles.

full_output.paper_title: Analysis on the epidemiological and drug resistance characteristics of osteoarticular tuberculosis in South-central China.
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed the epidemiological and drug resistance characteristics of osteoarticular tuberculosis (OATB) in Hunan province, China. It found that OATB primarily affects males, farmers, and individuals aged 20-29 and 60-69 years. The resistance situation of OATB was serious, with 14.87% resistant to rifampicin (RFP), 26.77% resistant to isoniazid (INH), 6.31% resistant to ethambutol (EMB), and 18.96% resistant to streptomycin (STR). Multi-drug resistance (MDR) was observed in 14.13% of cases.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of OATB patients with Mycobacterium tuberculosis culture positive at Hunan Chest Hospital from 2013 to 2022, involving collection of demographic, clinical, and drug susceptibility data.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) with a nasal carriage rate of 11.4% among children with asthma. High resistance to cefoxitin (99%) and penicillin (92%) was observed, while gentamicin resistance was lower (25%).
full_output.methodology: PCR and Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method for antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.key_findings: Water chlorination increases the relative abundance of integron 1, a genetic mechanism associated with the horizontal exchange of antibiotic resistance genes in spoilage and pathogenic bacteria.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic requirements for uropathogenic E. coli proliferation in the bladder cell infection cycle.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies hisF and neuC as critical genes for UPEC intracellular growth and survival, demonstrating their importance in the bladder cell infection cycle through gene deletion experiments.
full_output.methodology: Transposon-directed insertion-site sequencing (TraDIS) and gene deletion studies were used to identify and validate genes essential for UPEC growth in human bladder epithelial cells.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of pKPN945B, a novel transferable IncR plasmid from hypervirulent carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae, harboring bla(IMP-4) and qnrS1.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes a novel transferable IncR plasmid, pKPN945B, from a hypervirulent carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae strain, KPN945, which harbors the bla(IMP-4) and qnrS1 genes.
full_output.methodology: Genomic sequencing, PCR, Sanger sequencing, conjugation experiments, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Comparison of bloodstream infections due to Corynebacterium striatum, MRSA, and MRSE.
full_output.key_findings: Corynebacterium striatum bloodstream infections (BSIs) were found to be highly resistant to multiple antibiotics, with the majority showing susceptibility to linezolid, tigecycline, teicoplanin, and vancomycin. However, the appropriate antibiotic therapy within 24 hours was significantly lower compared to MRSA and MRSE BSIs.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective study analyzing blood culture data and antibiotic susceptibility testing.

full_output.key_findings: The study developed 3D-printed porous titanium rods with vancomycin-loaded hydrogels and PCL membranes for intelligent antibacterial drug release, demonstrating effective inhibition of Staphylococcus aureus growth and controlled vancomycin release in response to bacterial lipase.
full_output.methodology: The study fabricated 3D-printed titanium rods, incorporated vancomycin-loaded mPEG 750 - b -PCL 2500 gel, and coated them with a PCL layer. In vitro and in vivo experiments were conducted to evaluate antibacterial efficacy, drug release, and biocompatibility.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic and phenotypic diversity of Flavobacterium psychrophilum isolates from Czech salmonid fish farms.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterized the genetic and phenotypic diversity of 70 Flavobacterium psychrophilum isolates from Czech salmonid fish farms, revealing a high proportion of isolates with reduced susceptibility to several antibiotics, including oxolinic acid, oxytetracycline, flumequine, and enrofloxacin.
full_output.methodology: The study used multiplex PCR-based serotyping, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and whole-genome sequencing to analyze the genetic and phenotypic diversity of F. psychrophilum isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic resistance, virulence genes, and phylogenetic groups of bacteria isolated from wild passerine birds in Iran.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified tetracycline resistance genes (tet(A), tet(B), tet(M), tet(L)) and the blaTEM gene associated with ampicillin resistance in bacteria isolated from wild passerine birds in Iran.
full_output.methodology: PCR and antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to detect resistance genes and assess antimicrobial resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Complete genome of Escherichia coli sequence type 73 with acquired blaTEM-1 and high genotypic virulence load identified in human saliva.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the complete genome of a genomically hypervirulent E. coli ST73 strain carrying the acquired blaTEM-1 gene, which confers resistance to ampicillin and piperacillin.
full_output.methodology: Second and third generation sequencing with Illumina and Oxford-Nanopore-Technologies platforms, along with bioinformatic analysis of antibiotic resistance genes and virulence factors.

full_output.paper_title: Human breast milk isolated lactic acid bacteria: antimicrobial and immunomodulatory activity on the Galleria mellonella burn wound model.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antimicrobial and immunomodulatory activity of lactic acid bacteria (LAB) isolated from human breast milk against Pseudomonas aeruginosa in a Galleria mellonella burn wound model. Several LAB strains showed significant antibacterial activity, with some demonstrating efficacy comparable to gentamicin.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial overlay assay, in vivo burn wound infection model using Galleria mellonella, and qRT-PCR for gene expression analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Cefepime-taniborbactam demonstrates potent in vitro activity vs Enterobacterales with bla(OXA-48).
full_output.key_findings: Cefepime-taniborbactam shows potent in vitro activity against Enterobacterales carrying bla(OXA-48), significantly reducing MIC values and demonstrating bactericidal activity.
full_output.methodology: Agar dilution susceptibility testing, immunoblotting, and time-kill assays.

full_output.paper_title: ProT-Diff: A Modularized and Efficient Strategy for De Novo Generation of Antimicrobial Peptide Sequences by Integrating Protein Language and Diffusion Models.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents ProT-Diff, a deep generative model combining a protein language model and a diffusion model to generate antimicrobial peptides (AMPs). 44 out of 45 generated AMPs showed antimicrobial activity, with AMP_2 demonstrating potent broad-spectrum efficacy, low hemolysis, and minimal cytotoxicity. In vivo assessments confirmed its effectiveness against a drug-resistant E. coli strain.
full_output.methodology: ProT-Diff utilizes a pretrained protein language model (ProtT5-XL-UniRef50) and a diffusion model to generate AMPs. The model was trained on a dataset of known AMPs and non-AMPs, and the generated peptides underwent in silico, in vitro, and in vivo evaluations.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified non-carbapenemase β-lactamase genes and chromosomal mutations, including missense mutation or loss of ompK36 porin and frameshift missense mutation in efflux pump systems, as potential mechanisms of carbapenem resistance in NC-CRKP.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, comparative genomic and phylogenetic analyses, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to investigate the resistance mechanisms of NC-CRKP isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Selective degradation of phage RNAs by the Csm6 ribonuclease provides robust type III CRISPR immunity in Streptococcus thermophilus.
full_output.key_findings: Csm6 RNase activity is sufficient and essential for robust type III CRISPR immunity against phage infections in Streptococcus thermophilus.
full_output.methodology: In vivo phage interference assays, RNA sequencing, and genetic modifications of the type III-A system in S. thermophilus.

full_output.paper_title: Dietary zinc supplementation inhibits bacterial plasmid conjugation in vitro by regulating plasmid replication (rep) and transfer (tra) genes.
full_output.key_findings: Dietary zinc supplementation inhibits bacterial plasmid conjugation in vitro by regulating plasmid replication (rep) and transfer (tra) genes.
full_output.methodology: In vitro broth conjugation assays and quantitative RT-qPCR to analyze gene expression.

full_output.paper_title: Inhibition of Streptococcus pyogenes biofilm by Lactiplantibacillus plantarum and Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus.
full_output.key_findings: This study demonstrates that Lactiplantibacillus plantarum and Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus produce glycolipid bioactive compounds that reduce the viability of Streptococcus pyogenes in both planktonic and biofilm cultures.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the anti-biofilm properties of cell-free supernatants from L. plantarum and L. rhamnosus on S. pyogenes biofilms using various concentrations and growth conditions, along with enzymatic treatments and FTIR analysis to identify the active compounds.

full_output.paper_title: Lipopeptide antibiotics disrupt interactions of undecaprenyl phosphate with UptA.

mutations_found.validated_by: mass spectrometry analysis of protein-ligand interactions

UptA.evidence_note: The paper describes mutations in UptA that reduce C 55 -P binding, but does not state that these mutations confer resistance to any drugs.

full_output.paper_title: Predominance of enterotoxigenic Escherichia coli among ESBL/plasmid-mediated AmpC-producing strains isolated from diarrheic foals: a public health concern.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified ESBL and pAmpC-producing E. coli strains in diarrheic foals, highlighting the presence of bla TEM, bla CTX-M, bla SHV, bla OXA, and bla CMY-2 genes, along with the heat-stable enterotoxin (ST) gene, indicating a public health concern.
full_output.methodology: Molecular detection, sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were employed to characterize the AMR genes and virulence factors in E. coli isolates from diarrheic foals.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characteristics and antimicrobial susceptibility profiles of bovine mastitis agents in western Türkiye.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various bacterial species causing bovine mastitis, including Staphylococcus spp., Escherichia coli, Streptococcus spp., and others, and noted their antimicrobial resistance profiles.
full_output.methodology: 16S rRNA gene sequencing and Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method for antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization and biological activity of selenium nanoparticles biosynthesized by Yarrowia lipolytica.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the biosynthesis of selenium nanoparticles (SeNPs) by Yarrowia lipolytica and evaluates their antimicrobial and antioxidant activities. The SeNPs exhibited potent antimicrobial effects against various bacteria and the yeast Candida albicans, with minimal inhibitory concentrations (MICs) ranging from 80 to 640 μg/mL. Additionally, the nanoparticles showed significant antioxidant activity.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized electron microscopy, XRD, FTIR, and DLS for characterization of the SeNPs. Antimicrobial activity was assessed using the microdilution method, and antioxidant activity was evaluated via the DPPH assay.

full_output.paper_title: High frequency of acquired virulence factors in carbapenemase-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from a large German university hospital, 2013-2021.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the aerobactin gene iuc as a frequently acquired virulence factor in carbapenemase-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates, highlighting its association with hypervirulence and clinical infections.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and phenotypic tests were used to analyze the presence of acquired virulence factors in carbapenemase-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Impact of porin deficiency on the synergistic potential of colistin in combination with β-lactam/β-lactamase inhibitors against ESBL- and carbapenemase-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the resistance mechanisms conferred by bla CTX-M-15, bla KPC-2, and bla OXA-48 in Klebsiella pneumoniae, showing their roles in reducing susceptibility to ceftazidime and meropenem. Porin loss further increased MICs, highlighting the complex interplay of resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Chromosomal integration of β-lactamase genes, MIC testing, and time-lapse microscopy screening were used to evaluate resistance and synergy.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of antibacterial and anticancer properties of secondary metabolites isolated from soil Bacillus spp focusing on two strains of Bacillus licheniformis and Bacillus siamensis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies secondary metabolites from Bacillus licheniformis and Bacillus siamensis that exhibit antimicrobial and anticancer properties, inducing apoptosis and cell cycle arrest in PC-3 prostate cancer cells.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized GC-MS for identifying bioactive compounds, MTT assay for cytotoxicity, flow cytometry for apoptosis analysis, and real-time PCR for gene expression profiling.

full_output.paper_title: Nosocomial carbapenem-drug resistant Acinetobacter baumannii, related factors and clinical outcomes in Northeast Iran.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies carbapenem resistance as a significant risk factor for mortality in patients with Acinetobacter baumannii infections, emphasizing the clinical impact of multidrug-resistant strains in hospital settings.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective cross-sectional study analyzing patient data, antibiotic susceptibility testing, and clinical outcomes.

full_output.paper_title: Experimental evolution under different nutritional conditions changes the genomic architecture and virulence of Acinetobacter baumannii.

ata.notes: The deletion of the ata gene is associated with decreased biofilm formation and altered PMB susceptibility.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several AMR genes, including aph(6)-I, aphE, bla oxa-133, nepA, aac2-I, and bap, which show altered expression in evolved Acinetobacter baumannii strains under different nutritional conditions. These genes are associated with resistance to various antibiotics and biofilm formation.
full_output.methodology: Transcriptome analysis, PCR assays, and biofilm formation assays were used to investigate gene expression and phenotypic changes in evolved Acinetobacter baumannii strains.

full_output.key_findings: The study models the impact of doxycycline post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) on gonorrhoea prevalence and antimicrobial resistance in men who have sex with men (MSM) in the USA, highlighting that while PEP reduces infection rates, it accelerates tetracycline resistance.
full_output.methodology: A deterministic compartmental model was used to simulate gonorrhoea transmission dynamics in an MSM population, incorporating parameters related to sexual behavior, treatment, and resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Neisseria meningitidis activates pyroptotic pathways in a mouse model of meningitis: role of a two-partner secretion system.

hrpB.encodes: channel-forming β-barrel activator/transporter protein of the HrpA/HrpB TPS
hrpB.notes: hrpB gene was inactivated in the 93/4286 strain to create the isogenic mutant 93/4286Ω hrpB.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified that the hrpB gene, encoding the channel-forming β-barrel activator/transporter protein of the HrpA/HrpB two-partner secretion system, is essential for the virulence of Neisseria meningitidis in a mouse model of meningitis. The hrpB-defective mutant exhibited reduced bacterial replication and pyroptotic pathway activation compared to the wild-type strain.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a mouse model of meningitis, including generation of an isogenic hrpB mutant through insertional inactivation, followed by assessment of bacterial replication, survival, and pyroptotic pathway activation.
full_output.sample_size: 24 mice (6 mice/dose for wild-type, 7 mice/dose for mutant)

full_output.paper_title: Comparison of the mechanism of antimicrobial action of the gold(I) compound auranofin in Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria.

tolC.notes: Deletion of tolC increases susceptibility to auranofin.

gor.notes: Mutation in gor does not affect MIC

trxB.notes: Inhibition of trxB contributes to auranofin's mechanism of action

nemA.notes: Deletion of nemA increases resistance to auranofin.

full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the mechanism of auranofin's antimicrobial action in Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, focusing on the role of thioredoxin reductase (TrxB). Both E. coli and B. subtilis TrxB were inhibited by auranofin, but E. coli's resistance was attributed to the presence of glutathione rather than differences in TrxB susceptibility.
full_output.methodology: Protein expression, purification, and activity assays were conducted to evaluate the effect of auranofin on TrxB. Additionally, proteomic profiling and redox state measurements were used to assess cellular responses.

full_output.key_findings: This study identifies the importance of N-terminal high cationicity in antimicrobial peptides for activity against Gram-negative pathogens. It characterizes several designed peptides, including RIK-10+, which exhibits strong antimicrobial activity against Gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.methodology: The study involved designing and testing antimicrobial peptides based on the human cathelicidin LL-37, evaluating their antimicrobial activity, cytotoxicity, and mechanism of action through various assays.

full_output.paper_title: Exploring uncatalogued genetic variation in antimicrobial resistance gene families in Escherichia coli: an observational analysis.

blaTEM-1.validation_method: Analysis of variant alleles and their association with resistance phenotypes

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies significant uncatalogued genetic variation in antimicrobial resistance gene families in E. coli, particularly within the bla TEM-1 gene family. Synonymous mutations in bla TEM-1 variants were associated with reduced resistance to amoxicillin-clavulanic acid and piperacillin-tazobactam.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis of 9001 E. coli isolates using AMRFinder and empirical reclassification of gene families.

full_output.paper_title: The discovery and structural basis of two distinct state-dependent inhibitors of BamA.

PTB1-1.mechanism: targets a closed state of BamA

bamA.notes: Mutations in bamA conferred resistance to PTB1-1 and PTB2-1.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies two novel macrocyclic peptides, PTB1 and PTB2, which target distinct conformational states of BamA, a critical component of the BAM complex involved in outer membrane protein insertion and folding. PTB1 targets a closed state of BamA, while PTB2 targets an open state. Both peptides show potent antibacterial activity against various Gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.methodology: The study uses cryo-electron microscopy, surface plasmon resonance, and minimum inhibitory concentration assays to characterize the binding and inhibitory effects of PTB1 and PTB2 on BamA.

full_output.paper_title: First report of carbapenems encoding multidrug-resistant gram-negative bacteria from a pediatric hospital in Gaza Strip, Palestine.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple carbapenem resistance genes, including bla KPC-2, bla PDC-36/12, and bla POM-1, in multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria isolated from a pediatric hospital in the Gaza Strip. These genes were found in various bacterial species such as Escherichia coli and Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing was used to identify and characterize antibiotic resistance genes in 15 multidrug-resistant bacterial isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Complete genome sequence of a high-risk Escherichia coli ST10 isolated from avian feces in Pakistan.

qnrS1.mechanism: Protection of DNA gyrase from quinolone action

full_output.key_findings: The study presents the complete genome sequence of a high-risk Escherichia coli ST10 strain isolated from avian feces in Pakistan, identifying several plasmid-borne antibiotic resistance genes including blaTEM-1, blaCTX-M-15, aph(3'')-Ib, aph(6)-Id, qnrS1, sul2, tet(A), and dfrA14.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing and annotation using PacBio technology, followed by identification of antibiotic resistance genes using the Resistance Gene Identifier (RGI) tool.

full_output.paper_title: Salmonella enterica serovars Takoradi, Tananarive and Uganda from foods in Tripura, their virulence & antimicrobial resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Salmonella enterica serovars Takoradi, Tananarive, and Uganda from food samples in Tripura, highlighting their resistance to tetracycline and reduced susceptibility to azithromycin.
full_output.methodology: Biochemical tests, serotyping, antimicrobial susceptibility testing via disk diffusion, and PCR analysis for virulence genes.

full_output.paper_title: In vivo development of resistance to novel β-lactam/β-lactamase inhibitor combinations in KPC-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae infections: a case series.

full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were performed on longitudinal KPC-Kp strains from patients.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of mrkD, pgaC and wcaJ as biomarkers for rapid identification of K. pneumoniae biofilm infections from endotracheal aspirates and bronchoalveolar lavage.

wcaJ.role_in_paper: negative marker for biofilm-forming K. pneumoniae

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates mrkD, pgaC, and wcaJ as biomarkers for rapid identification of biofilm-forming K. pneumoniae from clinical samples using RT-PCR. The assay showed high sensitivity and specificity for detecting K. pneumoniae and distinguishing biofilm-forming from non-biofilm-forming strains.
full_output.methodology: RT-PCR, biofilm formation assay, and metagenomic sequencing were used to evaluate the genes as biomarkers for K. pneumoniae biofilm infections.
full_output.sample_size: 351 isolates of K. pneumoniae from bloodstream infections and 114 isolates from respiratory infections

full_output.paper_title: Plasmodium falciparum quinine resistance is multifactorial and includes a role for the drug/metabolite transporters PfCRT and DMT1.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies DMT1 and ftsh1 as novel contributors to quinine resistance in Plasmodium falciparum, along with pfcrt. DMT1 is a drug/metabolite transporter that localizes to the digestive vacuole and lipid bodies, while ftsh1 is an ATP-dependent zinc metalloprotease involved in resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Genetic cross, QTL mapping, CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing, drug assays, and subcellular localization studies.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characterization and genotype of multi-drug resistant Staphylococcus epidermidis in nasal carriage of young population, Mahasarakham, Thailand.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antimicrobial resistance genes in Staphylococcus epidermidis isolates from nasal carriers, including mecA, ermA, tetM, tetL, and biofilm-associated genes icaA and icaD.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of resistance genes and biofilm-associated genes, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and biofilm formation assays.

full_output.paper_title: Features and efficacy of triple-targeted therapy for patients with EGFR-mutant non-small-cell lung cancer with acquired BRAF alterations who are resistant to epidermal growth factor receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitors.

BRAF.notes: BRAF V600E mutation was the most common subtype detected in patients with acquired BRAF alterations.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified BRAF mutations and fusions as resistance mechanisms in EGFR-mutant NSCLC patients resistant to EGFR-TKIs, with BRAF V600E being the most common mutation. Triple-targeted therapy with prior EGFR-TKIs plus RAF and MEK inhibitors showed improved progression-free survival.
full_output.methodology: Next-generation sequencing (NGS) and clinical outcome analysis were used to identify BRAF alterations and assess the efficacy of triple-targeted therapy.

full_output.paper_title: Activity-based protein profiling guided new target identification of quinazoline derivatives for expediting bactericide discovery: Activity-based protein profiling derived new target discovery of antibacterial quinazolines.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified FabF as a new target for quinazoline derivatives, showing that compound 7a selectively and covalently binds to FabF, inhibiting fatty acid biosynthesis and damaging cell membrane integrity, thus killing the bacteria.
full_output.methodology: Activity-based protein profiling, molecular docking, molecular dynamic simulations, and Western blot analysis were used to validate the target and mechanism of action of compound 7a.

full_output.paper_title: A highly conserved SusCD transporter determines the import and species-specific antagonism of Bacteroides ubiquitin homologues.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies ButCD, a highly conserved SusCD transporter in Bacteroides fragilis, as the transporter for BfUbb, an antimicrobial ubiquitin homologue. ButCD determines the species-specific toxicity of BfUbb by facilitating its import into recipient cells.
full_output.methodology: Transposon mutagenesis, cryo-EM structure analysis, and functional assays were used to characterize the role of ButCD in BfUbb import and toxicity.

full_output.paper_title: Enhancing antifungal and antibacterial properties of denture resins with nystatin-coated silver nanoparticles.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antifungal and antibacterial effects of nystatin-coated silver nanoparticles (Nys-coated AgNPs) embedded in acrylic resin, showing that Nys-coated AgNPs (10% w/w) effectively inhibited C. albicans growth and exhibited significant antibacterial activity against S. mutans.
full_output.methodology: The study synthesized and characterized AgNPs and Nys-coated AgNPs, prepared PMMA disks with varying concentrations, and evaluated their antifungal and antibacterial properties using agar diffusion assays and MIC/MBC tests.

full_output.paper_title: Unraveling the genomic diversity of the Pseudomonas putida group: exploring taxonomy, core pangenome, and antibiotic resistance mechanisms.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple beta-lactamase genes in Pseudomonas putida group strains, highlighting their role in beta-lactam resistance.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis and clustering of Pseudomonas genomes using the GRUMPS pipeline.

full_output.paper_title: Structure-guided discovery of novel dUTPase inhibitors with anti-Nocardia activity by computational design.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Ns dUTPase as a promising target for anti-Nocardia drugs and discovers novel inhibitors, including compounds 4b and 12b, which show potent anti-Nocardia activity with low cytotoxicity.
full_output.methodology: Computational design, crystallography, molecular docking, and enzyme inhibition assays.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical and genomic characterization of carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales bloodstream infections in patients with hematologic malignancies.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla KPC-2 and bla NDM-5 as the主要 carbapenemase genes in carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales (CRE) bloodstream infections among patients with hematologic malignancies.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and enzymatic profiling were used to identify AMR genes in CRE isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Interactions between Helcococcus kunzii and Staphylococcus aureus: How a commensal bacterium modulates the virulence and metabolism of a pathogen in a chronic wound in vitro model.
full_output.key_findings: Helcococcus kunzii secretes proteins that downregulate the agrA gene in Staphylococcus aureus, reducing its virulence. Key secreted proteins include polysaccharide deacetylase, peptidoglycan DD-metalloendopeptidase, glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase, trypsin-like peptidase, and an extracellular solute-binding protein.
full_output.methodology: Proteomic analysis and qRT-PCR were used to study the interaction between H. kunzii and S. aureus in a chronic wound model.

full_output.paper_title: Nucleotide sequence variants, gene expression and serum profile of immune and antioxidant markers associated with bacterial diarrhea susceptibility in Barki lambs.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified eleven single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) linked to either diarrhea resistance or susceptibility in Barki lambs. Virulent genetic markers of pathogenic characteristics of E. coli and Salmonella were detected in all diarrheic lambs.
full_output.methodology: PCR-DNA sequencing and real-time PCR were used to analyze immune, antioxidant, and gastrointestinal health genes in healthy and diarrheic lambs.

full_output.paper_title: Computational and Experimental Analysis of NHC-TP Analogues for SARS-CoV-2 RdRp Inhibition
full_output.key_findings: The study identified and evaluated several NHC-TP analogues for their binding affinity and selectivity towards SARS-CoV-2 RdRp, highlighting their potential as antiviral agents.
full_output.methodology: The research combined molecular dynamics simulations, MM-GBSA binding free energy calculations, and docking studies to analyze the interactions of NHC-TP analogues with SARS-CoV-2 RdRp.

full_output.paper_title: Integrating whole genome sequencing and machine learning for predicting antimicrobial resistance in critical pathogens: a systematic review of antimicrobial susceptibility tests.
full_output.key_findings: This systematic review evaluates the efficacy of machine learning (ML) approaches in predicting antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in critical pathogens (CP) using whole genome sequencing (WGS) and antimicrobial susceptibility testing (AST).
full_output.methodology: Systematic review of studies published between 2016 and 2023, focusing on ML models for AMR prediction using WGS and AST data.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of pathogens and antimicrobial resistance of isolated Staphylococcus spp. in bovine mastitis milk in South Korea, 2018-2022.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antimicrobial resistance genes in Staphylococcus spp. isolated from bovine mastitis milk, including mecA, blaZ, tetK, ermC, lnuA, and lnuB. These genes were associated with resistance to penicillins, tetracyclines, erythromycin, and lincomycin.
full_output.methodology: PCR and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize antimicrobial resistance genes in Staphylococcus isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified a high level of multidrug resistance (MDR) among Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates in Saudi Arabia, with 22.2% classified as difficult-to-treat (DTR) and 5.4% as pandrug-resistant (PDR). High susceptibility was observed to amikacin (76.8%), while susceptibility to colistin was 43.8%.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using broth microdilution (BMD) with Sensititre GNX3F plates according to CLSI guidelines.

full_output.paper_title: Sentinel Surveillance reveals phylogenetic diversity and detection of linear plasmids harboring vanA and optrA among enterococci collected in the United States.

vanA.validation_method: whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing

optrA.validation_method: whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing

full_output.key_findings: The study identified vanA and optrA genes in enterococci, highlighting the presence of glycopeptide and oxazolidinone resistance mechanisms. Linear plasmids carrying these genes were detected, emphasizing the importance of monitoring resistance spread.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and phylogenetic analysis were used to characterize resistance mechanisms in enterococci.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular basis of cell membrane adaptation in daptomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecalis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies cls1 and cls2 as cardiolipin synthases essential for daptomycin resistance in Enterococcus faecalis, and highlights the role of LiaY in mediating membrane remodeling associated with resistance.
full_output.methodology: Trans-complementation, lipid analysis, qPCR, and mutant analysis were used to investigate the role of cls1, cls2, and liaY in daptomycin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Mucosal sugars delineate pyrazine vs pyrazinone autoinducer signaling in Klebsiella oxytoca.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the leup operon and pyr gene as crucial for leupeptin and pyrazine biosynthesis in Klebsiella oxytoca, respectively, with Neu5Ac serving as a key activator for leupeptin production.
full_output.methodology: The research utilized a GFP-based reporter system, HPLC-QTOF-MS, and genetic manipulation to investigate the biosynthesis of leupeptin and pyrazines in K. oxytoca.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial and antibiotic-potentiating effect of calcium peroxide nanoparticles on oral bacterial biofilms.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that calcium peroxide nanoparticles (CaO2 NP) enhance the antimicrobial efficacy of tobramycin (Tob) against Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilms, both in vitro and in situ. CaO2 NP alone increased the fraction of dead bacteria in oral biofilms, and when combined with Tob, further improved bacterial killing.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized in vitro biofilm assays, fluorescence microscopy, and in situ oral biofilm treatment protocols to evaluate the antimicrobial and antibiotic-potentiating effects of CaO2 NP.

full_output.paper_title: Colloidal Structure Dictates Antimicrobial Efficacy in LL-37 Self-Assemblies With Glycerol Monooleate.
full_output.key_findings: The study explores how the colloidal structure of LL-37 self-assemblies with glycerol monooleate (GMO) affects antimicrobial efficacy against Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Staphylococcus aureus. It finds that the antimicrobial activity varies with the LL-37/GMO ratio, with cylindrical micelles showing greater efficacy than vesicles or cubosomes.
full_output.methodology: The study uses SAXS, DLS, cryo-TEM, and antimicrobial assays to investigate the self-assembly of LL-37 with GMO and evaluate its antimicrobial effects.

full_output.paper_title: Biological Potential and Essential Oil Profile of Two Wild Apiaceae Species from Algeria (Daucus carota L. and Foeniculum vulgare Mill.): Larvicidal and Antibacterial Effects.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the larvicidal and antibacterial effects of essential oils (EOs) from Daucus carota L. (DCEO) and Foeniculum vulgare Mill. (FVEO). DCEO and FVEO showed strong larvicidal activity against Culex pipiens larvae with LC50 values of 30.6 and 34.7 ppm, respectively. DCEO exhibited moderate antibacterial activity against Gram-positive bacteria, while FVEO showed limited effectiveness against Gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.methodology: Essential oils were extracted from aerial parts using steam distillation and analyzed via GC/MS. Larvicidal and antibacterial activities were assessed using standard protocols.

full_output.paper_title: Essential Oil-Based Soap with Clove and Oregano: A Promising Antifungal and Antibacterial Alternative against Multidrug-Resistant Microorganisms.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antimicrobial activity of clove, oregano, and thyme essential oils against various bacterial and fungal strains, including multidrug-resistant isolates, and found them to be effective inhibitors.
full_output.methodology: The study used in vitro and in vivo antimicrobial assays, including MIC, MBC, and MFC, along with GC-MS analysis to determine the chemical composition of the oils.

full_output.paper_title: Design, Synthesis, and Antimicrobial Evaluation of New Thiopyrimidine-Benzenesulfonamide Compounds.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents the design, synthesis, and evaluation of new thiopyrimidine-benzenesulfonamide compounds with broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity against Gram-positive, Gram-negative, and fungal strains, particularly showing effectiveness against K. pneumoniae and P. aeruginosa.
full_output.methodology: Chemical synthesis, antimicrobial activity testing, MIC and MBC assays, and biofilm formation inhibition experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial Activity and Mechanism of Taxillμs chinensis (DC.) Danser and Its Active Ingredients.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies 4-indolecarbaldehyde as an active antibacterial compound from Taxillμs chinensis, which disrupts bacterial membrane permeability, leading to reduced viability of pathogens such as Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial activity testing, growth curve analysis, extracellular conductivity measurement, and potassium ion content determination.

full_output.paper_title: Antioxidant and Antibacterial Activities of Selected Medicinal Plants from Addis Ababa against MDR-Uropathogenic Bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the antioxidant and antibacterial activities of Thymus schimperi, Rhamnus prinoides, and Justicia schimperiana against MDR-uropathogenic bacteria, highlighting the potential of these plants in combating antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study conducted phytochemical analysis, GC-MS, antioxidant assays, and in vitro antibacterial activity tests.

full_output.paper_title: Silver nanoparticles synthesized using aerial part of Achillea fragrantissima and evaluation of their bioactivities.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the antibacterial and anticancer properties of silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) synthesized from the aerial parts of Achillea fragrantissima. The AgNPs show significant antibacterial activity against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, with the lowest MIC value recorded against Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Additionally, the AgNPs exhibit potent cytotoxic effects on MCF-7 and HepG2 cancer cell lines, inducing apoptosis through the activation of caspase-3, -8, and -9, and the downregulation of anti-apoptotic genes Bcl-xL and Bcl-2.
full_output.methodology: The study involves the green synthesis of AgNPs using the aqueous extract of A. fragrantissima aerial parts, followed by characterization via UV-Vis spectroscopy, FTIR, SEM, and TEM. The antibacterial activity was assessed using disc diffusion and MIC assays, while the cytotoxicity and apoptotic effects were evaluated using MTT assays and RT-PCR.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified N87K and D91N mutations in the gyrA gene associated with fluoroquinolone resistance and A2147G mutation in the rrl gene associated with clarithromycin resistance in Helicobacter pylori strains from Serbia.
full_output.methodology: Molecular testing using GenoType Helico DR kit for detection of resistance genes and mutations in H. pylori.

full_output.paper_title: Analyzing Antibiotic Resistance in Bacteria from Wastewater in Pakistan Using Whole-Genome Sequencing.

gyrA.notes: confers resistance to quinolones

parC.notes: confers resistance to quinolones

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several AMR genes and mutations in wastewater isolates from Pakistan, highlighting the presence of carbapenemases like blaNDM-5 and blaOXA-1, as well as quinolone resistance determinants such as gyrA and parC mutations. These findings emphasize the role of wastewater as a reservoir for clinically relevant AMR genes.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and phenotypic testing were used to identify AMR genes and mutations in wastewater isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Guanethidine Restores Tetracycline Sensitivity in Multidrug-Resistant Escherichia coli Carrying tetA Gene.

tetA.validation_method: synergistic effect with tetracycline, MIC reduction, molecular docking

full_output.key_findings: Guanethidine restores tetracycline sensitivity in multidrug-resistant E. coli carrying the tetA gene by inhibiting the TetA efflux pump, leading to increased intracellular tetracycline concentration and reduced MIC.
full_output.methodology: MIC measurements, FIC index determination, fluorescence assays, molecular docking, RT-PCR, and plasmid construction.

full_output.paper_title: Development of a High-Resolution Melting Method for the Detection of Clarithromycin-Resistant Helicobacter pylori in the Gastric Microbiome.

23S rRNA.role_in_paper: key genetic target associated with CLR resistance

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the A2143G mutation in the 23S rRNA gene as a key determinant of clarithromycin resistance in Helicobacter pylori, and develops an HRM method for its detection.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, HRM analysis, and MIC testing were used to identify and validate the A2143G mutation in the 23S rRNA gene associated with clarithromycin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Combinations of Terminalia bellirica (Gaertn.) Roxb. and Terminalia chebula Retz. Extracts with Selected Antibiotics Against Antibiotic-Resistant Bacteria: Bioactivity and Phytochemistry.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antibacterial activity of Terminalia bellirica and Terminalia chebula fruit extracts against various antibiotic-resistant bacteria, showing notable zones of inhibition and minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) against S. aureus, MRSA, E. coli, ESBL E. coli, K. pneumoniae, and ESBL K. pneumoniae. The extracts exhibited varying degrees of antibacterial activity, with some showing good activity against the tested strains. The study also identified several phytochemicals in the extracts, including flavonoids, tannins, and phenolic acids, which may contribute to their bioactivity.
full_output.methodology: The study used agar disc diffusion and broth microdilution assays to evaluate the antibacterial activity of the plant extracts. LC-MS was used for metabolomic fingerprinting of the extracts.

full_output.paper_title: Development of a One-Step Multiplex qPCR Assay for Detection of Methicillin and Vancomycin Drug Resistance Genes in Antibiotic-Resistant Bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a one-step multiplex qPCR assay for the detection of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) and vancomycin-resistant enterococci (VRE) by targeting the mecA, vanA, and vanB genes.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized a one-step multiplex qPCR assay to detect the mecA, vanA, and vanB genes in clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Susceptibility of Enterococci Isolated from Nestlings of Wild Birds Feeding in Supplementary Feeding Stations: The Case of the Canarian Egyptian Vulture.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified antimicrobial resistance patterns in Enterococci isolated from Canarian Egyptian vulture chicks, highlighting resistance to quinolones, vancomycin, and linezolid. It emphasizes the need for further research on antimicrobial resistance in wildlife.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed using the disk diffusion method and E-test ® for Enterococci isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Escherichia coli Occurrence and Antimicrobial Resistance in a Swine Slaughtering Process.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high levels of antimicrobial resistance in E. coli isolates from swine slaughterhouses, with 80.71% of isolates being multidrug resistant. ESBL-producing isolates were found to be highly resistant to multiple antibiotics, including amoxicillin, tetracycline, and chloramphenicol.
full_output.methodology: The study used agar disk diffusion tests and double-disk synergy tests to determine antimicrobial resistance profiles and detect ESBL-producing E. coli isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study compares direct cDNA and PCR-cDNA nanopore sequencing for transcriptomic analysis of E. coli isolates, identifying 36 AMR genes including blaCTX-M-15, aac(3)-IIe, catB3, blaOXA-1, aac(6')-Ib-cr5, tet(A), blaTEM-1, dfrA14, sul2, aph(3")-Ib, aph(6)-Id, tet(B), aadA5, dfrA17, mph(A), blaCTX-M-27, sul1, and dfrA5.
full_output.methodology: The study uses nanopore RNA-Seq with direct cDNA and PCR-cDNA kits to analyze transcriptomes of four E. coli isolates, focusing on AMR gene expression.

full_output.paper_title: Toxoplasma gondii macrophage migration inhibitory factor shows anti-Mycobacterium tuberculosis potential via AZIN1/STAT1 interaction.

CD74.notes: The R62K mutation in CD74 competes with TgMIF for binding, reducing TgMIF-induced inflammatory responses.

STAT1.encodes: signal transducer and activator of transcription 1
STAT1.notes: The K76R mutation in STAT1 enhances TgMIF-induced M1 macrophage polarization.

AZIN1.notes: AZIN1 inactivation impairs TgMIF's ability to restore mitochondrial function.

full_output.key_findings: TgMIF interacts with CD74, STAT1, and AZIN1 to modulate inflammatory responses, mitochondrial function, and macrophage polarization, enhancing host defense against Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
full_output.methodology: Protein interaction studies, gene expression analysis, and functional assays in macrophages and mouse models.

full_output.paper_title: Structural basis for regulation of a CBASS-CRISPR-Cas defense island by a transmembrane anti-σ factor and its ECF σ partner.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the DdvA-DdvS regulon as a critical component of Myxococcus xanthus defense against phage Mx4. The structural and functional analysis reveals that DdvA and DdvS form a transmembrane anti-σ-ECF σ pair that regulates the expression of a genomic island containing two CBASS and one CRISPR-Cas system, contributing to antiviral defense.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized cryo-electron microscopy, nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, and biochemical assays to analyze the structure and function of the DdvA-DdvS complex and its role in antiviral defense.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the synergistic effect of fosfomycin and colistin against KPC-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae, highlighting their ability to induce ROS accumulation and inhibit ribosomal protein transcription, leading to reduced resistance and cytotoxicity.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized time-kill assays, transcriptomic analysis, and oxidative stress-related assays to evaluate the synergistic effects of fosfomycin and colistin against KPC-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae.

full_output.paper_title: Chloramphenicol Interferes with 50S Ribosomal Subunit Maturation via Direct and Indirect Mechanisms.
full_output.key_findings: Chloramphenicol (CAM) interferes with the maturation of the 50S ribosomal subunit in E. coli by affecting the formation of the central protuberance (CP), H89, and H58, as well as the folding of H68 and PTC. CAM binding to ribosomal precursors was confirmed through ELISA, indicating direct and indirect mechanisms of action.
full_output.methodology: Label-free quantitative mass spectrometry, cryo-electron microscopy, and ELISA were used to analyze the effects of CAM on ribosome maturation.

full_output.paper_title: In Vitro Cytotoxicity and Antimicrobial Activity against Acne-Causing Bacteria and Phytochemical Analysis of Galangal (Alpinia galanga) and Bitter Ginger (Zingiber zerumbet) Extracts.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antimicrobial activity of galangal and bitter ginger extracts against acne-causing bacteria, including C. acnes, S. aureus, and S. epidermidis, and identified phytochemicals such as zerumbone, tectorigenin, piperic acid, and others that may contribute to their antimicrobial and antioxidant properties.
full_output.methodology: The study used broth micro-dilution assays to determine antimicrobial activity, DPPH assays for antioxidant activity, and GC-MS/LC-MS/MS for phytochemical analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of Antimicrobial Resistant Escherichia coli from Sinking Creek in Northeast Tennessee.
full_output.key_findings: The study found a high prevalence of multidrug-resistant (MDR) Escherichia coli in Sinking Creek, with resistance to ciprofloxacin (64.2%), nitrofurantoin (62.7%), and ceftriaxone (40.1%). Colistin resistance was detected in 6% of isolates.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing was performed using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method and broth disk elution for colistin. E. coli isolates were cultured from water samples collected monthly over 6 months.

full_output.paper_title: Characteristics of the Enterococcus Phage vB_EfS_SE, and the Properties of Its Chimeric Endolysins Harboring a PlySE-Carbohydrate-Binding Domain and a Synthetic Enzymatic Domain.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the Enterococcus phage vB_EfS_SE and its endolysins, including PlySE, PlyIME-SE, and PlySheep-SE, which show lytic activity against several Enterococcus species. The phage exhibits stability under various temperature and pH conditions, and the endolysins display distinct thermostability and pH activity profiles.
full_output.methodology: The phage was isolated, its genome sequenced, and endolysin genes were cloned and expressed. The lytic activity of the endolysins was assessed through spot tests and turbidimetric assays.

full_output.paper_title: Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus among Students: Nasal Carriage Rate, Contributing Factors, and Antimicrobial Susceptibility.

mecA.validation_method: PCR detection of mecA gene in MR-SA isolates

full_output.key_findings: The study identified the mecA gene as a key determinant of methicillin resistance in Staphylococcus aureus isolates from students, with 95.5% of MR-SA isolates carrying this gene.
full_output.methodology: PCR amplification and sequencing of the mecA gene in S. aureus isolates.

full_output.paper_title: MOF-Enhanced Phototherapeutic Wound Dressings Against Drug-Resistant Bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents a novel phototherapeutic wound dressing using MIL-100(Fe) nanoparticles loaded with IR775 dye, demonstrating effective eradication of MRSA through low-dose photodynamic therapy and photothermal therapy.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis and characterization of MOF@dye nanosystems, electrospinning of gelatin films, and in vitro and in vivo evaluations of antibacterial efficacy.

full_output.paper_title: Evolution of the use, effectiveness and safety of bismuth-containing quadruple therapy for Helicobacter pylori infection between 2013 and 2021: results from the European registry on H. pylori management (Hp-EuReg).
full_output.key_findings: The study analyzed the use, effectiveness, and safety of bismuth-containing quadruple therapy (BQT) for Helicobacter pylori infection in Europe from 2013 to 2021. It found that BQT usage increased significantly, with the single-capsule BQT (ScBQT) being the most effective regimen, achieving cure rates above 90% in various regions.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized data from the European Registry on Helicobacter pylori Management (Hp-EuReg) to analyze the effectiveness of different BQT regimens, focusing on treatment outcomes, adherence, and safety.

full_output.key_findings: The study focuses on the role of the oral microbiota in the effectiveness of adjunctive antibiotics in treating periodontitis, highlighting the importance of microbial community shifts and their impact on clinical outcomes.
full_output.methodology: The study used topic models to analyze microbial communities and their association with clinical outcomes in periodontitis patients receiving antibiotic treatment.

full_output.paper_title: Synergistic effect of antibiotics, α-linolenic acid and solvent type against Staphylococcus aureus biofilm formation.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified that α-linolenic acid (LNA) synergizes with antibiotics (gentamicin, tobramycin, azithromycin) to reduce biofilm formation in Staphylococcus aureus, allowing for significant reductions in antibiotic doses.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the synergistic effects of antibiotics and LNA using metabolic activity tests, crystal violet assays, and checkerboard assays to determine biofilm inhibition and synergy.

full_output.paper_title: Virulence, multiple drug resistance, and biofilm-formation in Salmonella species isolated from layer, broiler, and dual-purpose indigenous chickens.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antimicrobial resistance genes in Salmonella isolates from different chicken types, including ant (3"-la), tet (A), tet (B), sul1, and sul2, indicating multidrug resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of antimicrobial resistance genes and antimicrobial susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Triple-Branch Catalytic Assembly DNAzyme Motivated DNA Tweezer for Sensitive and Reliable mecA Gene Detection in Staphylococcus aureus.

mecA.validation_method: fluorescent biosensor with triple-branch catalytic hairpin assembly (CHA) triggered DNAzyme switch-based DNA tweezer

full_output.key_findings: The study presents a fluorescent biosensor for detecting the mecA gene in Staphylococcus aureus using a triple-branch catalytic hairpin assembly (CHA) triggered DNAzyme switch-based DNA tweezer, achieving a low limit of detection of 1.5 fM and demonstrating high sensitivity and selectivity.
full_output.methodology: Fluorescent biosensor with triple-branch CHA and DNAzyme-controlled DNA tweezer for mecA detection.

full_output.paper_title: Severe co-infection caused by difficult-to-diagnose hypermucoviscous Klebsiella pneumoniae K1-ST82 in a patient with COVID-19: a case report.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports a case of severe co-infection with a difficult-to-diagnose hypermucoviscous Klebsiella pneumoniae K1-ST82 strain in a patient with COVID-19. The strain was genetically classified as hypervirulent K. pneumoniae (hvKp) with the presence of hvKp-associated virulence genes rmpA, iroCD, and iucABCD-iutA. The strain exhibited atypical phenotypes, including ampicillin susceptibility due to a defective bla SHV gene.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and MALDI-TOF MS analysis were used for strain identification and characterization.

full_output.paper_title: Rational Exploration of 2,4-Diaminopyrimidines as DHFR Inhibitors Active against Mycobacterium abscessus and Mycobacterium avium, Two Emerging Human Pathogens.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies P218, a 2,4-diaminopyrimidine, as a potent inhibitor of DHFR in Mycobacterium abscessus and Mycobacterium avium, demonstrating its potential as a therapeutic agent against NTM infections.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized enzymatic assays, structural analyses, and compound screening to evaluate the activity of P218 and its derivatives against NTM DHFRs.

full_output.paper_title: Multigeographic clinical assessment of a molecular diagnostic assay for detection of key codons to predict decreased susceptibility or resistance to cephalosporins in Neisseria gonorrhoeae.

penA.evidence_note: The paper states that the A311V mutation in the penA gene is critical for ceftriaxone resistance and that this mutation is associated with increased MIC values.

full_output.paper_title: Real-time plasmid transmission detection pipeline.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates a real-time plasmid transmission detection pipeline in SeqSphere+ for identifying carbapenemase-carrying plasmids and their transmission dynamics in clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: METTL3 confers oxaliplatin resistance through the activation of G6PD-enhanced pentose phosphate pathway in hepatocellular carcinoma.

full_output.sample_size: Multiple cell lines and mouse models

full_output.paper_title: Surgical site infection and antimicrobial use following caesarean section at QECH in Blantyre, Malawi: a prospective cohort study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified Staphylococcus aureus, Enterobacteriaceae, and Acinetobacter baumanni as the most common bacterial isolates from surgical site infections (SSIs) following caesarean sections. Resistance patterns showed that S. aureus was resistant to several antibiotics, while Enterobacteriaceae were sensitive to certain drugs but resistant to others. Acinetobacter baumannii was resistant to multiple antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Prospective cohort study involving 208 pregnant women who underwent caesarean sections, with wound swabs collected for microbiological culture and susceptibility testing using the Kirby-Bauer disk diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: PMCNA_RS00975 activates NF-κB and ERK1/2 through TLR2 and contributes to the virulence of Pasteurella multocida.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies PMCNA_RS00975 as a virulence factor in P. multocida, contributing to the activation of NF-κB and ERK1/2 pathways through TLR2, thereby enhancing the pathogenicity of the bacterium.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized gene knockout and complementation strategies, along with biochemical and molecular analyses to validate the role of PMCNA_RS00975 in virulence and signaling pathways.

full_output.paper_title: CRISPR/Cas9-Mediated Genome Editing of T4 Bacteriophage for High-Throughput Antimicrobial Susceptibility Testing.

lacZa.mechanism: overexpression of beta-galactosidase leads to color change upon reaction with CPRG
lacZa.validation_method: colorimetric detection using T4 lacZa phage

full_output.key_findings: The study describes the engineering of T4 bacteriophage with the lacZa gene using CRISPR/Cas9 for high-throughput antimicrobial susceptibility testing. The T4 lacZa phage enables colorimetric detection of bacterial growth and resistance through the overexpression of beta-galactosidase.
full_output.methodology: CRISPR/Cas9-mediated genome editing of T4 phage, colorimetric detection using CPRG, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing in urine samples.

full_output.paper_title: Metabolic interplay between Proteus mirabilis and Enterococcus faecalis facilitates polymicrobial biofilm formation and invasive disease.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the role of E. faecalis arcD and P. mirabilis argI in metabolic interplay that enhances biofilm formation and disease severity in polymicrobial infections.

full_output.paper_title: Aminoglycoside heteroresistance in Enterobacter cloacae is driven by the cell envelope stress response.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the CpxRA two-component system as essential for aminoglycoside heteroresistance in Enterobacter cloacae, demonstrating that its activation leads to increased resistance through cell envelope stress responses.
full_output.methodology: RNA sequencing, disk-diffusion assays, time-to-kill experiments, and genetic manipulation of the cpxRA gene.

full_output.paper_title: Development of a suite of Proteus mirabilis-derived urea-inducible promoters.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a suite of urea-inducible promoters derived from the urease promoter of Proteus mirabilis, focusing on optimizing their regulation and activity for gene expression in experimental urinary tract infections.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized reporter constructs and Miller assays to evaluate promoter activity and characterize the effects of sequence modifications on gene expression.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic characterization of a clonal emergent Salmonella Minnesota lineage in Brazil reveals the presence of a novel megaplasmid of resistance and virulence.

blaCMY-2.evidence_note: The paper states that bla CMY-2 is present in emergent genomes and is associated with resistance to ampicillin.

full_output.paper_title: High prevalence of carbapenem-resistant Enterobacter cloacae complex in a tertiary hospital over a decade.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic epidemiology and resistant genes of Acinetobacter baumannii clinical strains in Vietnamese hospitals.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified 52 antibiotic-resistant genes in 51 Acinetobacter baumannii strains, including blaADC-25, blaOXA-23, blaOXA-66, qnrD1, qnrVC6, catB8, floR, mph(E), msr(E), tet(B), tet(39), armA, ant(3'')-Ia, aph(3'')-Ib, aph(6)-Id, aph(3')-Ia, ARR-3, Sul1, sul2, and blaTEM-1D.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to identify antibiotic-resistant genes in Acinetobacter baumannii strains.

full_output.paper_title: Risk factors and drug resistance of adult community-onset urinary tract infections caused by Escherichia coli-producing extended-spectrum β-lactamase in the Chongqing region, China: a retrospective case-control study.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that ESBL-EC accounted for 48.7% of adult community-onset urinary tract infections in the Chongqing region, China. ESBL-EC showed high resistance to penicillins, cephalosporins, and quinolones, while showing 100% sensitivity to carbapenems and amikacin.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective case-control study analyzing drug resistance profiles of ESBL-EC isolates from patients with community-onset urinary tract infections.

full_output.paper_title: Single-cell landscape of innate and acquired drug resistance in acute myeloid leukemia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies BCL2 and CD36 as key players in innate and treatment-related venetoclax resistance in AML, with BCL2 downregulation and CD36 upregulation correlating with resistance.
full_output.methodology: Single-cell and bulk molecular profiling combined with ex vivo drug response assays.

full_output.paper_title: The CRISPR-dCas9 interference system suppresses inhA gene expression in Mycobacterium smegmatis.
full_output.key_findings: CRISPRi targeting the inhA gene in Mycobacterium smegmatis significantly reduced gene expression and increased susceptibility to isoniazid and rifampicin.

full_output.paper_title: An antimicrobial resistance gene situationer in the backyard swine industry of a Philippine City.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical Outcomes and Molecular Characteristics of Bacteroides fragilis Infections.

full_output.paper_title: bla(GES)-producing ST654 comprises a quarter of all carbapenem-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa in blood isolates from 15 hospitals.

full_output.paper_title: In vivo efficacy of enmetazobactam combined with cefepime in a murine pneumonia model induced by OXA-48-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the in vivo efficacy of cefepime/enmetazobactam against OXA-48-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae in a murine pneumonia model, demonstrating significant antibacterial effects compared to cefepime or meropenem monotherapies.

full_output.paper_title: A novel esterase regulates Klebsiella pneumoniae hypermucoviscosity and virulence.

wcsU.validation_method: deletion mutant studies showing reduced CPS acetylation and virulence

full_output.paper_title: H(2)S scavenger as a broad-spectrum strategy to deplete bacteria-derived H(2)S for antibacterial sensitization.

full_output.paper_title: Development of Novel Antimicrobial Agents with Potent Antibiofilm Activities
full_output.key_findings: The study presents new quaternary 3-substituted quinuclidine compounds, QA p Cl and QA p Br, which show potent antibacterial activity against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria. These compounds exhibit low toxicity to human cells and minimal potential to induce bacterial resistance. They also effectively inhibit biofilm formation.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antibacterial activity of synthesized quaternary 3-substituted quinuclidine compounds through MIC testing, biofilm inhibition assays, and cytotoxicity assessments.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular characteristics, risk factors, and clinical outcomes of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus infections among critically ill pediatric patients in Shanghai, 2016-2021.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) as a significant cause of infection among critically ill pediatric patients in Shanghai, highlighting the molecular characteristics and risk factors associated with MRSA infections. It found that MRSA strains showed higher resistance rates to several antibiotics compared to methicillin-susceptible S. aureus (MSSA) strains.
full_output.methodology: The study involved a retrospective case-control analysis of S. aureus isolates from critically ill pediatric patients in a tertiary hospital, utilizing antimicrobial susceptibility testing, molecular typing (MLST and spa typing), and statistical analysis to identify risk factors and clinical outcomes.

full_output.key_findings: The study describes a bioinspired strategy for creating gelated cell sheet-supported lactobacillus biofilms (GCS-LBs) for the treatment of aerobic vaginitis. GCS-LBs demonstrate enhanced resistance to environmental stresses, including antibiotics and high temperatures, and show effective antimicrobial activity against pathogens such as E. coli, S. aureus, and C. albicans. Additionally, GCS-LBs exhibit improved colonization capacity in the vaginal environment compared to conventional probiotic formulations.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the preparation and characterization of GCS-LBs using human vaginal epithelial cells and Lactobacillus acidophilus. The biofilms were tested for their resistance to environmental stresses, antimicrobial activity, and colonization capacity in a mouse model of vaginitis.

full_output.paper_title: Optogenetic patterning generates multi-strain biofilms with spatially distributed antibiotic resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that beta-lactamase-producing cells can protect neighboring susceptible cells from ampicillin in a spatially dependent manner within biofilms.
full_output.methodology: Optogenetic patterning and biophysical modeling were used to engineer and analyze biofilm communities.

full_output.paper_title: Limonene encapsulated alginate/collagen as antibiofilm drug against Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the OmpA and Bap biofilm genes in Acinetobacter baumannii and demonstrates that limonene and LAC nanoparticles significantly reduce their transcription, suggesting potential anti-biofilm activity.
full_output.methodology: qRT-PCR, MIC testing, and nanoparticle synthesis.

full_output.paper_title: In-vitro and In-silico evaluation of antimicrobial and antibiofilm effect of Neem oil and Calcium hydroxide nanoparticles against Mutans Streptococci and Enterococcus faecalis isolated from endodontic infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the antimicrobial and antibiofilm effects of Neem oil and Calcium hydroxide nanoparticles against Mutans Streptococci and Enterococcus faecalis. Neem oil and its nanoparticles showed significant antibacterial and antibiofilm activity, particularly at lower concentrations. Calcium hydroxide nanoparticles exhibited improved antimicrobial effects compared to conventional Calcium hydroxide. Molecular docking revealed that Neem compounds like Sitosterol, Gedunin, and Nimbin interacted strongly with surface proteins of Streptococcus mutans.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial efficacy was assessed using disc diffusion and biofilm formation assays. Molecular docking was employed to analyze interactions between Neem compounds and Streptococcus mutans proteins.

full_output.paper_title: Haematological Profile and Antibiotic Resistance of Bacteria Responsible for Enteric Infections Isolated From Patients Suffering From Malaria and Enteric Infections on Consultation at the Dschang Regional Hospital.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified Escherichia coli as a major pathogen with high resistance to amoxicillin (AMX), clindamycin (CDA), amikacin (AKI), and erythromycin (ERY) in patients with malaria and enteric infections.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing using agar diffusion and microdilution methods.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic and phenotypic characterization of a Clostridioides difficile strain of the epidemic ST37 type from China.
