full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, ELISA, and mouse model experiments were used to characterize the strain's genomic features, toxin production, and pathogenicity.

full_output.paper_title: Longitudinal genomic surveillance of a UK intensive care unit shows a lack of patient colonisation by multi-drug-resistant Gram-negative bacterial pathogens.
full_output.key_findings: The study found a lack of multi-drug resistance in the QEHB ICU, with only one carbapenemase-producing organism, a Citrobacter carrying bla KPC-2, isolated. No evidence of nosocomial acquisition or circulation of colonising E. coli was found.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome and metagenomic sequencing were used to detect and report strain-level colonisation of patients, focusing on E. coli sequence types (STs), their colonisation dynamics and antimicrobial resistance gene carriage.

full_output.paper_title: Personalized CZA-ATM dosing against an XDR E. coli in liver transplant patients; the application of the in vitro hollow fiber system.
full_output.key_findings: The study utilized the hollow fiber system (HFS) to evaluate the effectiveness of ceftazidime-avibactam (CZA) and aztreonam (ATM) against an XDR E. coli isolate, demonstrating the necessity of multiple infusions for bacterial clearance.
full_output.methodology: The hollow fiber system was used to simulate in vivo antibiotic concentrations and assess bacterial killing dynamics.

full_output.paper_title: Reassessing the substrate specificities of the major Staphylococcus aureus peptidoglycan hydrolases lysostaphin and LytM.
full_output.key_findings: The study redefines the substrate specificities of lysostaphin (LSS) and LytM, revealing that they preferentially hydrolyze the D-Ala-Gly cross-link in peptidoglycan, with LytM additionally acting as a D-alanyl-glycine hydrolase.
full_output.methodology: Used NMR spectroscopy and turbidity reduction assays to analyze substrate specificities and hydrolysis rates of LSS and LytM.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of carbapenemases in Enterobacterales and other Gram-negative bacilli recovered from hospital and municipal wastewater in Mexico City.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several carbapenemase genes, including bla KPC, bla NDM, bla VIM−2, bla OXA−48, bla NDM−1, and bla NDM−5, in various Gram-negative bacteria from hospital and municipal wastewater in Mexico City.
full_output.methodology: PCR and sequencing were used to detect and characterize beta-lactamase genes in isolates from wastewater samples.

full_output.paper_title: Mycobacterium tuberculosis evolution from monoresistance to pre-extensive drug resistance during a prolonged household outbreak.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified mutations in katG, rpoB, embB, pncA, and gyrA genes that contributed to the evolution of Mycobacterium tuberculosis from isoniazid monoresistance to pre-extensive drug resistance during a prolonged household outbreak.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing (WGS) was used to analyze the evolution of drug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis strains.

full_output.paper_title: Systematic Review of the Role of the Ubiquitin-Proteasome System in Artemisinin Resistance in Malaria Parasites
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in pfk13 and rpn2 that contribute to artemisinin resistance and proteasome inhibitor resistance in malaria parasites.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed mutations in the ubiquitin-proteasome system and their impact on artemisinin and proteasome inhibitor resistance through susceptibility testing of transformed parasites.

full_output.paper_title: In silico evaluation of eugenol derivatives as antibacterial agents targeting DNA gyrase
full_output.key_findings: The study focuses on the computational design of eugenol derivatives targeting DNA gyrase, identifying compounds with improved binding affinity. While no AMR genes or mutations were experimentally validated in this paper, the research highlights the potential of eugenol derivatives as antibacterial agents by analyzing their interactions with DNA gyrase.
full_output.methodology: Computational molecular docking simulations, physicochemical property analysis, and toxicity assessment were used to evaluate eugenol derivatives and their binding affinity to DNA gyrase.

full_output.paper_title: Metagenome mining divulges virulent and multidrug resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa ST242 and Klebsiella michiganensis ST∗1b23 coinfecting an 8-month-old meningitis infant under ICU in Kampala, Uganda, East Africa.

full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis using Kleborate and ResFinder, along with mutation analysis from ResFinder.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic diversity of Campylobacter jejuni and Campylobacter coli isolates recovered from human and poultry in Australia and New Zealand, 2017 to 2019.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes and mutations in Campylobacter jejuni and Campylobacter coli isolates from Australia and New Zealand, including blaOXA-193, blaOXA-61, tet(O), erm(B), and lnu(C), as well as the blaOXA-61 G57T mutation. These genes and mutations were associated with resistance to various antibiotics, highlighting the importance of continued AMR surveillance.
full_output.methodology: Genomic screening using AMRFinderPlus and Abricate, along with analysis of mutations in housekeeping genes.

full_output.paper_title: A scientific research training programme for teaching biomedical students to identify the horizontal transfer of antibiotic resistance genes.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrated that students could identify the antibiotic resistance integrative and conjugative element (ICE) Sma M1 from the Stenotrophomonas maltophilia MER1 genome and visualize the horizontal transfer of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) from S. maltophilia MER1 to E. coli 25DN through conjugation and PCR assays.
full_output.methodology: Students identified the ICE Sma M1 using bioinformatics tools, performed conjugation assays, and verified the transfer of ARGs through PCR.

full_output.paper_title: Highly resistant Salmonella Heidelberg circulating in broiler farms in southern Brazil.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high levels of antimicrobial resistance in Salmonella Heidelberg isolates from broiler farms in southern Brazil, with 98% classified as multidrug-resistant. Key resistance genes detected include bla TEM, sul2, tet(A), strB, cmlA, and tet(B).
full_output.methodology: The study used phenotypic antimicrobial susceptibility testing and molecular detection of resistance genes via PCR.

full_output.paper_title: In silico discovery of druggable targets in Citrobacter koseri using echinoderm metabolites and molecular dynamics simulation.
full_output.key_findings: Two druggable proteins, WP_012000829.1 and WP_275157394.1, were identified as potential targets for Citrobacter koseri using in silico approaches. These proteins showed high binding affinities with echinoderm metabolites, suggesting their potential as therapeutic targets.
full_output.methodology: Computational methods including ORF prediction, sequence analysis, virtual screening, molecular docking, and MD simulations were used to identify and validate potential drug targets in Citrobacter koseri.

full_output.paper_title: Pyoverdine-antibiotic combination treatment: its efficacy and effects on resistance evolution in Escherichia coli.

full_output.paper_title: Bioenergetic suppression by redox-active metabolites promotes antibiotic tolerance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that redox-active metabolites (RAMs) such as pyocyanin (PYO), phenazine-1-carboxylic acid (PCA), phenazine-1-carboxyamide (PCN), and toxoflavin (TOX) lower the membrane potential (ΔΨ), proton pumping efficiency, and ATP levels in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, leading to increased tolerance to antibiotics like tobramycin, gentamicin, and ciprofloxacin.
full_output.methodology: The study used a combination of biochemical assays, flow cytometry, and microbiological techniques to assess the effects of RAMs on the bioenergetic state and antibiotic tolerance of P. aeruginosa.

full_output.paper_title: Design of a Biocatalytic Heterojunction for Treating Inflammatory Mandible Defects
full_output.key_findings: The study introduces Ru-Cu/EDHJ, a biocatalytic heterojunction with enhanced antioxidase-like activities and pH-controlled antibacterial properties, showing effectiveness in reducing ROS and eradicating bacterial biofilms.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis and characterization of biocatalytic heterojunctions, evaluation of antioxidase-like and antibacterial activities, and in vivo testing for bone regeneration.

full_output.paper_title: Public health concern of antimicrobial resistance and virulence determinants in E. coli isolates from oysters in Egypt.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple AMR genes in E. coli isolates from oysters in Egypt, including bla TEM, bla CTX-M, bla SHV, bla OXA-1, bla CMY-2, bla KPC, bla NDM, bla OXA-48, and bla VIM, as well as virulence genes such as papC, sfa, exhA, eaeA, and estA.
full_output.methodology: PCR and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify AMR and virulence genes in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis and biological evaluation of novel aminoguanidine derivatives as potential antibacterial agents.
full_output.key_findings: The study presents novel aminoguanidine derivatives with strong in vitro antibacterial activity against various bacterial strains, including multidrug-resistant ones. Compound 5f showed potent activity with MIC values ranging from 2-8 µg/mL against S. aureus, E. coli, S. epidermidis, B. subtilis, C. albicans, and multidrug-resistant strains. The compound also demonstrated low toxicity and mechanisms involving membrane permeabilization.
full_output.methodology: The compounds were synthesized and evaluated for antibacterial activity using MIC assays, disc diffusion, and membrane permeability studies. TEM was used to observe cellular effects.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial and biodegradable hydrogel based on nanocellulose/alginate incorporated with silver nanoparticles as active packaging for poultry products.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the development of an antimicrobial hydrogel composed of nanocellulose, alginate, and silver nanoparticles (AgH) for use in poultry product packaging. The hydrogel exhibited strong antimicrobial activity against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, effectively inhibiting bacterial growth. The optimal silver nanoparticle concentration was identified as 0.0156 phr, which maintained high cell viability (82%) in Caco-2 cells and prolonged the shelf life of chicken meat. The hydrogel was also biodegradable, degrading completely within 15-30 days in organic soil.
full_output.methodology: The study characterized the physicochemical properties, antimicrobial activity, cytotoxicity, and biodegradability of the nanocellulose/alginate hydrogels incorporating silver nanoparticles through various analytical techniques including SEM, XRD, TGA, rheology, and antimicrobial assays.

full_output.paper_title: Metabolic profiling unveils enhanced antibacterial synergy of polymyxin B and teixobactin against multi-drug resistant Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.key_findings: The study reveals that the combination of polymyxin B and Leu 10 -teixobactin exhibits strong synergistic antibacterial activity against both polymyxin-susceptible and -resistant A. baumannii strains, targeting multiple metabolic pathways including cell envelope biogenesis and cellular respiration.
full_output.methodology: The study used metabolomics, time-kill assays, peptidoglycan assays, and electron microscopy to analyze the synergistic effects of polymyxin B and Leu 10 -teixobactin against A. baumannii.

full_output.paper_title: Epidemiological and molecular characteristics of carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae from pediatric patients in Henan, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaKPC, blaNDM, and blaIMP as the major carbapenemase genes in carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKP) isolates from pediatric patients in Henan, China. blaKPC was the most prevalent, followed by blaNDM and blaIMP. Some isolates co-harbored multiple carbapenemase genes.
full_output.methodology: Multiplex PCR and MLST were used to identify carbapenemase genes and sequence types in CRKP isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Copper Sulfide Nanorod-Embedded Urinary Catheter with Hydrophobicity and Photothermal Sterilization.

Their structural and optical properties were characterized using SEM, TEM, XRD, Raman, and UV-Vis-NIR spectroscopy. full_output.paper_title: In vitro antimicrobial and antioxidant activities of bioactive compounds extracted from Streptomyces africanus strain E2 isolated from Moroccan soil.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified Streptomyces sp. strain E2 as a source of bioactive compounds with antimicrobial and antioxidant activities. full_output.methodology: The study involved isolation of Actinobacteria from soil samples, antimicrobial activity testing using disk diffusion and MIC assays, and characterization of bioactive compounds via GC-MS and HPLC analyses.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Characterization of Pseudomonas aeruginosa Clinical Isolates Through Whole-Genome Sequencing: A Comprehensive Analysis of Biotypes, Sequence Types, and Antimicrobial and Virulence Genes.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antibiotic resistance genes in Pseudomonas aeruginosa clinical isolates, including bla PDC, bla OXA, and bla VIM, which confer resistance to beta-lactams, as well as aac(6')-Il, aadA10, aph, and others that confer resistance to aminoglycosides. full_output.paper_title: Emergence of hypervirulent and carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae from 2014 - 2021 in Central and Eastern China: a molecular, biological, and epidemiological study.

full_output.paper_title: Assessing the propensity of TB clinical isolates to form viable but non-replicating subpopulations.

Rv2756c.evidence_note: The paper mentions 'Rv2756c O33298 hsdM L306P 540 site-specific DNA-methyltransferase' in the context of non-synonymous variants in failed/recurrent clinical isolates.

Rv3113.evidence_note: The paper mentions that the gene Rv3113 has a non-synonymous variant G134E in failed/recurrent clinical isolates.

Rv2438c.evidence_note: The paper mentions that the Rv2438c gene (nadE) has a non-synonymous variant L225R in the failed/recurrent clinical isolate S43dx, and that NadE is essential for persistence.

mutations_found.effect_on_function: Anaerobic nitrate reduction is required for persistence of M. bovis BCG in the lungs, liver, and kidneys

Rv0126.evidence_note: The paper identifies a non-synonymous variant in Rv0126 (E252Q) in failed/recurrent clinical isolates, which is associated with trehalose synthase/amylase function and may contribute to persistence.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies non-synonymous genomic variants in clinical isolates from individuals with unsuccessful TB treatment outcomes, which may contribute to the formation of viable but non-replicating (VBNR) subpopulations of M. tuberculosis. These variants are not present in isolates from cured cases.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and phenotypic drug susceptibility testing were used to analyze the genetic and resistance profiles of M. tuberculosis isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Synthetic indole derivatives as an antibacterial agent inhibiting respiratory metabolism of multidrug-resistant gram-positive bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified SMJ-2 and SMJ-4 as synthetic indole derivatives with potent antibacterial activity against multidrug-resistant gram-positive bacteria. These compounds inhibit respiratory metabolism and disrupt membrane potential, leading to bacterial cell death. SMJ-2 showed low resistance development and effective biofilm eradication.
full_output.methodology: The study used in vitro and in vivo experiments, including MIC determination, time-kill assays, biofilm assays, and transcriptomic analysis to evaluate the antibacterial activity and mechanisms of SMJ-2 and SMJ-4.

full_output.paper_title: Overexpression of outer membrane protein A (OmpA) increases aminoglycoside sensitivity in mycobacteria.
full_output.key_findings: Overexpression of OmpA increases aminoglycoside sensitivity in mycobacteria, indicating that OmpA acts as a porin facilitating the uptake of hydrophilic antibiotics like streptomycin, amikacin, and gentamicin.
full_output.methodology: Construction of OmpA-overexpressing strains, MIC determination, plate assays, macrophage infection assays, and ethidium bromide/nile red uptake experiments.

full_output.key_findings: The study found that hops bitter β-acids, lupulone and colupulone, exhibit antibacterial effects against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) but do not inhibit Pseudomonas aeruginosa. These compounds also induce ciliotoxicity and mitochondrial dysfunction in sinonasal epithelial cells.
full_output.methodology: The study used human nasal primary cells (HNECs) and RPMI2650 cell cultures to evaluate the antibacterial effects and cellular impacts of lupulone and colupulone.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of a Novel Sequence Type (ST) 6758 Klebsiella Pneumoniae and the Role of IncX3 Plasmid in the Transmission of bla (NDM).
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel sequence type ST6758 of Klebsiella pneumoniae carrying the bla NDM-1 gene on an IncX3-type plasmid, highlighting the role of this plasmid in the transmission of carbapenem resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize the strain and its resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotics-encapsulated nanoparticles as an antimicrobial agent in the treatment of wound infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the efficacy of antibiotic-loaded solid lipid nanoparticles (SLNs) in treating wound infections caused by Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Staphylococcus aureus. The results showed that the nanoparticles effectively reduced bacterial load and promoted wound healing.
full_output.methodology: The study used the double emulsion method to synthesize nanoparticles and evaluated their antimicrobial activity through well diffusion and MIC assays.
full_output.sample_size: Male rats aged 6 to 8 weeks were used in the study.

full_output.paper_title: Development and preliminary assessment of the iFIND TBR: all-in- one molecular diagnostic assay for rapid detection of Mycobacterium tuberculosis and rifampicin resistance.

rpoB.validation_method: fluorescent probes and melting Tm peak shifts

full_output.key_findings: The iFIND TBR assay effectively detects Mycobacterium tuberculosis and rifampicin resistance by targeting the rpoB gene, showing high sensitivity and specificity.
full_output.methodology: The iFIND TBR assay uses fluorescent probes and melting curve analysis to detect rpoB gene mutations associated with rifampicin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Catalase activity deficiency sensitizes multidrug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis to the ATP synthase inhibitor bedaquiline.
full_output.key_findings: Deficiency in catalase activity, particularly due to katG mutations, increases the susceptibility of multidrug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis to bedaquiline.
full_output.methodology: Growth inhibition dose-response experiments, RNA sequencing, and ELISA-based assays were used to evaluate the effects of catalase activity deficiency on bedaquiline susceptibility.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial, antioxidant, anti-aging, and anti-hyperpigmentation activities of volatile components from Melaleuca rugulosa leaves
full_output.key_findings: The study identified 1,8-cineol, dl-alpha-tocopherol, and alpha-terpineol as having antimicrobial activity against Staphylococcus aureus and Clostridium perfringens. These compounds showed promising results in suppressing the growth of skin-related microbial strains.
full_output.methodology: The antimicrobial activity of the volatile components was evaluated using agar well diffusion assay and broth microdilution assay.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified bioactive compounds from Bacillus gottheilii MSB1 that show antifungal, antibacterial, and nematicidal activities against plant pathogens such as Alternaria alternata, Fusarium oxysporum, and Meloidogyne incognita.
full_output.methodology: The study involved isolation and characterization of Bacillus gottheilii MSB1 from a marine sponge, extraction of bioactive compounds, and evaluation of their antimicrobial and nematicidal activities using in vitro assays.

full_output.key_findings: The paper discusses the development of a MALDI-TOF-based antimicrobial resistance (AMR) recommender system using dual-branch neural networks. It highlights the effectiveness of species-specific models and the importance of drug embeddings in improving AMR prediction accuracy.
full_output.methodology: The study employs dual-branch neural networks, utilizing various drug embedding techniques such as Morgan fingerprints, SMILES strings, and 1D/2D CNNs, alongside spectrum embeddings for AMR prediction.

full_output.paper_title: Effects of sulfamethoxazole and copper on the natural microbial community from a fertilized soil.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of sul1 and sul2 genes in the soil microbial community, which confer resistance to sulfamethoxazole. The presence of copper was found to increase the persistence of these resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: The study used qPCR to quantify the abundance of sul1 and sul2 genes in soil samples, along with other microbiological and chemical analyses.

full_output.paper_title: Rationally designed pooled CRISPRi-seq uncovers an inhibitor of bacterial peptidyl-tRNA hydrolase.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies peptidyl-tRNA hydrolase (Pth) as a target of PHAR(A), a novel growth inhibitory compound. It also reveals that PHAR(A) affects translation-related genes such as rpsA, mnmA, pepP, and waaA.
full_output.methodology: CRISPRi-Seq and biochemical assays were used to identify the mechanism of action of PHAR(A) and validate the targets.

full_output.paper_title: Biofilm targeting with chitosan-based nanohydrogel containing Quercus infectoria G. Olivier extract against Streptococcus mutans: new formulations of a traditional natural product.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the effectiveness of chitosan-based nanohydrogels containing Quercus infectoria extract (QI-NH) and tannic acid (TA-NH) against Streptococcus mutans. Both formulations showed strong antibacterial and anti-biofilm activities, with TA-NH exhibiting the lowest MIC. The expressions of gtf B, gtf C, gtf D, and gbp B genes involved in biofilm formation were significantly reduced by QI-NH and TA-NH.
full_output.methodology: The study used HPLC, SEM, FTIR, DLS, zeta potential, MIC/MBC, anti-biofilm assays, and real-time PCR to analyze the properties and efficacy of the nanohydrogels.

full_output.paper_title: Population Pharmacokinetic/Pharmacodynamic Study of Linezolid in Hospital-Acquired Pneumonia Patients with Renal Insufficiency.
full_output.key_findings: The study compared linezolid and teicoplanin in HAP patients with renal insufficiency, finding linezolid had higher bacterial eradication rates but more adverse reactions. Optimal dosing regimens for linezolid were proposed based on renal function.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective study with pharmacokinetic analysis and Monte Carlo simulations.

full_output.paper_title: A case of penicillin-resistant group B Streptococcus isolated from a patient in the UK.

pbp2x.evidence_note: The paper describes mutations in pbp2x that confer resistance to penicillin in a Streptococcus agalactiae isolate.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several non-synonymous mutations in penicillin-binding protein genes (pbp1a, pbp2a, pbp2b, and pbp2x) in a penicillin-resistant group B Streptococcus (PRGBS) isolate from the UK, which are likely responsible for the observed resistance to penicillin.
full_output.methodology: Genomic sequencing and analysis of the PRGBS isolate, along with comparisons to reference strains and other PRGBS isolates, were conducted to identify mutations associated with penicillin resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Mutant prevention concentrations, in vitro resistance evolution dynamics, and mechanisms of resistance to imipenem and imipenem/relebactam in carbapenem-susceptible Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates showing ceftazidime/avibactam resistance.

blaKPC-31.mechanism: D179Y substitution in the Omega loop enhances resistance to ceftazidime/avibactam and carbapenems.

blaKPC-3 D179N.evidence_note: The D179N substitution was identified in the KPC-31 enzyme in the ST512/KPC-31 isolate.

blaKPC-35.mechanism: L169P substitution in the Omega loop enhances resistance to ceftazidime/avibactam and carbapenems.

mutations_found.position_in_molecule: loop three di-amino acid insertion GD

ompK36.notes: Disruption of OmpK36 plays a prominent role in resistance to imipenem and imipenem/relebactam.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several KPC variants, including KPC-31, KPC-3, KPC-3 D179N, KPC-35, KPC-2, KPC-2 L169A, and KPC-2 L169T, which contribute to resistance to ceftazidime/avibactam. Additionally, mutations in the outer membrane porin OmpK36 are associated with reduced internalization of carbapenems, contributing to resistance.
full_output.methodology: Cloning experiments, whole genome sequencing, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize the resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Resistance and Zoonotic Potential of Nontyphoidal Salmonella From Household Dogs.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified 55 different antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs) in dog-associated Salmonella strains and 53 in human-associated isolates, highlighting the presence of AMR determinants in NTS from both sources.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) was used to analyze NTS isolates from dogs and humans, identifying AMR genes and conducting phylogenetic analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Cryo-EM characterization of the anydromuropeptide permease AmpG central to bacterial fitness and β-lactam antibiotic resistance.

AmpG.notes: Mutants K62A, Y152A, K66A, Y159A, and D74N showed decreased resistance to cefoxitin.

ampG.notes: mutations in ampG affect cefuroxime resistance

full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the structure and function of AmpG, a permease involved in transporting peptidoglycan fragments, and identifies key residues (K62, Y152, K66, Y159, and D74) critical for its activity and substrate binding.
full_output.methodology: Cryo-EM, mutagenesis, and β-lactam susceptibility assays were used to analyze AmpG's structure and function.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic characterisation of an extended-spectrum β-Lactamase-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae isolate assigned to a novel sequence type (6914).
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the genomic characterization of an extended-spectrum β-Lactamase-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae isolate, Cow102, which exhibits multidrug resistance. It identifies several resistance genes, including blaSHV-1, blaSHV-11, blaSHV-13, blaSHV-26, blaSHV-70, blaSHV-78, blaSHV-98, blaSHV-145, blaTEM-1B, aadA2, catA2, catII, dfrA16, fosA, oqxA, oqxB, sul1, sul2, and tet(D).
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were performed to identify resistance genes and their associated resistance profiles.

full_output.paper_title: LysSYL-Loaded pH-Switchable Self-Assembling Peptide Hydrogels Promote Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus Aureus Elimination and Wound Healing.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes LysSYL, an endolysin that exhibits antimicrobial activity against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) under acidic conditions. LysSYL-loaded pH-switchable hydrogels (L5@LysSYL) show effective elimination of MRSA through membrane disruption and cell separation inhibition, along with promoting wound healing.
full_output.methodology: Peptide design, synthesis, and screening for pH-switchable antimicrobial activity, followed by assessment of antimicrobial efficacy and wound healing promotion in a mouse model.

full_output.paper_title: Endolysins as Alternatives to Antibiotics in the Treatment of Bovine Mastitis and Food Safety Applications
full_output.key_findings: The paper highlights the effectiveness of endolysins as alternatives to antibiotics in treating bovine mastitis and foodborne pathogens, demonstrating their lytic activity against various staphylococcal strains and their potential in food preservation and diagnostics.
full_output.methodology: Experimental validation of endolysins through in vitro and in vivo testing, biosensor development, and lytic activity assessment.

full_output.paper_title: The antibacterial activity of a prophage-encoded fitness factor is neutralized by two cognate immunity proteins.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies BAH as an ARH1-like immunity protein and Bsi as a non-enzymatic immunity protein that neutralizes the antibacterial activity of Bxa, an ADP-ribosyltransferase. These immunity proteins protect B. stercoris from self-intoxication caused by Bxa.
full_output.methodology: Expression in E. coli, co-purification, mutagenesis, and immunoblotting were used to characterize BAH and Bsi.

full_output.paper_title: Phylogenetic analysis of Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates of respiratory tract infections in humans and sheep.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from human and sheep respiratory tract infections and found significant genetic similarities between the isolates, indicating potential transmission between species. The isolates exhibited varying levels of antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used biochemical tests, VITEK-2 analysis, antibiotic susceptibility testing, and molecular techniques including PCR and phylogenetic analysis to characterize K. pneumoniae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Collateral susceptibility-guided alternation of ceftolozane/tazobactam with imipenem prevents resistance development in XDR Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilms.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in the Omega loop of AmpC that confer resistance to ceftolozane/tazobactam and collateral susceptibility to imipenem, demonstrating that alternating ceftolozane/tazobactam with imipenem prevents the selection of resistant mutants in XDR Pseudomonas aeruginosa biofilms.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize ceftolozane/tazobactam resistant mutants.

full_output.paper_title: Pooled prevalence of Escherichia coli phenotypic and genotypic antimicrobial resistance profiles in poultry: systematic review and meta-analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple antimicrobial resistance genes in Escherichia coli from poultry, highlighting high prevalence of resistance to tetracyclines, quinolones, and beta-lactams.
full_output.methodology: Systematic review and meta-analysis of published studies on antimicrobial resistance in poultry-associated Escherichia coli.

full_output.paper_title: G-CSF resistance of ELANE-mutant neutropenia depends on SERF1-containing truncated-neutrophil elastase aggregates.

SERF1.mechanism: interacts with cytoplasmic NE of mutant neutrophil precursors
SERF1.validation_method: downregulation of SERF1 enhanced survival and differentiation of iPSC-derived neutrophil precursors

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies SERF1 as a critical factor in G-CSF resistance of ELANE-mutant neutropenia, showing that its downregulation restores G-CSF sensitivity and reduces aggrephagy-induced cell death.
full_output.methodology: Gene editing, iPSC differentiation, immunoblotting, flow cytometry, and confocal microscopy were used to analyze the role of SERF1 in ELANE-mutant neutropenia.

full_output.paper_title: Antisense transcription is associated with expression of metal resistance determinants in Cupriavidus metallidurans CH34.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several metal resistance genes in Cupriavidus metallidurans CH34, including merA, merT, arsC2, arsC1, arsB, arsR, czcC2, tauD, atoD, czcC, copF, copD, copC, copB, copA, copR, copS, cupR, cupA, cupC, silC, silB, silA, gshA, and gshB, which are up-regulated under metal stress conditions and are associated with antisense transcription activities.
full_output.methodology: RNA sequencing and RT-PCR were used to analyze the transcriptome of Cupriavidus metallidurans CH34 and its plasmid-free derivative AE104 under various metal stress conditions.

full_output.paper_title: Metagenomic analysis reveals houseflies as indicators for monitoring environmental antibiotic resistance genes.

mecA.mechanism: penicillin-binding protein alteration

full_output.key_findings: Houseflies were found to carry a variety of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs), including multidrug, beta-lactam, bacitracin, and tetracycline resistance genes. The study highlights the potential of houseflies as indicators for monitoring environmental ARGs.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to characterize ARGs on housefly body surfaces.

blaNDM.validation_method: PCR detection of carbapenem resistance genes

full_output.methodology: VITEK-2 system for antibiotic susceptibility testing, multiplex PCR for detection of carbapenem-resistant genes, and ERIC-PCR for genetic diversity analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Selenocompounds as Potent Efflux Pump Inhibitors on Gram-positive Bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several selenoester derivatives that act as efflux pump inhibitors, specifically targeting the NorA efflux pump in Staphylococcus aureus. These compounds showed significant inhibition of biofilm formation and enhanced the efficacy of antibiotics like ciprofloxacin and tetracycline.
full_output.methodology: Antibacterial activity was determined using MIC assays, efflux pump inhibition was assessed via real-time ethidium bromide accumulation assay, and biofilm formation was evaluated using crystal violet staining.

full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing of resistant mutants and MIC assays.

full_output.paper_title: Whole genome sequencing revealed high proportions of ST152 MRSA among clinical Staphylococcus aureus isolates from ten hospitals in Ghana.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high proportions of ST152 MRSA among clinical S. aureus isolates in Ghana, with blaZ, mecA, cat, tetK, and dfrG being the most prevalent resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing was used to analyze the genetic diversity, antimicrobial resistance, and virulence genes of S. aureus isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic epidemiology and phenotypic characterisation of Salmonella enterica serovar Panama in Victoria, Australia.

mphA.evidence_note: The paper mentions that the mphA gene was detected in an invasive isolate (AUSMDU00067711) and is associated with macrolide resistance.

mcr-1.1.genetic_context: plasmid-mediated colistin resistance gene, mcr1 . 1 , was detected in one Australian S . Panama isolate, carried by an IncI plasmid previously reported in Salmonella and Escherichia coli isolates collected from poultry in South-East Asia
mcr-1.1.evidence_note: The plasmid sequence of AUSMDU00067711 was screened against the NCBI database (nt) with blastn ( https://blast.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/Blast.cgi ). The top four hits were selected ( AP018355.1 , OM038692.1 , MN232197.1 and KU934209.1 ) which all had >99% query coverage and >90% identity. MN232197.1 was annotated for this study using Bakta v.1.6.1 [ 49 ]. To visualise the comparison of the identity of mcr-1 . 1 gene containing IncI2 plasmid from AUSMDU00067711 to public reference plasmids Blast Ring Image Generator (BRIG) v0.95 was used [ 52 ].

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the first plasmid-mediated colistin-resistant Salmonella enterica serovar Panama in Australia, highlighting the emergence of multidrug resistance in this invasive non-typhoidal Salmonella serovar.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, plasmid analysis, and in vitro infection experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Effect of Moringa oleifera seeds on the removal of pathogens and pharmaceutical residues in a domestic wastewater treatment plant by an interdisciplinary approach.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that Moringa oleifera seeds (MOS) effectively reduced the abundance of antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) such as bla CTX-M, bla SHV, and bla TEM in wastewater. MOS treatment significantly decreased the copy numbers of these genes, indicating potential for mitigating antibiotic resistance in wastewater treatment.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized qPCR to quantify the abundance of ARGs in wastewater samples before and after treatment with Moringa oleifera seeds.

full_output.paper_title: Bio-computational modeling, POM analysis and molecular dynamic simulation for novel synthetic quinolone and benzo[d][1,3]oxazine candidates as antimicrobial inhibitors.
full_output.key_findings: The study focuses on the synthesis and evaluation of novel quinolone and benzo[d][1,3]oxazine compounds as antimicrobial agents, highlighting their potential as inhibitors of carbonic anhydrase XII with minimal toxicity.
full_output.methodology: The paper describes the synthesis of quinolone and benzo[d][1,3]oxazine compounds, followed by molecular docking, POM analysis, and molecular dynamics simulations to evaluate their antimicrobial activity and drug-like properties.

full_output.paper_title: Increased Severity of Multidrug-Resistant Shigella sonnei Infections in People Experiencing Homelessness.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a clonal expansion of multidrug-resistant Shigella sonnei (genotype 3.6.1.1.2) with resistance to multiple antibiotics, including ampicillin, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, ciprofloxacin, and azithromycin.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to analyze the resistance mechanisms in Shigella sonnei isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Diclofenac sensitizes multi-drug resistant Acinetobacter baumannii to colistin.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that diclofenac enhances the susceptibility of colistin-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii to colistin, and identifies pmrC, pmrAB, and emrAB as genes involved in colistin resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used a combination of in vitro and in vivo experiments, including MIC assays, transcriptomic and proteomic analyses, and a murine pneumonia model.
full_output.sample_size: Multiple clinical isolates of Acinetobacter baumannii and other Gram-negative pathogens.

full_output.paper_title: Rapid Emergence of S. aureus Resistance to Silver Nanoparticles Upon Repeated Exposure
full_output.key_findings: Gram-positive Staphylococcus aureus and Gram-negative Escherichia coli develop resistance to silver nanoparticles through distinct mechanisms, with E. coli utilizing flagellin production and S. aureus relying on biofilm formation, both leading to nanoparticle aggregation and reduced antibacterial efficacy.
full_output.methodology: Synthesis and characterization of silver nanoparticles, evaluation of bacterial resistance through MIC testing, biofilm analysis using SEM and the Christensen method, and investigation of resistance mitigation strategies such as pomegranate rind extract and graphene-silver composites.

full_output.paper_title: Unveiling the biosynthesis mechanism of novel lantibiotic homicorcin: an in silico analysis.
full_output.key_findings: The study unveils the biosynthesis mechanism of the novel lantibiotic homicorcin, identifying eight genes involved in its sequential maturation, including structural, dehydratase, cyclase, protease, immunity, oxidoreductase, and transporter genes.
full_output.methodology: Computational modeling, protein-protein docking, and structural analysis were used to investigate the biosynthesis of homicorcin.

full_output.paper_title: Escherichia coli from six European countries reveals differences in profile and distribution of critical antimicrobial resistance determinants within One Health compartments, 2013 to 2020.

qnrS1.evidence_note: The paper states that "Acquired resistance mechanisms were relatively rare in human isolates in Norway, Spain and France (9/237, 10/110, 17/243, respectively; 3.8–9.1%), and were mostly due to presence of qnrS1" and "Resistance to ciprofloxacin in animal and meat isolates was due to qnrS1".

full_output.key_findings: The study identified various AMR genes in E. coli isolates from different sources in six European countries, highlighting differences in resistance profiles and the prevalence of specific resistance mechanisms such as beta-lactamases, quinolone resistance genes, and tetracycline resistance genes.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to detect and characterize AMR genes in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Optimized methods for the targeted surveillance of extended-spectrum beta-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli in human stool.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes the resistance mechanisms of ESBL-producing E. coli, focusing on the blaCTX-M-15, blaIMP, and blaCTX-M-27 genes, demonstrating their role in conferring resistance to various beta-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The study uses a combination of spiked stool models, selective agar plating, and sequencing to identify and characterize ESBL-producing E. coli strains.

full_output.paper_title: New Insights into the Mechanism of Action of L-681,217, a Medicinally Promising Polyketide Inhibitor of Bacterial Protein Translation.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes L-681,217, a polyketide inhibitor of bacterial protein translation targeting EF-Tu, and investigates its mechanism of action and resistance profiles.
full_output.methodology: The study uses biochemical assays, cell-free protein synthesis, and structural analysis to investigate the mechanism of L-681,217.

full_output.paper_title: Whole genome sequencing-based characterization and determination of quinolone resistance among methicillin-resistant and methicillin-susceptible S. Aureus isolates from patients attending regional referral hospitals in Tanzania.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various AMR genes and mutations associated with quinolone resistance in S. aureus isolates from Tanzania, highlighting the prevalence of resistance mechanisms such as blaZ, dfrG, aac(6')-aph(2''), mecA, ermC, and tet(K), along with specific mutations in grlA and gyrA genes.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to identify AMR genes and mutations in S. aureus isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Fecal carriage of extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing, and carbapenem-resistant gram-negative bacteria among hemodialysis patients in a palestinian tertiary care hospital.
full_output.key_findings: The study found a high prevalence of fecal carriage of extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing (ESBL)-Gram-negative bacteria (GNB) among hemodialysis patients, with 84.7% being colonized. Carbapenem-resistant (CR)-GNB colonization was less common, at 5.8%. Advanced age, hypertension, ischemic heart disease, morning dialysis shifts, and elevated blood urea nitrogen levels were significant risk factors for ESBL-GNB colonization.
full_output.methodology: Cross-sectional study analyzing stool samples from hemodialysis patients to detect ESBL-GNB and CR-GNB colonization using selective agar media.

full_output.key_findings: The study focuses on the development of amphiphilic Janus nanoparticles (SSK1@PDA/CaP@CIP) for the treatment of Pseudomonas aeruginosa pneumonia, highlighting their effectiveness in targeting infection sites, reducing inflammation, and eradicating biofilms and planktonic bacteria.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the synthesis and characterization of SSK1@PDA/CaP@CIP nanoparticles, evaluation of their antibacterial activity through MIC assays, live/dead assays, and SEM analysis, as well as assessment of biofilm eradication using crystal violet staining.

full_output.paper_title: Screening and identification of phytochemicals from Acorus calamus L. to overcome NDM-1 mediated resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae using in silico approach.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several phytochemicals from Acorus calamus L. that show potential to inhibit NDM-1, a metallo-beta-lactamase responsible for carbapenem resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.methodology: In silico molecular docking studies and GC-HRMS analysis were used to screen and identify phytochemicals targeting NDM-1.

full_output.paper_title: Evolution of copper resistance in Xanthomonas euvesicatoria pv. perforans population.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies chromosomal and plasmid-borne copper resistance (CuR) genes in Xanthomonas euvesicatoria pv. perforans, revealing that chromosomal CuR is widespread and exhibits variations across phylogenetic groups. Strains with both chromosomal and plasmid-borne CuR show increased copper tolerance.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis, plasmid prediction, and growth assays were conducted to characterize CuR mechanisms in Xanthomonas euvesicatoria pv. perforans.

full_output.paper_title: Florfenicol administration in piglets co-selects for multiple antimicrobial resistance genes.

full_output.key_findings: Florfenicol administration in piglets leads to the selection of multiple antimicrobial resistance genes, including those conferring resistance to phenicols, aminoglycosides, beta-lactams, sulfonamides, and oxazolidinones.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic sequencing, plasmid analysis, and MIC testing were used to identify and characterize antimicrobial resistance genes in florfenicol-treated and control piglets.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial and antioxidant activities of peptide derived from turmeric plant (Curcuma longa L).
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several peptides derived from turmeric hydrolysate, including Cur-1, Cur-14, and Cur-25, which exhibited potent antibacterial activity against various pathogenic bacteria such as Acinetobacter baumannii, Staphylococcus aureus, Staphylococcus epidermidis, and Salmonella enterica. These peptides also demonstrated antioxidant properties.
full_output.methodology: Peptides were isolated through chromatographic techniques and evaluated for antimicrobial and antioxidant activities using various assays.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of a depupylation regulator for an essential enzyme in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies CoaX, a pseudopantothenate kinase, as a regulator of depupylation of PanB, an essential enzyme in pantothenate synthesis in Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
full_output.methodology: Immunoprecipitation, mass spectrometry, in vitro depupylation assays, and cryo-electron microscopy.

full_output.paper_title: Mesoporous silica nanoparticles co-loaded with lysozyme and vancomycin for synergistic antimicrobial action.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs) co-loaded with lysozyme (Lys) and vancomycin (Van) to enhance antimicrobial efficacy against Staphylococcus aureus. The co-loaded formulation showed significant reductions in MIC values compared to free drugs, demonstrating synergistic antibacterial effects.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the antimicrobial activity of MSNs loaded with Lys and Van using MIC and MBC assays, and assessed the stability and release profiles of the drugs.

Relebactam showed the highest efficacy in reducing resistance, particularly when combined with ceftolozane.

full_output.methodology: Transcriptome analysis of venom glands, in silico homology analysis, and in vitro antimicrobial efficacy testing.

full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis, qPCR, and in silico methods were used to identify and evaluate the expression of TA systems in response to different stress conditions.

full_output.paper_title: High carriage and possible hidden spread of multidrug-resistant Salmonella among asymptomatic workers in Yulin, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several AMR genes, including qnrS, oqxA, aac(6')-Ib-cr, blaTEM, blaCTX-M, blaOXA, mcr-1, and mcr-9, in Salmonella isolates from asymptomatic workers in Yulin, China, highlighting the presence of multidrug-resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: Genomic sequencing and resistance profiling of Salmonella isolates from asymptomatic workers.

full_output.paper_title: Guardians of resistance and virulence: detection of mec, femA, Van, pvl, hlg and spa genes in methicillin and vancomycin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus from clinical and food samples in Southwestern Nigeria.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence and molecular characterization of ESBL-producing Escherichia coli isolated from broiler chicken and their respective farms environment in Malaysia.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Surfaces: Stainless Steel Functionalized with the Essential Oil Component Vanillin.

full_output.methodology: The study involved the functionalization of stainless steel surfaces with vanillin via a multi-step process, including surface activation, silica layer deposition, and vanillin derivative immobilization, followed by antimicrobial testing against S. epidermidis.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Characterization of Multidrug-Resistant and Hypervirulent New Delhi Metallo-Beta-Lactamase Klebsiella pneumoniae in Lazio, Italy: A Five-Year Retrospective Study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified blaNDM-1 and blaNDM-5 as the predominant resistance genes in NDM-Kpn isolates, highlighting their widespread distribution and association with high-risk clones.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and molecular typing techniques were used to analyze the resistance and virulence profiles of NDM-Kpn isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Verification of the Vitek Reveal System for Direct Antimicrobial Susceptibility Testing in Gram-Negative Positive Blood Cultures.
full_output.key_findings: The Vitek Reveal AST assay showed high essential agreement rates (96.1% for simulated and 98.8% for clinical GN-PBC samples) and categorical agreement rates (97.7% for simulated and 99.2% for clinical samples) when compared to the reference AST assay, demonstrating its effectiveness for rapid antimicrobial susceptibility testing in Gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.methodology: The study evaluated the Vitek Reveal AST assay against the reference broth microdilution method, comparing MIC results for various antibiotics against Gram-negative bacterial isolates from simulated and clinical positive blood cultures.

full_output.paper_title: Differential Host Gene Expression in Response to Infection by Different Mycobacterium tuberculosis Strains-A Pilot Study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified differences in host gene expression in response to infection with different Mycobacterium tuberculosis strains, particularly highlighting the overexpression of interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) in cells infected with the isoniazid-resistant strain. Key genes included IDO1 and IL-1β, which were upregulated in virulent strains compared to avirulent ones.
full_output.methodology: Gene expression profiling using microarrays in THP-1 cells infected with different M. tuberculosis strains.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic Insights on Meropenem Resistance Concerning Klebsiella pneumoniae Clinical Isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several AMR genes in Klebsiella pneumoniae clinical isolates, including bla KPC, bla OXA-48-like, bla NDM, bla SHV, bla CTX-M, aac(3)IIa, qnr B, and tet B, which confer resistance to carbapenems, beta-lactams, aminoglycosides, fluoroquinolones, and tetracyclines.
full_output.methodology: Molecular detection techniques such as PCR were used to identify AMR genes in K. pneumoniae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Is It Time to Start Worrying? A Comprehensive Report on the Three-Year Prevalence of ESBL-Producing Bacteria and Their Trends in Antibiotic Resistance from the Largest University Hospital in Slovakia.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the prevalence of ESBL-producing bacteria, highlighting the dominance of TEM, CTX-M, and SHV beta-lactamases, along with AGL AAC (6′)-I and AGL ANT (2′)-I aminoglycoside modifying enzymes in E. coli, P. mirabilis, and K. pneumoniae.
full_output.methodology: Susceptibility testing of 1599 ESBL-producing bacterial samples against 20 antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: Enhanced Antibacterial, Anti-Inflammatory, and Antibiofilm Activities of Tryptophan-Substituted Peptides Derived from Cecropin A-Melittin Hybrid Peptide BP100.
full_output.key_findings: The study reports the design and evaluation of tryptophan-substituted BP100 analogs, which show enhanced antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, and antibiofilm activities against multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa. These analogs demonstrate improved efficacy compared to the parent peptide BP100.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the synthesis of BP100 analogs, determination of their antibacterial activity via MIC assays, assessment of anti-inflammatory effects using ELISA, and evaluation of antibiofilm activity through crystal violet staining.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis and Antimicrobial Activity of 3-Alkylidene-2-Indolone Derivatives.
full_output.key_findings: The study synthesized and evaluated 32 3-alkylidene-2-indolone derivatives for antimicrobial activity, identifying compounds 10f, 10g, and 10h as having the highest antibacterial activity against Gram-positive bacteria with MIC values of 0.5 μg/mL. These compounds showed potential as antibacterial agents.

full_output.paper_title: Influence of Nisin Grafting on the Antibacterial Efficacy of AMP Self-Assembled Monolayers (SAMs).
full_output.key_findings: The study investigates the antibacterial efficacy of Nisin grafted onto gold surfaces via self-assembled monolayers (SAMs). Nisin showed bactericidal effects against Gram-positive bacteria but not against Gram-negative bacteria.
full_output.methodology: The study used FT-IR and XPS to characterize the grafting of Nisin on SAMs, and microbiological tests to assess antibacterial activity.

full_output.paper_title: Investigation of the Antimicrobial Resistance of Important Pathogens Isolated from Poultry from 2015 to 2023 in the United States.

rpsJ.evidence_note: An amino acid substitution mutation, V57L, in the ribosomal small subunit constitutive protein S10 encoding gene rpsJ has been identified in tigecycline resistant K. pneumoniae , which has been previously reported to relate to tetracycline resistance in Neisseria gonorrhoeae ( Villa et al., 2014 ). This mutation is located at the tip of a conserved flexible loop consisting of amino acids 53-60 in the S10 ribosomal protein and this region is near the tigecycline target site and is associated with the ribosome binding to tigecycline. The article postulated that the mutation in rpsJ affected tigecycline susceptibility by altering the ribosome structure near the tigecycline-binding site or interfering with the coordination of Mg 2+ ions, which resulted in reduced tigecycline binding to the 16S rRNA therefore reduced the tigecycline susceptibility. Mutations in rpsJ at V57 locus were identified in all resistant isolates through tigecycline resistance screening of E. coli , K. pneumoniae , and A. baumannii , as well as in another report about tigecycline resistant K. pneumoniae from clinical source and laboratory evolution ( Beabout et al., 2015 ; Fang et al., 2016 ). Other rpsJ mutations, predominantly V57L amino acid substitutions, have been documented in S. maltophilia , K. pneumoniae , E. coli , and A. baumannii with the mutations reducing tigecycline susceptibility by affecting the structure of ribosomal protein S10 ( Villa et al., 2014 ; Hammerstrom et al., 2015 ; Li et al., 2016a ; He et al., 2018 ; Blanco et al., 2019 ; Xu et al., 2020 ; Zhang et al., 2021a ).

The complementation of the wild-type plsC gene recovered the tigecycline MIC reduction, suggesting that plsC was related to decreased tigecycline susceptibility.'

They demonstrated that the abrp knockout resulted in reduced susceptibility to tigecycline and increased cell membrane permeability in the isolate, whereas complementation with wild-type abrp restored both susceptibility and cell membrane permeability.'

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies NAT2 genetic variants, specifically slow acetylator genotypes, as significantly associated with an increased risk of hepatotoxicity in tuberculosis patients treated with isoniazid (INH).
full_output.methodology: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 24 studies evaluating the association between NAT2 genotypes and INH-induced hepatotoxicity.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic insights on cgMLST markers, drug resistance, and urease cluster of Proteus mirabilis strains.

full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, plasmid construction, and MIC determination were used to analyze resistance mechanisms.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of a bla (NDM-5) Carrying IncHI2/IncHI2A Plasmid in a Multidrug Resistant Clinical ST1431 Escherichia coli Strain.

full_output.paper_title: Anticariogenic activity of marine brown algae Padina boergesenii and its active components towards Streptococcus mutans.

MEPB reduced the expression of virulence-related genes such as gtfB, gtfC, gtfD, vicR, gbpB, and gbpC, indicating its potential as an anticariogenic agent.

full_output.paper_title: Adaptive evolution of extensive drug resistance and persistence in epidemic ST11 KPC-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae during antimicrobial chemotherapy.

blaKPC-179.validation_method: cloning and expression in E. coli

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the integration of IS Kpn26 into the mgrB gene, leading to mgrB inactivation and colistin resistance, as well as novel bla KPC-2 variants (bla KPC-71 and bla KPC-179 ) that confer resistance to ceftazidime/avibactam in KPC-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae.

full_output.paper_title: Microbial community structure and functional traits involved in the adaptation of culturable bacteria within the gut of amphipods from the deepest ocean.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antibiotic resistance genes in Pediococcus pentosaceus XY62, including bla, aac(6')-Ib, tet(M), qnrS1, erm(B), mef(A), mph(A), lnu(D), lsa(E), vat(D), vgb, sul2, and dfrA12, which confer resistance to various antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The study used 16S rRNA sequencing, genome sequencing, and functional assays to identify and characterize antibiotic resistance genes in Pediococcus pentosaceus XY62.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of the double-zone hemolysis (DZH) test for the detection of livestock-associated methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the double-zone hemolysis (DZH) test for detecting livestock-associated methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (LA-MRSA). The DZH test showed high positive and negative predictive values, sensitivity, and specificity for identifying LA-MRSA-CC398 and other LA-MRSA lineages. The presence of the scn gene and the integrity of the hlb gene were strongly correlated with the DZH phenotype.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR to characterize the scn and hlb genes, and the DZH test was performed on sheep blood agar plates. Whole-genome sequencing was conducted on an isolate with an atypical DZH phenotype.

full_output.paper_title: Using genomics to explore the epidemiology of vancomycin resistance in a sewage system.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies vanHAX and vanHBX as the primary glycopeptide resistance genes in the Lynetten sewage system, with vanHAX predominantly associated with Enterococcus faecalis and Enterococcus faecium, and vanHBX mainly linked to Enterococcus faecium.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic sequencing and Hi-C technology were used to analyze glycopeptide resistance genes in sewage samples.

full_output.paper_title: The increasing burden of group B Streptococcus from 2013 to 2023: a retrospective cohort study in Beijing, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the increasing burden of Group B Streptococcus (GBS) in both pregnant and non-pregnant women, with high resistance rates to erythromycin, clindamycin, and levofloxacin. Invasive GBS strains showed higher resistance to levofloxacin compared to colonizing strains.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of GBS data from a large tertiary hospital in Beijing, including antimicrobial susceptibility testing using disk diffusion and broth microdilution methods.

full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that nutrient conditions significantly affect the pharmacodynamic response of Pseudomonas aeruginosa to antibiotics, particularly tobramycin, with glucose reducing and lactate increasing the EC50 values, indicating altered antibiotic sensitivity.
full_output.methodology: The study used time-kill assays with a bioluminescent P. aeruginosa PAO1 strain to evaluate the impact of different carbon sources on antibiotic sensitivity, combined with pharmacodynamic modeling and PK-PD simulations.

full_output.paper_title: Lipid discovery enabled by sequence statistics and machine learning.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies MprF enzymes from various bacterial species that synthesize novel cationic lipids, including Lys-Glc-DAG and Lys-Glc2-DAG, demonstrating their role in lipid modification and potential implications for microbial resistance mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Sequence analysis, lipidomic profiling, and heterologous expression in S. mitis.

full_output.paper_title: Epigenetic control of tetrapyrrole biosynthesis by m4C DNA methylation in a cyanobacterium.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a suppressor mutation in the slr1790 promoter of Synechocystis 6803, which changes the GGCC motif to GGTC, affecting hemJ expression and reversing the bluish pigmentation phenotype caused by the absence of M.Ssp6803II.
full_output.methodology: Resequencing analysis, qRT-PCR, and promoter activity assays were used to investigate the impact of the GGCC methylation on hemJ expression.

full_output.key_findings: The study established epidemiological cut-off (ECOFF) values for etimicin against several bacterial species, including Escherichia coli, Klebsiella pneumoniae, Proteus mirabilis, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Acinetobacter baumannii, and Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.methodology: The study used broth microdilution method to determine minimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) of etimicin and calculated ECOFFs using ECOFFinder software and visual estimation following EUCAST principles.

full_output.paper_title: Exploring the diversity of anti-defense systems across prokaryotes, phages and mobile genetic elements.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes Apyc1, a bacterial enzyme that cleaves cyclic nucleotides, which was co-opted by phages to counteract defense systems utilizing cyclic nucleotides.
full_output.methodology: Development of AntiDefenseFinder tool, in vitro cleavage assays, structural analysis, and phylogenetic analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Bacteria of the order Burkholderiales are original environmental hosts of type II trimethoprim resistance genes (dfrB).

full_output.paper_title: Genomic perspective on the bacillus causing paratyphoid B fever.

gyrB.notes: Mutations in quinolone resistance-determining regions of gyrA and gyrB

full_output.paper_title: Development and application of a quadruplex TaqMan real-time fluorescence quantitative PCR assay for four porcine digestive pathogens.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a quadruplex TaqMan real-time PCR assay for the detection of four porcine digestive pathogens: Salmonella enterica, Escherichia coli, Lawsonia intracellularis, and Brachyspira hyodysenteriae. The assay demonstrated high sensitivity and specificity, with detection limits of 10 copies/μL for Salmonella invA and 100 copies/μL for the other targets.
full_output.methodology: The study used a quadruplex TaqMan real-time PCR assay with specific primers and probes targeting the invA gene of Salmonella, the 23S rRNA gene of E. coli, the aspA gene of L. intracellularis, and the nox gene of B. hyodysenteriae.

full_output.paper_title: Vibrio alginolyticus is the pathogen of "Baotou" disease causing serious damage to Gracilariopsis lemaneiformis cultivation in China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies Vibrio alginolyticus as the pathogen responsible for 'Baotou' disease in Gracilariopsis lemaneiformis, demonstrating its dominance in affected samples and its ability to cause disease symptoms consistent with 'Baotou' disease.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed bacterial communities using 16S rRNA sequencing and assessed pathogenicity through controlled infection experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Bacteria-specific modified nucleoside is released and elevated in urine of patients with bacterial infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies 2-methyladenosine (m2A) as a bacteria-specific modified nucleoside that is released upon bacterial lysis and elevated in the urine of patients with bacterial infections.
full_output.methodology: The study used LC-MS to analyze modified nucleosides in bacterial and human RNA, along with mouse and clinical urine samples to validate m2A levels.

Mutations in this region, such as I13C/M47C and I16C/M47C, disrupt DNA binding by immobilizing the N-terminal helix, highlighting its importance in the mechanism of MarA-mediated gene regulation.

full_output.paper_title: Non-toxigenic cases of Vibrio cholerae in Spain from 2012 to 2022.

Additionally, a mutation in the parE gene (D476N) was found to be associated with resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Highly Sensitive In Vivo Imaging of Bacterial Infections with a Hydrophilicity-Switching, Self-Immobilizing, Near-Infrared Fluorogenic β-Lactamase Probe Enriched within Bacteria.

full_output.methodology: The study involved the design, synthesis, and in vitro/in vivo characterization of the BIN-3 probe, along with assessing its performance in detecting β-lactamase activity in bacterial infections.

full_output.paper_title: Distinct molecular epidemiology of resistances to extended-spectrum cephalosporins and carbapenems in Enterobacter hormaechei in cats and dogs versus horses in France.

full_output.paper_title: Development a risk prediction nomogram for multidrug-resistant bacterial and fungal infection in gastrointestinal fistula patients during the perioperative period.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria, particularly carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae and Klebsiella pneumoniae, as the primary causes of infections in gastrointestinal fistula patients during the perioperative period.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective cohort study analyzing resistance patterns and risk factors for multidrug-resistant infections in gastrointestinal fistula patients.

full_output.paper_title: Terpenoids as principal bioactive compound of Cissampelos oppositifolia essential oils: enhancing synergistic efficacy with conventional antibiotics.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies terpenoids from Cissampelos oppositifolia essential oils, including alpha-pinene, delta-carene, and caryophyllene, which show synergistic effects with antibiotics like amoxicillin and erythromycin against E. coli and S. aureus. Delta-carene exhibited the strongest antimicrobial activity and synergistic effects with erythromycin, while alpha-pinene showed significant synergy with amoxicillin.
full_output.methodology: The study used disc diffusion, MIC determination, time-kill assays, FTIR, UV spectroscopy, and molecular docking to evaluate the antimicrobial effects of terpenoids and their combinations with antibiotics.

full_output.paper_title: A nationwide survey of antimicrobial resistance of Escherichia coli isolated from broiler chickens in Malawi.

full_output.paper_title: Applying a polysaccharide lyase from Stenotrophomonas maltophilia to disrupt alginate exopolysaccharide produced by Pseudomonas aeruginosa clinical isolates.
full_output.key_findings: Smlt1473, a polysaccharide lyase from Stenotrophomonas maltophilia, inhibits and degrades alginate exopolysaccharide produced by Pseudomonas aeruginosa clinical isolates, demonstrating effectiveness against acetylated alginate.

full_output.paper_title: Screening novel antiviral compounds to treat Clostridioides difficile infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified four antiviral compounds (rottlerin, alpha-mangostin, dryocrassin ABBA, and obefazimod) with potent anti-Clostridioides difficile activity, showing MIC values comparable to vancomycin. These compounds exhibited minimal to no activity against gut microbiota and demonstrated either bactericidal or bacteriostatic effects against C. difficile.
full_output.methodology: The study used broth microdilution techniques to screen antiviral compounds for anti-C. difficile activity, determining MIC values and assessing bactericidal/bacteriostatic effects through time-kill assays.

full_output.paper_title: Recombinant design of the enzymatically active domain of phage Enc34 endolysin to improve its activity against Gram-negative bacteria.

full_output.paper_title: Hypusination in intestinal epithelial cells protects mice from infectious colitis.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that hypusination in intestinal epithelial cells protects against infectious colitis caused by A/E pathogens like C. rodentium and EPEC. Deletion of Dhps, which is critical for hypusination, exacerbates colitis and reduces the expression of detoxification enzymes.
full_output.methodology: The study used Western blotting, RNA sequencing, proteomics, and histological analysis to examine the role of hypusination in protecting against colitis.

full_output.paper_title: The phage protein paratox is a multifunctional metabolic regulator of Streptococcus.
full_output.key_findings: Prx interacts with several DNA-binding proteins including Esub1 and JM3, indicating a broader role in regulating metabolic processes in Streptococcus pyogenes.
full_output.methodology: Pull-down experiments, SEC-binding assays, and X-ray crystallography were used to identify and validate Prx interaction partners.

full_output.paper_title: Lonidamine, a Novel Modulator for the BvgAS System of Bordetella Species.

full_output.paper_title: Investigation of integron gene cassettes in trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Metabolic response of Klebsiella oxytoca to ciprofloxacin exposure: a metabolomics approach.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies IDO1 and HDAC as promising targets for synergistic immunotherapy in colorectal cancer, demonstrating that their inhibition enhances antitumor immune responses and suppresses tumor growth.

full_output.paper_title: Fecal Carriage and Risk Factors Associated with Extended-Spectrum β-Lactamase-/AmpC-/Carbapenemase-Producing Escherichia coli in Dogs from Italy.

full_output.paper_title: Development of Naphthalene-Derivative Bis-QACs as Potent Antimicrobials: Unraveling Structure-Activity Relationship and Microbiological Properties.

full_output.paper_title: Cytotoxic and Antibacterial Cyclodepsipeptides from an Endophytic Fungus Fusarium avenaceum W8.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial activity of iron-depriving pyoverdines against human opportunistic pathogens.

full_output.paper_title: Curcumin and doxorubicin encapsulated in biocompatible clay-based nanomaterial: A strategy to overcome multidrug resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Efficacy of carbonyl cyanide-3-chlorophenylhydrazone in combination with antibiotics against Mycobacterium abscessus.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that carbonyl cyanide 3-chlorophenylhydrazone (CCCP) enhances the antibacterial effects of antibiotics against Mycobacterium abscessus, showing synergistic and additive interactions with clarithromycin, amikacin, linezolid, bedaquiline, and clofazimine.

full_output.paper_title: Establishment of Sample-to-Answer Loop-Mediated Isothermal Amplification-Based Nucleic Acid Testing Using the Sampling, Processing, Incubation, Detection and Lateral Flow Immunoassay Platforms.

full_output.paper_title: Epidemiology and Molecular Characterisation of Multidrug-Resistant Escherichia coli Isolated from Cow Milk.

full_output.paper_title: Advancements in MRSA treatment: the role of berberine in enhancing antibiotic therapy.
full_output.key_findings: Berberine (BBR) showed variable but significant inhibitory effects on 50 clinical MRSA strains, with synergistic effects observed when combined with amikacin in 6 strains. BBR disrupted MRSA cell wall integrity, leading to leakage of cellular contents. Network pharmacology analysis revealed BBR targets multiple pathways essential for bacterial survival.
full_output.methodology: Antibiotic susceptibility testing, time-kill curve studies, conductivity tests, flow cytometry, and transmission electron microscopy were used to evaluate BBR's antibacterial effects.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified tetracycline resistance mediated by tetO and macrolide resistance mediated by ermB in human Streptococcus suis serotype 14 isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial resistance profile, biofilm forming capacity and associated factors of multidrug resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa among patients admitted at Tikur Anbessa Specialized Hospital and Yekatit 12 Hospital Medical College in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia.

full_output.paper_title: Genotypic diversity and virulence factors of Klebsiella pneumoniae in a North Indian tertiary care hospital.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial Activity of Tea and Agarwood Leaf Extracts Against Multidrug-Resistant Microbes.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the prevalence of extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL) and aminoglycoside modifying enzyme (AME) genes in multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacteria, highlighting the significant presence of blaTEM, blaCTX-M, blaSHV, aac(6')-Ib, aac(6')-Ic, aac(3)-Ia, aac(3)-Ib, aac(3)-IIa, ant(2'')-Ia, and ant(4'')-IIa genes.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization and functionality of Ligilactobacillus agilis 1003 isolated from chicken cecum against Klebsiella pneumoniae.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified two antibiotic resistance genes, rpoB2 and vatI, in the genome of Ligilactobacillus agilis 1003. full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial activity and synergistic effect of phage-encoded antimicrobial peptides with colistin and outer membrane permeabilizing agents against Acinetobacter baumannii.
full_output.key_findings: Three phage-encoded antimicrobial peptides (PE04-1, PE04-1(NH2), and PE04-2) showed significant antimicrobial activity against multidrug-resistant (MDR) and extensively drug-resistant (XDR) Acinetobacter baumannii, as well as other bacterial species. full_output.paper_title: Mucosal-adapted bacteriophages as a preventive strategy for a lethal Pseudomonas aeruginosa challenge in mice.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies two phages, VAC1 and VAC3, which infect Pseudomonas aeruginosa. VAC3 shows superior performance in mucin-exposed conditions and retains in the respiratory tract of mice, offering protection against a lethal P. aeruginosa challenge.
full_output.methodology: Phages were isolated from environmental water samples, characterized using transmission electron microscopy, and their genomic sequences were analyzed. In vivo experiments assessed phage retention and protective effects against P. aeruginosa infection.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic typing, antimicrobial resistance gene, virulence factor and plasmid replicon database for the important pathogenic bacteria Klebsiella pneumoniae.

full_output.paper_title: Chitosan nano-formulation enhances stability and bactericidal activity of the lytic phage HK6.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that encapsulating phage HK6 in chitosan nanoparticles (CS-NPs) significantly enhances its stability, efficacy, and delivery against Enterobacter cloacae. The phage remained effective at high pH levels (11 and 12) and demonstrated superior antibacterial activity within 2 hours of exposure.
full_output.methodology: The study involved the synthesis and characterization of chitosan nanoparticles (CS-NPs) encapsulating phage HK6. Techniques included FTIR, DLS, zeta potential measurements, SEM, TEM, and antibacterial activity assays.

full_output.paper_title: Exploration of the feasibility of clinical application of phage treatment for multidrug-resistant Serratia marcescens-induced pulmonary infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study explored the feasibility of using phage Spe5P4 for treating multidrug-resistant Serratia marcescens infections, demonstrating its efficacy and safety in a patient with refractory pulmonary infection.

full_output.paper_title: Study on the Effect of Phillyrin on Streptococcus suis In Vivo and In Vitro.
full_output.key_findings: Phillyrin was found to inhibit the growth of Streptococcus suis (SS2) in vitro, disrupt membrane integrity, increase DNA exosmosis, reduce hemolysin secretion, inhibit biofilm formation, and protect NPTr cells from SS2 infection. Molecular docking suggested that phillyrin binds to suilysin (SLY), a key virulence factor of SS2.
full_output.methodology: Antibacterial activity was assessed through MIC/MBC determination, DNA exosmosis assays, hemolysis assays, biofilm formation analysis, and molecular docking studies.
