full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to identify antibiotic resistance genes and mutations in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Mucous Permeable Nanoparticle for Inducing Cuproptosis-Like Death In Broad-Spectrum Bacteria for Nebulized Treatment of Acute Pneumonia.
full_output.key_findings: The study introduces Cu2O-BSO NPs, a nanoparticle formulation designed to induce cuproptosis-like death in bacteria, showing broad-spectrum antibacterial activity against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, including MRSA and PAO1. The nanoparticles demonstrate effectiveness in eradicating biofilms, reducing bacterial virulence, and enhancing macrophage phagocytosis.
full_output.methodology: The study involves the synthesis and characterization of Cu2O-BSO NPs, evaluation of their antibacterial and anti-biofilm effects in vitro and in vivo, and investigation of their impact on bacterial transcriptomes and macrophage responses.

full_output.paper_title: Experience in Ceftazidime-Avibactam for treatment of MDR BGN infection in Oncologic Children.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates the effectiveness of Ceftazidime-Avibactam (CAZ-AVI) in treating multidrug-resistant Gram-negative bacilli (MDR-GNB) infections in pediatric oncology patients, achieving microbiological sterilization in 92% of episodes and a 30-day survival rate of 84%.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective observational study analyzing 13 episodes of MDR-GNB infections in 11 pediatric oncology patients treated with CAZ-AVI.

full_output.paper_title: Pathogen Distribution, Drug Resistance, and Postoperative High-Quality Nursing Intervention Effectiveness in Knee Osteoarthritis Patients After Knee Arthroplasty With Postoperative Infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified Staphylococcus aureus and Staphylococcus epidermidis as the primary Gram-positive pathogens causing postoperative infections in knee osteoarthritis patients after knee arthroplasty. These pathogens showed high resistance to several antibiotics, including penicillin, ampicillin, erythromycin, and ciprofloxacin, but remained sensitive to vancomycin and teicoplanin. Gram-negative bacteria, mainly Escherichia coli and Pseudomonas aeruginosa, exhibited high resistance to fluoroquinolones but lower resistance to carbapenems. High-quality nursing interventions were found to significantly improve postoperative pain management, knee function, and patient satisfaction.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of clinical data from 87 patients with postoperative infections and 87 controls, including pathogen culture, drug susceptibility testing via K-B disk diffusion, and assessment of inflammatory markers and patient outcomes.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified high antibiotic resistance and genetic diversity among uropathogenic E. coli (UPEC) strains, with particular emphasis on the pap gene's increased expression in recurrent UTI isolates.
full_output.methodology: PCR, disk diffusion, ERIC-PCR, and real-time PCR were used to analyze virulence genes, antibiotic resistance, and genetic diversity.

full_output.paper_title: Analytical and clinical validation of a novel MeltPlus TB-NTM/RIF platform for simultaneous detection of Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex, Non-Tuberculous Mycobacteria and rifampicin resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The MeltPlus TB-NTM/RIF platform was validated for the simultaneous detection of Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex (MTBC), Non-Tuberculous Mycobacteria (NTM), and rifampicin (RIF) resistance. It demonstrated high sensitivity and specificity for MTBC (98.76% and 94.42%, respectively), NTM (91.98% and 99.59%, respectively), and RIF resistance (90.24% and 95.98%, respectively).
full_output.methodology: The platform combines asymmetric PCR with melting curve analysis for the detection of MTBC, NTM, and RIF resistance. It was evaluated using clinical samples and compared with existing methods such as GeneXpert MTB/RIF and a commercial PCR kit.

full_output.paper_title: Parallel Detection of the Unamplified Carbapenem Resistance Genes bla(NDM-1) and bla(OXA-1) Using a Plasmonic Nano-Biosensor with a Field-Portable DNA Extraction Method.

full_output.methodology: A gold nanoparticle-based plasmonic biosensor was used for the detection of bla(NDM-1) and bla(OXA-1) genes, with DNA extracted using a commercial kit and a boiling method.

full_output.paper_title: Marmaricines A-C: Antimicrobial Brominated Pyrrole Alkaloids from the Red Sea Marine Sponge Agelas sp. aff. marmarica.
full_output.key_findings: The study isolated three new brominated pyrrole alkaloids, marmaricines A-C, from the Red Sea sponge Agelas sp. aff. marmarica. full_output.methodology: Bioassay-guided fractionation, NMR spectroscopy, and HPLC purification were used to isolate and characterize the compounds. Antimicrobial activities were evaluated using disk diffusion assay, MIC, MBC, and MFC tests.

full_output.paper_title: Inhibitors of Lysinoalanine Cross-Linking in the Flagella Hook as Antimicrobials against Spirochetes.

full_output.paper_title: Eradication of Helicobacter pylori reshapes gut microbiota and facilitates the evolution of antimicrobial resistance through gene transfer and genomic mutations in the gut.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a negative correlation between type II toxin-antitoxin (TA) systems and antibiotic resistance (AR) determinants in Staphylococcus aureus. Several AR genes, including ermT, ermB, blaZ, mecA, dfrK, dfrG, qacA, aad(6), aph(3')-IIIa, sat-4, msrA, mphC, ermA, tet(K), and ermC, were found to be negatively correlated with TA systems. The research highlights the functional impact of TA systems on AR, showing that the expression of certain TA systems can decrease antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: Genomic analysis, co-occurrence studies, and experimental validation of TA system effects on antibiotic resistance in S. aureus.

This allele was found in commensal Neisseria isolates and was horizontally transferred to a quinolone-resistant N. meningitidis ST4821 strain, causing fulminant meningitis.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and natural transformation experiments were conducted to characterize the penA795 allele and its impact on resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Iron-sulfur cluster proteins present the weak spot in non-thermal plasma-treated Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that [FeS] cluster proteins are targeted by non-thermal plasma, leading to their inactivation. Mutants defective in [FeS] cluster synthesis and maintenance show increased plasma sensitivity. Overexpression of sodA and katE significantly improves plasma resistance by protecting [FeS] cluster-containing enzymes.
full_output.methodology: Genome-wide screening, enzyme activity assays, and plasmid-based over-expression experiments were used to investigate the role of [FeS] cluster proteins and antioxidant enzymes in plasma resistance.

full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing, conjugation assays, MIC testing, and phylogenetic analysis were used to characterize the IncFII K34 KPC-2 plasmid and its role in CR-hvKp.
full_output.sample_size: 485 CRKp isolates from a multi-center study, 259 CRKp isolates from 11 hospitals, and 67,631 K. pneumoniae genomes from GenBank.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical utility of nanopore-targeted sequencing for diagnosing and treating pulmonary infectious diseases from bronchoalveolar lavage fluid.
full_output.key_findings: The study evaluates the clinical utility of nanopore-targeted sequencing (NTS) for diagnosing pulmonary infectious diseases, highlighting its higher sensitivity compared to conventional microbial testing (CMTs) in detecting pathogens such as Mycobacterium tuberculosis, non-tuberculous mycobacteria, Aspergillus, and Pneumocystis jirovecii. NTS provides faster results and aids in adjusting antibiotic treatments effectively.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of plasmid-mediated fosfomycin resistance among Escherichia coli harboring fosA4, tet(X4), and mcr-1 genes in wild birds.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic insights into extended-spectrum β-lactamase- and plasmid-borne AmpC-producing Escherichia coli transmission between humans and livestock in rural Cambodia.

full_output.paper_title: The analysis of antimicrobials epidemiological cut-off values of mycoplasma gallisepticum isolated from goose.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified a high incidence of multidrug-resistant organisms (MDROs) among surgical site infections (SSIs) in a tertiary medical center in Malaysia. Key MDROs included methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), methicillin-resistant coagulase-negative Staphylococci (MRCoNS), multidrug-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii, multidrug-resistant Escherichia coli, multidrug-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae, and multidrug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed clinical and microbiological data from 1,826 surgical patients over a period of 28 months, focusing on the incidence of SSIs and the antimicrobial resistance profiles of isolated pathogens.

The cobas MTB-RIF/INH assay detected 19 out of 21 INH-resistant and 22 out of 24 RIF-resistant TB strains, highlighting the importance of specific mutations in rpoB, katG, and inhA genes for resistance detection.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of antibiotic determinants and heavy metal resistance genes in Escherichia coli from pigs in Catalonia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various AMR genes in Escherichia coli isolates from pigs in Catalonia, including mdfA, aph(3")-Ib, bla TEM-1B, aph(6)-Id, bla CTX-M, bla SHV, mcr-1, mcr-4, mcr-5, oqxA, oqxB, qnrB19, qnrD1, and qnrS1. These genes conferred resistance to multiple antibiotic classes, including beta-lactams, aminoglycosides, quinolones, and colistin.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to identify AMR and HM tolerance genes in Escherichia coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: The spread of antimicrobial resistance in the aquatic environment from faecal pollution: a scoping review of a multifaceted issue.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies various antimicrobial resistance genes (AMRs) in aquatic environments linked to faecal pollution, emphasizing the role of wastewater treatment plants and agricultural practices in spreading resistance. Key genes include beta-lactamases (bla CTX, bla TEM, bla OXA, bla SHV, bla KPC), tetracycline resistance genes (tet A, tet O, tet Q, tet W, tet X), sulfonamide resistance genes (sul 1, sul 2), aminoglycoside resistance genes (aph, aad, aac), quinolone resistance gene (qnr S), MLSB resistance genes (erm B, erm F), phenicol resistance genes (cat, cml, flo R), colistin resistance gene (mcr), glycopeptide resistance genes (van A, van B, van C), and integrons (int I1, int I2, int I3).
full_output.methodology: Literature review and analysis of studies on antimicrobial resistance in aquatic environments.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic and phenotypic characterization of staphylococci isolated from the skin of non-human primates.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified 85 antimicrobial resistance determinants across 14 staphylococcal isolates, with only one case of clinical resistance observed. Genes such as arlR, mepR, mgrA, qacJ, and dfrC were predicted to confer resistance to various antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Genomic and phenotypic analysis of staphylococci isolated from non-human primates, including whole-genome sequencing and disc diffusion assays.

full_output.key_findings: The study focuses on regulatory genes and their associations with biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) in Streptomyces, identifying potential markers for discovering and prioritizing BGCs with bioactive potential.
full_output.methodology: The research involved analyzing regulatory protein domain architectures from 440 Streptomyces genomes, identifying associations between regulatory genes and BGCs, and using clustering algorithms to explore structural similarities within candidate BGC regions.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of FosA13, a novel fosfomycin glutathione transferase identified in a Morganella morganii isolate from poultry.

fosA13.evidence_note: The gene was identified through whole-genome sequencing and confirmed by cloning and functional analysis.

full_output.key_findings: A novel chromosomal fosfomycin resistance gene, fosA13, was identified in a Morganella morganii isolate from poultry. The gene encodes a glutathione S-transferase that inactivates fosfomycin, resulting in a fourfold increase in MIC values.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, molecular cloning, enzyme kinetics analysis, and MIC testing.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic analysis of multidrug-resistant Escherichia coli isolated from dairy cows in Shihezi city, Xinjiang, China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified key AMR genes, including mphA, qnrS1, and bla CTX-M-55, in multidrug-resistant E. coli isolates from dairy cows in Shihezi City, China, highlighting the presence of resistance to macrolides, quinolones, and beta-lactams.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and comparative genomic analysis were used to identify AMR genes and virulence factors in E. coli isolates.
full_output.sample_size: Two MDR E. coli isolates (E.coli_30 and E.coli_45)

full_output.paper_title: Comparative analysis of proteomics and transcriptomics reveals novel mechanism underlying the antibacterial activity and immune-enhancing properties of horse milk.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies four antimicrobial-associated proteins in horse milk, namely LPO, B2M, CD14, and PGL, which exhibit in vitro antibacterial activity and immune activation.
full_output.methodology: Label-free mass spectrometry-based protein quantification, prokaryotic expression, and disk diffusion assay were used to analyze the antimicrobial activity of proteins in horse milk.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization and ex vivo modelling of endodontic infections from the Arabian Gulf region.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antibiotic resistance genes, including bla, aac(6')-Ib, tet(M), qnrS1, erm(B), and mcr-1, in endodontic infection samples from the Arabian Gulf region. These genes were found to confer resistance to various antibiotics, highlighting the presence of multidrug-resistant bacteria in these infections.
full_output.methodology: Shotgun metagenomic sequencing and culture-dependent techniques were used to analyze the microbial composition, resistome, and virulome of endodontic infection samples.

full_output.paper_title: Burkholderia cenocepacia-mediated inhibition of Staphylococcus aureus growth and biofilm formation.
full_output.key_findings: Burkholderia cenocepacia produces secreted compounds that inhibit Staphylococcus aureus biofilm formation and growth, with the mechanism involving a contact-independent process potentially mediated by siderophores like pyochelin.
full_output.methodology: Biofilm survival assays, co-culture experiments, and metabolomic analysis were used to investigate the inhibitory effects of B. cenocepacia on S. aureus.

full_output.paper_title: The Streptococcus pyogenes mannose phosphotransferase system (Man-PTS) influences antimicrobial activity and niche-specific nasopharyngeal infection.

full_output.methodology: Transposon mutagenesis, genetic complementation, and RNA-seq analysis were used to investigate the role of Man-PTS in sugar metabolism and infection.

full_output.paper_title: Post-pandemic upsurge in Group A Streptococcus infections at an Italian tertiary university hospital.

gyrA.notes: Isolate #30

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies quinolone resistance in two Group A Streptococcus isolates through mutations in the parC and gyrA genes, highlighting the emergence of resistance mechanisms in post-pandemic GAS infections.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of novel amrR deletions as meropenem resistance mechanisms in clinical Burkholderia pseudomallei isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of a novel phage depolymerase against ST11 K64 carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae and its therapeutic potential.

full_output.methodology: Phage isolation, depolymerase expression and purification, assessment of antibacterial activity, biofilm disruption, and in vivo evaluation in a Galleria mellonella infection model.

full_output.paper_title: The extent of carbapenem-resistant encoding genes in Klebsiella pneumoniae from COVID-19 and non-COVID-19 patients in a tertiary care center, Saudi Arabia.

full_output.methodology: Multiplex PCR and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to detect and characterize carbapenem-resistant genes in K. pneumoniae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of Helicobacter pylori and the Genotypes of Resistance to Clarithromycin, Fluoroquinolones, and Metronidazole in Gastric Biopsies: An In Silico Analysis to Help Understand Antibiotic Resistance.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified various mutations in the gyrA and rdxA genes associated with resistance to fluoroquinolones and metronidazole in Helicobacter pylori, respectively. These mutations were analyzed through in silico methods to understand their potential roles in antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized real-time PCR and sequencing to detect mutations in the 23S rRNA, gyrA, and rdxA genes, followed by in silico analysis to evaluate the structural impacts of these mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Whole-Genome Sequencing of Extended-Spectrum β-Lactamase-Producing Klebsiella pneumoniae Isolated from Human Bloodstream Infections.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple AMR genes in ESBL-producing K. pneumoniae isolates, including blaCTX-M-15, blaKPC-3, and others conferring resistance to β-lactams, aminoglycosides, fluoroquinolones, sulfonamides, tetracyclines, and chloramphenicol.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing was used to identify AMR genes in 14 ESBL-producing K. pneumoniae isolates.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified OXA-48, NDM, and KPC as the most prevalent carbapenemase genes in carbapenem-resistant K. pneumoniae isolates. CZA showed high efficacy against OXA-48-producing isolates, whereas MEV had limited activity.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of carbapenemase genes and antibiotic susceptibility testing using disk diffusion and automated systems.

full_output.paper_title: Emergence of Tigecycline-Nonsusceptible Carbapenem-Resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae with Metallo-β-Lactamase and Transferable Ceftazidime-Avibactam Resistance in China.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies multiple AMR genes and mutations in MBL-CRKP strains, including blaIMP-4, blaNDM-1, blaNDM-29, and tmexCD2-toprJ2, which confer resistance to carbapenems, CZA, and tigecycline. Mutations in rpsJ, tet(A), ompK35, and ompK36, along with upregulation of efflux pump genes, contribute to tigecycline resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, conjugation experiments, and efflux pump inhibition assays were used to characterize AMR genes and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Expanded Gram-Negative Activity of Marinopyrrole A.
full_output.key_findings: Marinopyrrole A shows efficacy against a broader range of Gram-negative bacteria, including Neisseria gonorrhoeae, Campylobacter jejuni, and Moraxella catarrhalis, which are susceptible due to the absence of canonical LPS and the presence of lipooligosaccharides (LOS).
full_output.methodology: In vitro antibacterial susceptibility testing and LpxC inhibitor assays were conducted to evaluate the efficacy of marinopyrrole A against various Gram-negative bacteria.

full_output.paper_title: Molecular Characterization and Antimicrobial Resistance Evaluation of Listeria monocytogenes Strains from Food and Human Samples.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several intrinsic antimicrobial resistance genes in Listeria monocytogenes strains, including fosX, norB, sul, and lmo0919, which confer resistance to fosfomycin, quinolones, sulfonamides, and lincosamides, respectively.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify and characterize antimicrobial resistance genes in Listeria monocytogenes strains.

full_output.paper_title: Pharmacogenomic heterogeneity of N-acetyltransferase 2: a comprehensive analysis of real world data in Indian tuberculosis patients and from literature and database review.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified NAT2 SNPs, particularly rs1041983 (282C > T), associated with increased risk of antitubercular drug-induced liver injury (AT-DILI) in Indian tuberculosis patients.
full_output.methodology: Genotyping of six NAT2 SNPs in TB patients from Southern and Western India using TaqMan assay.

full_output.paper_title: Mechanism of antibacterial and antibiofilm of thiazolidinone derivative TD-H2-A against Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the antibacterial and antibiofilm effects of thiazolidinone derivative TD-H2-A against Staphylococcus aureus. TD-H2-A was found to inhibit WalK autophosphorylation, leading to changes in gene expression related to biofilm formation, membrane transport, and ribosome synthesis. The compound affected multiple molecular pathways, suggesting a multitarget mechanism.
full_output.methodology: The study used RNA-seq to analyze gene expression changes in S. aureus after TD-H2-A treatment, along with phosphorylation assays and qRT-PCR validation.

full_output.paper_title: The efficient chitosan-polythiophene-graphene oxide bionanocomposite with enhanced antibacterial activity, dye adsorption ability, mechanical and thermal properties.
full_output.key_findings: The study developed a chitosan-polythiophene-graphene oxide (CS-PTh-GO) bionanocomposite with enhanced antibacterial activity against Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, achieving a minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of 5 µg/mL against E. coli and S. aureus. The material also exhibited high dye removal efficiency for methylene blue (MB).
full_output.methodology: The bionanocomposite was synthesized through interfacial polymerization and characterized using FTIR, XRD, SEM, TEM, and tensile analysis. Antibacterial activity was assessed via MIC testing.

full_output.paper_title: Serotype distribution of invasive Pneumococcal disease in a tertiary children's hospital in Vietnam.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high levels of antibiotic resistance in Streptococcus pneumoniae isolates, with nearly 100% resistance to erythromycin and clindamycin, and 75.3% resistance to third-generation cephalosporins. Serotypes 6A/B, 19A, 23F, 19F, and 14 were the most prevalent.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of S. pneumoniae isolates from children with invasive pneumococcal disease, including serotyping and antibiotic susceptibility testing.

full_output.paper_title: Zoonotic potential of uropathogenic Escherichia coli lineages from companion animals.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antimicrobial resistance genes in uropathogenic E. coli strains from companion animals, including blaTEM-1b, sul1, sul2, dfrA1_10, dfrA17_1, dfrA1_8, dfrA7_5, gyrA_S83L, tetA, tetB, aph(6)-Id, aph(3'')-Ib, ant(3'')-Ia, blaCTX-M-15, blaTEM-106, blaSHV-102, and blaCMY-2. These genes confer resistance to various antibiotics such as penicillins, sulfonamides, trimethoprim, quinolones, tetracyclines, streptomycin, and cephalosporins.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to analyze the resistance genes and mutations in E. coli strains from companion animals.

full_output.paper_title: Scaptotrigona mexicana Propolis from Totonacapan Region: Chemical Composition, Antioxidant and Antibacterial Activities.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various compounds in Scaptotrigona mexicana propolis, including taraxeryl acetate, lupeol, and others, and evaluated its antibacterial activity against specific bacteria.
full_output.methodology: Chemical profiling, extraction, isolation, and antimicrobial activity testing using microdilution methods.

full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the high usage of antibiotics in ICUs after the third wave of COVID-19 in Pakistan, with a focus on the WHO AWaRe classification. It found that carbapenems were the most effective against bacterial isolates, while resistance to other antibiotics was prevalent.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of antibiotic usage in ICUs of four public hospitals in Pakistan, including data on prescriptions, sensitivity, and resistance patterns.

full_output.paper_title: Bacteriophage Resistance, Adhesin's and Toxin's Genes Profile of Staphylococcus aureus Causing Infections in Children and Adolescents.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several virulence genes in Staphylococcus aureus isolates from pediatric infections, including fnbA, fnbB, sasG, icaD, eta, etb, PVL, and tst. These genes were associated with biofilm formation, adhesion, and toxin production, contributing to the pathogenicity of the isolates.
full_output.methodology: PCR and molecular analysis were used to detect the presence of specific virulence genes in S. aureus isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Evolution of β-Lactam Antibiotic Resistance in Proteus Species: From Extended-Spectrum and Plasmid-Mediated AmpC β-Lactamases to Carbapenemases.

full_output.key_findings: The paper reviews the evolution of β-lactam resistance in Proteus species, focusing on extended-spectrum β-lactamases (ESBLs), plasmid-mediated AmpC β-lactamases (p-AmpC), and carbapenemases. It highlights the prevalence of specific genes such as bla TEM-52, bla CTX-M-14, bla CTX-M-15, bla CTX-M-2, bla CTX-M-3, bla CTX-M-8, bla CTX-M-65, bla CTX-M-27, bla SHV-5, bla PER-1, bla VEB-1, bla CMY-16, bla CMY-2, bla DHA-1, bla KPC-2, bla VIM-1, bla NDM-5, bla OXA-48, bla OXA-23, and bla OXA-58, which confer resistance to various β-lactam antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: The paper presents a comprehensive review of existing studies on β-lactam resistance in Proteus species, analyzing the genetic and biochemical mechanisms underlying resistance, including the characterization of specific resistance genes and their impact on antimicrobial susceptibility.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a redox-sensitive acetyltransferase activity in Staphylococcus aureus GlmU, which is regulated by a reversible disulfide bond between C379 and C404. The C379A mutation abolishes this redox sensitivity, highlighting the importance of the redox-switch mechanism in GlmU function.
full_output.methodology: Enzyme assays, mass spectrometry, x-ray crystallography, and in silico modeling were used to characterize the functional and structural effects of the C379 and C404 variation in Sa GlmU.

full_output.paper_title: The prevalence of Group B Streptococcus rectovaginal colonization and antimicrobial susceptibility pattern in Turkish and Syrian pregnant women.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that all Group B Streptococcus (GBS) isolates were susceptible to penicillin, but resistance to non-penicillin antibiotics was observed in a significant proportion of Turkish and Syrian patients, particularly to erythromycin and clindamycin.
full_output.methodology: The study involved culturing vaginal and rectal samples from pregnant women and assessing antimicrobial susceptibility using standard microbiological protocols.

full_output.paper_title: Computational and Experimental Study of Metal-Organic Frameworks (MOFs) as Antimicrobial Agents against Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
full_output.key_findings: The study investigated the potential of metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) as antimicrobial agents against Neisseria gonorrhoeae, focusing on their interactions with the penicillin-binding protein 2 (PBP2). The Cu-BDC MOF was found to be bactericidal for multiple strains of Ng, showing specificity for Ng and low toxicity for human cells.
full_output.methodology: The study combined computational molecular docking analyses with experimental antimicrobial testing using agar diffusion assays and cytotoxicity evaluations.

full_output.paper_title: Characterizing the epidemiology of Mycoplasma pneumoniae infections in China in 2022-2024: a nationwide cross-sectional study of over 1.6 million cases.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a significant increase in macrolide-resistant Mycoplasma pneumoniae (MRMP) in China, with the T1-3R clade showing 100% resistance prevalence. Key mutations in the 23S rRNA gene (A2063G, A2064G, C2617G, and A2067G) were linked to macrolide resistance.
full_output.methodology: The study used targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS) and metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS) to analyze over 1.6 million cases of acute respiratory infections (ARIs) across China.

full_output.paper_title: Synergistic activity of dispersin B and benzoyl peroxide against Cutibacterium acnes/Staphylococcus epidermidis dual-species biofilms.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that dispersin B enhances the susceptibility of Cutibacterium acnes biofilms to benzoyl peroxide (BP), achieving a synergistic effect that significantly reduces C. acnes colony-forming units. Dispersin B degrades PNAG, a component of the biofilm matrix, thereby increasing BP efficacy.
full_output.methodology: The study used in vitro biofilm models, treated with dispersin B and BP, and assessed microbial load via colony counting and crystal violet staining.

full_output.paper_title: Isolation of vanA-Mediated Vancomycin-Resistant Enterococcus faecalis (ST1912/CC116) and Enterococcus faecium (ST80/CC17), optrA-Positive Linezolid-Resistant E. faecalis (ST32, ST1902) from Human Clinical Specimens in Bangladesh.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified vanA-mediated vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecalis and Enterococcus faecium, as well as optrA-positive linezolid-resistant E. faecalis in Bangladesh.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, PCR, sequencing, and MLST were used to analyze resistance genes and genotypes.

full_output.paper_title: Escherichia coli in Brazilian Poultry Fecal Samples: Co-Carriage of Fosfomycin and ESBL Resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies fosA3 as a major contributor to fosfomycin resistance in E. coli isolates from Brazilian poultry fecal samples, with the gene often co-located with ESBL genes on transmissible plasmids.
full_output.methodology: Phenotypic resistance testing, PCR screening, and whole-genome sequencing were used to characterize fosfomycin resistance in E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus T144: A Hypervirulent Model Strain for Infection Models.

It also shows a nonsynonymous mutation in the ParC gene contributing to fluoroquinolone resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and in vivo infection models in Galleria mellonella and mice.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of Antimicrobial Peptides from Nibribacter radioresistens, a UV and Gamma Radiation Tolerant Bacterium.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies 11 antimicrobial peptide (AMP) candidates from Nibribacter radioresistens, designated as NB_AMP1 to NB_AMP11, which show antibacterial activity against both Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria. Synthetic NB_AMP2 exhibits superior antibacterial activity compared to other NB_AMPs.
full_output.methodology: Genomic and transcriptomic analysis, gene cloning, and antibacterial activity assays using E. coli DH5α and S. aureus.

full_output.paper_title: Enhancing Antimicrobial Peptides from Frog Skin: A Rational Approach.
full_output.key_findings: The study focused on designing and characterizing novel antimicrobial peptides derived from hylin-Pul3, a peptide from the frog Boana pulchella, aiming to enhance their antimicrobial activity and reduce cytotoxicity.
full_output.methodology: The study involved rational design, synthesis, and in vitro testing of peptide derivatives to evaluate their antimicrobial, antiviral, and cytotoxic properties.

full_output.paper_title: Calprotectin-mediated survival of Staphylococcus aureus in coculture with Pseudomonas aeruginosa occurs without nutrient metal sequestration.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that calprotectin (CP) promotes the survival of Staphylococcus aureus in coculture with Pseudomonas aeruginosa independently of its metal-sequestering function. CP induces Fe-starvation responses in both bacteria, but its protective effect on S. aureus is not dependent on metal depletion.
full_output.methodology: The study used coculture experiments, RNA extraction, real-time PCR, and metabolite analysis to investigate the effects of CP on P. aeruginosa and S. aureus.

full_output.paper_title: Functionally important residues from graph analysis of coevolved dynamic couplings.

full_output.key_findings: The study introduces DyNoPy, a computational method that integrates residue coevolution analysis with molecular dynamics simulations to identify functionally important residues in beta-lactamases SHV-1 and PDC-3, which are crucial for antibiotic resistance.
full_output.methodology: DyNoPy combines residue coevolution analysis with molecular dynamics simulations to identify functionally important residues in beta-lactamases.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies mutations in genes such as ampC, acrB, acrR, marR, soxR, and ompR that contribute to antibiotic resistance in Escherichia coli under various antibiotic selections.
full_output.methodology: Genome sequencing of evolved E. coli populations under antibiotic selection pressure.

full_output.key_findings: The paper introduces Scorpio, a framework for nucleotide sequence analysis that improves embeddings through contrastive learning. It demonstrates effectiveness in tasks like taxonomic classification, gene identification, and antimicrobial resistance (AMR) prediction. The study highlights Scorpio's ability to generalize to novel sequences and its superior performance in AMR prediction compared to existing methods.
full_output.methodology: Scorpio uses 6-mer frequency and BigBird embeddings with triplet training for contrastive learning. It was evaluated on tasks including taxonomic classification, gene identification, and AMR prediction using datasets like MEGARes and CARD.

full_output.paper_title: (p)ppGpp-mediated GTP homeostasis ensures survival and antibiotic tolerance of Staphylococcus aureus.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that (p)ppGpp is essential for maintaining GTP homeostasis, membrane potential, and antibiotic tolerance in Staphylococcus aureus. Mutants lacking (p)ppGpp exhibit reduced culturability and increased susceptibility to antibiotics, highlighting the critical role of (p)ppGpp in bacterial survival and tolerance.
full_output.methodology: The study used mutant analysis, CFU enumeration, RT-qPCR, LC-MS/MS, and flow cytometry to investigate the role of (p)ppGpp in GTP homeostasis and antibiotic tolerance.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence, antibiotic resistance, virulence and antimicrobial resistance gene profiles of Salmonella species recovered from retail beef and poultry processing environments.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the presence of resistance genes bla TEM, tetA, and sul1 in Salmonella isolates from retail beef and poultry processing environments, indicating high levels of antimicrobial resistance.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of resistance genes and antimicrobial susceptibility testing using the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Serotypes distribution and antibiotic susceptibility of Streptococcus pneumoniae strains: five-year surveillance results of post-PCV-13.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the most prevalent serotypes of Streptococcus pneumoniae and analyzed the antibiotic susceptibility patterns, highlighting the need for more comprehensive pneumococcal vaccines due to increasing resistance rates.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective surveillance of pneumococcal infections, serotyping using multiplex PCR, and antibiotic susceptibility testing according to CLSI standards.

full_output.paper_title: Travel to low- and middle-income countries and travellers' diarrhoea increase risk of mismatching antimicrobial therapy for urinary tract infection.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that travel to low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) and travellers' diarrhoea increase the risk of mismatching antimicrobial therapy for urinary tract infections (UTIs). Non-ESBL-PE UTI patients with recent LMIC travel had higher trimethoprim resistance rates (42.1%) compared to those without (18.0%).
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed resistance profiles of urinary isolates from UTI patients with and without LMIC travel history, comparing antimicrobial susceptibility and treatment outcomes.

full_output.paper_title: From Bones to Bugs: Structure-Based Development of Raloxifene-Derived Pathoblockers That Inhibit Pyocyanin Production in Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies PhzB as a target for RAL (6) and its derivatives, which inhibit pyocyanin production in Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Compounds such as 10d and 10g show potent inhibition of pyocyanin biosynthesis with low micromolar IC50 values.
full_output.methodology: Structure-based design, cocrystallization, nDSF, ITC, and pyocyanin assays were used to evaluate the compounds.

full_output.paper_title: Genetic characterization and transmission of the multidrug resistance gene cfr in fecal and environmental pathways on a chicken farm in China.

cfr.validation_method: PCR, sequencing, conjugation experiments, S1-PFGE, Southern blotting

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the multidrug resistance gene cfr in 18 strains isolated from a chicken farm in China, highlighting its presence in various bacterial species and its transmission through clonal and horizontal gene transfer mechanisms.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, PCR, conjugation experiments, S1-PFGE, Southern blotting, and bioinformatics analysis.

full_output.paper_title: Polyclonal carbapenemase-producing Escherichia coli in Northern Italy: the emergence of NDM-7.

full_output.paper_title: Antimicrobial susceptibility and resistance mechanisms to antipseudomonal β-lactams in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from blood.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified that decreased oprD expression is significantly correlated with non-susceptibility to imipenem and meropenem, while increased ampC and mexA expression is correlated with non-susceptibility to various β-lactams in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates from blood.
full_output.methodology: The study used real-time PCR to analyze gene expression and antimicrobial susceptibility testing to evaluate resistance mechanisms in Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Terminal complement complexes with or without C9 potentiate antimicrobial activity against Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that the membrane attack complex (MAC) and C5b-C8 complexes disrupt the outer and inner membranes of Neisseria gonorrhoeae, enhancing the activity of various antibiotics and re-sensitizing multidrug-resistant strains to antibiotics. C9 is necessary for the potentiation of lysozyme and nisin, but not for azithromycin and ceftriaxone.
full_output.methodology: The study used serum bactericidal assays, flow cytometry, and MIC broth microdilution assays to evaluate the effects of complement components on Neisseria gonorrhoeae.

full_output.paper_title: Structural basis for spermidine recognition and modulation of Acinetobacter baumannii multidrug efflux regulator AmvR.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies AmvR as a TetR family transcription regulator that binds spermidine, a polyamine, and regulates the expression of the multidrug efflux pump AmvA. Key residues in the ligand-binding pocket, such as E164 and E106, are critical for spermidine recognition.
full_output.methodology: Crystallography, EMSA, DNase I footprinting, ITC, and mutagenesis experiments were used to analyze AmvR's structure and function.

full_output.paper_title: Real Way to Target Gram-Negative Pathogens: Discovery of a Novel Helicobacter pylori Antibiotic Class.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies a novel class of antibiotics targeting HpMurI, an essential enzyme in H. pylori, with compounds showing improved activity against antibiotic-resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: Virtual screening, enzyme activity assays, DSF, and MIC testing were used to identify and optimize HpMurI inhibitors.

full_output.paper_title: Comprehensive genomic epidemiology and antimicrobial resistance profiles of clinical Klebsiella pneumoniae species complex isolates from a tertiary hospital in Wenzhou, China (2019-2021).
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a variety of antimicrobial resistance genes in clinical Klebsiella pneumoniae species complex isolates, including bla KPC−2, bla CTX−M, bla SHV, aac(6')-Ib, aadA1, aadA2, aph(3')-Ia, oqxAB, qnrB19, qnrS1, tet(A), tet(D), sul1, sul2, sul3, cmlA1, floR, fosA, and fosA3. These genes confer resistance to multiple classes of antibiotics, highlighting the complexity of antimicrobial resistance in these isolates.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatic analysis were used to identify resistance genes, plasmid types, and virulence factors in the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Whole-genome sequencing of extended spectrum beta lactamases (ESBLs)-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae (kp) isolates from selected hospitals in Malaysia.

full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, PCR, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to identify AMR genes and assess resistance patterns.

full_output.paper_title: Comprehensive molecular epidemiology of Acinetobacter baumannii from diverse sources in Nigeria.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified 168 AMR genes in 189 Nigerian A. baumannii isolates, including blaADC-79, blaOXA-23, aph(3")-Ib, and others, highlighting the widespread presence of multidrug resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and in-silico analysis using ABRicate, CARD, Resfinder, and NCBI databases.

full_output.paper_title: Essential Oils and their Active Constituents Effective against Non-growing Mycobacterium intracellulare.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies carvacrol and citronellol as highly active components of essential oils against non-growing Mycobacterium intracellulare, demonstrating significant antimicrobial activity with low MIC values.
full_output.methodology: The study used MIC assays and CFU counting to evaluate the antimicrobial activity of essential oils and their active components against Mycobacterium intracellulare.

full_output.paper_title: Optimizing lipase production by Bacillus subtilis on cheese whey and evaluating its antimicrobial, antibiofilm, anti virulence and biosafety properties.
full_output.key_findings: The study optimized lipase production by Bacillus subtilis using cheese whey and evaluated its antimicrobial, antibiofilm, anti-virulence, and biosafety properties against Staphylococcus aureus. The lipase showed potent antibacterial activity, with a minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of 1/8 and a minimum bactericidal concentration (MBC) of 1/4, indicating a bactericidal effect. It also demonstrated significant biofilm inhibition and reduced pathogenicity markers such as protease and hemolysin production.
full_output.methodology: The study employed response surface methodology (RSM) for optimizing lipase production, followed by biochemical assays to evaluate antimicrobial, antibiofilm, and anti-virulence activities. Molecular docking was used to predict the interaction of the lipase with bacterial targets.

full_output.paper_title: Linalool as a potential agent for inhibiting Escherichia coli biofilm formation and exopolysaccharide production.
full_output.key_findings: Linalool inhibits Escherichia coli biofilm formation and exopolysaccharide (EPS) production by down-regulating the pgaABCD operon, which is involved in PGA synthesis.
full_output.methodology: RT-qPCR, crystal violet assay, CCK-8 assay, SEM, and CLSM were used to evaluate the effects of linalool on E. coli biofilm formation and EPS production.

full_output.methodology: The study utilized mPCR-CE technology alongside traditional culture methods to detect pathogens and antibiotic resistance genes in various clinical specimens.

full_output.paper_title: Vibrio cholerae O47 associated with a cholera-like diarrheal outbreak concurrent with seasonal cholera in Bangladesh.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified multidrug-resistant (MDR) Vibrio cholerae O47 isolates with resistance to azithromycin, ciprofloxacin, erythromycin, tetracycline, ampicillin, and sulfamethoxazole/trimethoprim. Key resistance mechanisms included the efflux pump gene mphA, the quinolone resistance gene qnrVC, and mutations in gyrA (S83) and parC (S85).

full_output.paper_title: Unveiling the synergistic power of 3-hydrazinoquinoxaline-2-thiol and vancomycin against MRSA: An in vitro and in silico evaluation.

full_output.methodology: In vitro susceptibility testing and in silico molecular docking analysis were used to evaluate the synergistic effects of vancomycin and 3HL against MRSA.

full_output.paper_title: Comparison of antimicrobial resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa from intensive care and non-intensive care units and its impact on treatment decisions.
full_output.key_findings: The study compares antimicrobial resistance in Pseudomonas aeruginosa from ICU and non-ICU patients, highlighting higher resistance to ciprofloxacin in non-ICU and higher resistance to piperacillin-tazobactam in ICU. Carbapenemase-producing strains were more frequent in ICU patients.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective analysis of 309 P. aeruginosa strains using antimicrobial susceptibility testing and resistance mechanism profiling.

full_output.paper_title: A quinolone N-oxide antibiotic selectively targets Neisseria gonorrhoeae via its toxin-antitoxin system.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified that NQNO selectively targets Neisseria gonorrhoeae by activating its toxin-antitoxin system, specifically the zeta1/epsilon1 system, leading to growth inhibition and cell death. Resistance to NQNO was linked to the loss of the pTetM plasmid, which contains the zeta1/epsilon1 operon.
full_output.methodology: The study used growth inhibition assays, electron transport chain analysis, and genetic manipulation to investigate the mechanism of NQNO's activity against N. gonorrhoeae.

full_output.paper_title: NMR characterisation of the antibiotic resistance-mediating 32mer RNA from the 23S ribosomal RNA.

full_output.methodology: Solution NMR spectroscopy was used to assign the chemical shifts of the 32mer RNA construct, comparing the unmethylated, monomethylated (m6A), and dimethylated (DMA) forms.

full_output.paper_title: CRISPR-Cas9 engineered Saccharomyces cerevisiae for endolysin delivery to combat Listeria monocytogenes.
full_output.key_findings: The study demonstrates that CRISPR-Cas9 engineered Saccharomyces cerevisiae can express and secrete the endolysin Ply511, which exhibits enzymatic activity against Listeria monocytogenes. The yeast secreting Ply511 significantly reduces L. monocytogenes levels in co-culture and in milk.
full_output.methodology: CRISPR-Cas9 engineering, yeast transformation, enzymatic activity assays, co-culture experiments, and microbial viability assessments.

full_output.paper_title: Seasonal prevalence and antimicrobial resistance profiles in Enterococcus spp. identified from mussels farmed along the coasts of the Abruzzo region.

full_output.paper_title: Evaluation of phenotypic and genotypic methods for detecting KPC variants.

full_output.methodology: Phenotypic and genotypic characterization, MIC testing, PCA, and evaluation of rapid diagnostic tests.

full_output.key_findings: The study evaluated the in vitro activity of ceftibuten-avibactam against a challenge set of Enterobacterales, demonstrating potent activity with a high susceptibility rate of 96.4%. full_output.methodology: Susceptibility testing was performed using manual broth microdilution and disc diffusion methods.

full_output.paper_title: MultiSeq-AMR: a modular amplicon-sequencing workflow for rapid detection of bloodstream infection and antimicrobial resistance markers.
full_output.key_findings: MultiSeq-AMR is a rapid and modular nanopore amplicon-sequencing workflow that accurately detects bacterial and fungal species and a comprehensive set of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) genes from various infection sources. It exhibits high accuracy in identifying AMR genes, with 99.4% categorical agreement with whole-genome sequencing and 97.4% accuracy for AMR gene prediction in BACT/ALERT positive samples.
full_output.methodology: MultiSeq-AMR uses amplicon sequencing with 93 targets across 14 primer pools to identify species and AMR genes. It was validated using reference strains, BACT/ALERT positive and negative samples, and rapid culture-enriched spiked blood samples.
full_output.sample_size: 16 bacterial and 5 fungal reference/ATCC/NCTC strains, 33 BACT/ALERT positive samples, 3 negative samples, and 13 rapid culture-enriched spiked blood samples

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies phage-associated antimicrobial resistance genes, including qnrS1, blaCTX-M-15, blaCTX-M-55, emrE, and tetA, in ESBL-producing E. coli from human, animal, and environmental sources.
full_output.methodology: In silico analysis of prophage regions in ESBL-EC genomes using PHASTER and other computational tools.

full_output.paper_title: Mutational profile of pfdhfr, pfdhps, pfmdr1, pfcrt and pfk13 genes of P. falciparum associated with resistance to different antimalarial drugs in Osun state, southwestern Nigeria.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified a validated C580Y mutation in the pfk13 gene, candidate R515K mutation, high frequency of pfdhfr mutant alleles, and significant variability in pfdhps haplotypes in P. falciparum isolates from Osun state, Nigeria.
full_output.methodology: Molecular analysis of resistance markers using sequencing techniques.

full_output.paper_title: Chemical Composition, Antioxidant, Antimicrobial, Antidiabetic, and Butyrylcholinesterase Inhibitory Activities in Vitro of the Essential Oil and Crude Extracts of the Aerial Parts of Thymus ciliatus.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the chemical composition and evaluates the antimicrobial, antioxidant, antidiabetic, and butyrylcholinesterase inhibitory activities of the essential oil and crude extracts of Thymus ciliatus. The essential oil showed significant antimicrobial activity against various bacterial and fungal strains, with notable inhibition zones against Gram-positive bacteria and the yeast Candida albicans.
full_output.methodology: Gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) was used for chemical composition analysis, and antimicrobial activity was assessed using agar diffusion and disc methods.

full_output.paper_title: Assessment of the Diagnostic Accuracy of the Modified Hodge Test and Modified Carbapenem Inactivation Method for Identifying Carbapenem Resistance Mechanisms in Klebsiella pneumoniae: A Whole Genome Sequencing-Based Exploratory Study.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified bla OXA-48-like, bla NDM-1, bla NDM-5, and bla KPC genes as the main carbapenem resistance mechanisms in Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates, with bla OXA-48-like being the most prevalent.
full_output.methodology: The study used PCR and whole-genome sequencing (WGS) to detect and characterize carbapenem resistance genes in Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Efflux pumps and membrane permeability contribute to intrinsic antibiotic resistance in Mycobacterium abscessus.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several membrane transporters, including MAB_2303, MAB_2807, MAB_1963, MAB_2624c, and MAB_4116c, that contribute to intrinsic linezolid resistance in Mycobacterium abscessus through mechanisms involving efflux and membrane permeability.
full_output.methodology: Transposon mutagenesis and sequencing (TnSeq), CRISPRi knockdown, and LC-MS accumulation assays were used to identify and validate the role of membrane transporters in linezolid resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial Essential Oils as Adjuvants to Inhibit Antibiotic Resistance in Multidrug-resistant Bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that Lippia graveolens and Artemisia ludoviciana essential oils exhibit antibacterial activity and inhibit antibiotic resistance in multidrug-resistant bacteria. Specifically, L. graveolens EO showed significant resistance modulation for vancomycin, nalidixic acid, and chloramphenicol against S. aureus, E. faecalis, and P. aeruginosa.
full_output.methodology: The study used broth microdilution to determine MIC and MBC, and GC-MS for chemical analysis of essential oils.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial macrocyclic peptides reveal a distinct mode of BamA inhibition.
full_output.key_findings: Three cyclic peptides (CP1, CP2, and CP3) were identified that bind to the lumen of the BamA β-barrel and inhibit OMP assembly in E. coli. These peptides exhibit antibacterial activity against BAM-deficient strains but not wild-type strains.
full_output.methodology: mRNA display screening, surface plasmon resonance (SPR), in vitro OMP assembly assay, and molecular dynamics simulations.

full_output.paper_title: Antibiotic resistance and virulence patterns of O25 and O16 serogroups in uropathogenic Escherichia coli.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antibiotic resistance genes, including bla CTX-M, bla TEM, qnrB, qnrS, acrB, tolC, Int1, and Int2, in O25 and O16 serogroups of uropathogenic E. coli. These genes were associated with resistance to various antibiotics such as cephalosporins, fluoroquinolones, and sulfonamides.
full_output.methodology: PCR and antibiotic susceptibility testing were used to detect resistance genes and assess antibiotic resistance patterns.

full_output.paper_title: Epidemiological characteristics and trends of notified enteric fevers in Germany, 2001 to 2023.
full_output.key_findings: The paper reports on the emergence of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) in Salmonella Typhi (STY) and Salmonella Paratyphi (SP) strains in Germany, particularly noting ciprofloxacin and cefotaxime resistance in STY and SPA cases. It highlights the need for improved surveillance and targeted vaccination strategies for travelers.
full_output.methodology: The study analyzed notified enteric fever cases in Germany from 2001 to 2023, focusing on demographic, clinical, and geographic data, along with antibiotic susceptibility testing results.

full_output.paper_title: Genome analyses of amphotericin B-susceptible and -resistant strains of Leishmania (Mundinia) martiniquensis reveal variations potentially related to amphotericin B resistance.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified a stop-gained SNV in the LSCM1_02556 gene, annotated as a putative sterol C-24 reductase, and two missense SNVs in the LSCM1_01856 gene, annotated as an ABC transporter-like/ABC transporter family, which are potentially related to amphotericin B resistance in Leishmania (Mundinia) martiniquensis.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing and bioinformatic analysis were used to identify SNVs associated with amphotericin B resistance.
full_output.sample_size: Three parasite samples: LSCM1-WT, LSCM1-6, and AmpBRP2i.

full_output.paper_title: Population structure of Helicobacter pylori and antibiotic resistance-associated variants in a high-risk area of gastric cancer.

full_output.key_findings: The study identified novel resistance variants in H. pylori strains from a high-risk area of gastric cancer, including mutations in the hefA gene associated with metronidazole and tetracycline resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, MIC Test Strip, and genome-wide association study (GWAS) were used to identify resistance variants and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Phenotypic and Genomic Assessment of Antimicrobial Resistance and Virulence Factors Determinants in Salmonella Heidelberg Isolated from Broiler Chickens.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified high levels of antimicrobial resistance in Salmonella Heidelberg strains from broiler chickens in Brazil, with resistance genes tet(A), sul2, fosA7, and aac(6')-Iaa, and mutations in gyrA and parC associated with fluoroquinolone resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and disk diffusion tests were used to analyze antimicrobial resistance and identify resistance genes and mutations.

full_output.paper_title: Genome characterization, pathogenicity, and evaluation of therapeutics of Klebsiella aerogenes in Bombyx larvae infection model.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified beta-lactamase genes in the genome of the K. aerogenes strain KA1, indicating resistance to ampicillin. However, in vivo experiments showed that the strain was susceptible to ampicillin in Bombyx larvae.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and in vivo experiments using Bombyx larvae.

full_output.paper_title: Disrupting antimicrobial resistance: unveiling the potential of vitamin C in combating biofilm formation in drug-resistant bacteria.
full_output.key_findings: Vitamin C reduces biofilm formation and restores susceptibility of multidrug-resistant (MDR) isolates to antimicrobial agents by downregulating the recA gene, which is involved in the SOS response and biofilm production.
full_output.methodology: Antimicrobial susceptibility testing, biofilm assays, RT-PCR, and kinetic studies were used to evaluate the effects of vitamin C on MDR bacteria.

full_output.paper_title: Antibacterial effects of cinnamaldehyde and hesperitin on resistant Glaesserella parasuis by suppressing QseBC two-component system.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that cinnamaldehyde (CAL) and hesperitin (HES) exhibit antibacterial activity against Glaesserella parasuis by suppressing the QseBC two-component system, reducing biofilm formation, and altering membrane permeability.
full_output.methodology: The study used in vitro susceptibility testing, time-kill assays, biofilm biomass assessment, SEM, and qRT-PCR to evaluate the effects of CAL and HES on G. parasuis.

full_output.paper_title: Frequency, Antimicrobial Susceptibility, and Molecular Characterization of Carbapenem-Resistant Enterobacterales Stratified by United States Census Divisions: Results From the INFORM Program (2018-2022).
full_output.key_findings: The study characterized the molecular mechanisms of carbapenem resistance in Enterobacterales, identifying KPC, NDM, and OXA-48-like beta-lactamases as the primary resistance determinants. Aztreonam-avibactam showed potent activity against these resistant strains.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic analyses reveal presence of extensively drug-resistant Salmonella enterica serovars isolated from clinical samples in Guizhou province, China, 2019-2023.

blaTEM-1.evidence_note: The paper states that bla TEM-1 was the most common beta-lactam resistance gene (54.9%) and was located on plasmids.

blaNDM-1.genetic_context: IncHI2/IncHI2A plasmid
blaNDM-1.evidence_note: bla NDM-1 gene was identified for the first time in Salmonella from Guizhou, and one S. 1,4,[5],12:i:- isolate contained the mcr-1.1 gene.

gyrA.notes: Mutations in quinolone resistance-determining regions (QRDRs)

parC.notes: Detected in S. Kentucky

full_output.key_findings: The study identified multiple antimicrobial resistance genes and mutations in XDR Salmonella isolates from Guizhou, China, including bla TEM-1, bla CTX-M-55, qnrS1, oqxA, aac(6')-Ib-cr, tetA, mcr-1.1, and bla NDM-1, as well as mutations in gyrA and parC associated with fluoroquinolone resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were used to identify antimicrobial resistance genes and mutations in XDR Salmonella isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Comparative efficacy of levofloxacin, azithromycin, and doxycycline prophylaxis and treatment in an experimental Ureaplasma murine lung infection model.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the tetM gene as responsible for doxycycline resistance in Ureaplasma urealyticum ATCC 33175.
full_output.methodology: Minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) determination using broth microdilution.

full_output.paper_title: PKPD modeling of the inoculum effect of combined ceftazidime/avibactam and colistin against KPC-3 Klebsiella pneumoniae isolate.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterized the inoculum effect of ceftazidime/avibactam (CZA) and colistin (CST) against a KPC-3 Klebsiella pneumoniae isolate using PKPD modeling. The inoculum effect significantly reduced the efficacy of the CZA+CST combination at high inoculum levels (10^8 CFU/mL), highlighting the importance of considering inoculum effects in antibiotic combination therapies.
full_output.methodology: PKPD modeling and time-kill curve experiments were used to evaluate the inoculum effect of CZA and CST against a KPC-3 K. pneumoniae isolate.

full_output.paper_title: Staphylococcus aureus AgrA Modulators From South African Antimicrobial Plants.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified five lead metabolites from South African plants that interact with the Staphylococcus aureus AgrA protein, showing strong affinity and potential as quorum sensing inhibitors (QSIs). These metabolites include hinokiflavone, asphodelin, mamegakinone, elliptinone, and robustaflavone.
full_output.methodology: The study used molecular docking, pharmacokinetic prediction, molecular dynamics simulations, and fingerprinting to identify and analyze lead metabolites from South African plants targeting the AgrA protein of S. aureus.

full_output.paper_title: Rapid formulation of a genetically diverse phage cocktail targeting uropathogenic Escherichia coli infections using the UTI89 model.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies and characterizes two lytic phages, SR02 and SR04, which demonstrate potent antibacterial activity against uropathogenic E. coli (UPEC) strain UTI89. These phages exhibit genetic diversity and are safe for therapeutic use, as no virulence or antimicrobial resistance genes were detected in their genomes.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized phage isolation, plaque morphology analysis, restriction fragment length polymorphism (RFLP) analysis, whole-genome sequencing, and biological assays to characterize the phages and their efficacy against UPEC.

full_output.paper_title: Disruption of MRSA Biofilm and Virulence by Deep-Sea Probiotics: Impacts on Energy metabolism and Host Antimicrobial Peptides.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies three deep-sea probiotic strains (L25_4, L25_6, and L25_7) that demonstrate significant antimicrobial activity against MRSA, reducing biofilm formation and altering host antimicrobial peptide expression.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized in vitro, in vivo, and ex vivo analyses, along with transcriptomic and NMR spectroscopy techniques to evaluate the antimicrobial properties of the probiotic strains.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic characterization of plasmids of mcr-1-positive Escherichia coli isolated from cohabiting rats, dairy cattle and pigs.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified mcr-1.1 and mcr-1.5 variants in E. coli isolates from cohabiting rats and pigs, highlighting the potential for horizontal plasmid transfer and the spread of colistin resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, plasmid profiling, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were used to characterize the mcr-1-positive E. coli isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Synthesis and Biological Activity of Ultrashort Antimicrobial Peptides Bearing a Non-Coded Amino Acid.
full_output.key_findings: The study focuses on the synthesis of ultrashort antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) containing a non-coded amino acid (NCAA) called His*, which enhances the peptides' stability and antimicrobial activity. The peptides P7 and P8 showed broad-spectrum activity against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria, as well as against Saccharomyces cerevisiae, with minimal hemolysis.
full_output.methodology: The peptides were synthesized using solid-phase peptide synthesis (SPPS) and characterized using HPLC, MS, and NMR. Antimicrobial activity was assessed using the disk diffusion method, while hemolytic activity and serum stability were also evaluated.

full_output.paper_title: Identification of host genetic factors modulating β-lactam resistance in Escherichia coli harbouring plasmid-borne β-lactamase through transposon-sequencing.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies several host genetic factors, including ompF, ompA, ompC, skp, gshA, phoP, and ypfN, that modulate β-lactam resistance in E. coli harboring plasmid-borne β-lactamase. These genes are involved in outer membrane integrity, glutathione synthesis, and regulation of membrane permeability, thereby affecting β-lactam resistance.
full_output.methodology: Transposon-sequencing (Tn-Seq) and deletion mutant analysis were used to identify and validate genes involved in β-lactam resistance.

full_output.paper_title: Structural characterization, derivatization, and bioactivities of secondary metabolites produced by termite-associated Streptomyces lannensis BYF-106.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified two new C-glycoside angucycline-related analogs, urdamycin Y (1) and grincamycin W (2), along with eight known metabolites from Streptomyces lannensis BYF-106. These compounds exhibited antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, and cytotoxic activities.
full_output.methodology: The study involved chemical analysis, molecular networking, NMR spectroscopy, and bioassays to characterize the metabolites and their activities.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence of New Delhi Metallo-β-lactamase (blaNDM) gene in a selected population of drug-resistant clinical isolates.
full_output.key_findings: The study found that the blaNDM gene was prevalent in 75.27% of CRE isolates, with blaNDM-1, blaNDM-5, and blaNDM-7 variants detected. The gene was associated with high antimicrobial resistance, particularly to carbapenems.
full_output.methodology: PCR, sequencing, and susceptibility testing were used to characterize the blaNDM gene and its variants.

full_output.paper_title: Characterization of phenotypic and genotypic traits of Klebsiella pneumoniae strains resistant to 3rd generation cephalosporins in hospital settings: A case study in Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies the prevalence of AmpC beta-lactamase, ESBL, and carbapenemase genes in Klebsiella pneumoniae isolates from Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam, highlighting the high resistance rates to third-generation cephalosporins and carbapenems.
full_output.methodology: Multiplex real-time PCR and disk diffusion method were used to identify resistance genes and phenotypes in K. pneumoniae isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Evidence of hypervirulent carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae in cats with urinary affections and associated humans in Egypt.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified hypervirulent carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae in cats and humans in Egypt, highlighting the presence of various virulence and resistance genes such as entB, mrKD, iucA, iroB, peg344, rmPA, rmPA2, K2, MagA, Kfu, KPC, NDM, OXA-48, and VIM.
full_output.methodology: Molecular identification and characterization of virulence and carbapenem-resistant encoding genes using PCR techniques.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic epidemiology and characterization of difficult-to-treat resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa isolates co-harboring bla(OXA-50) and crpP causing bronchiectasis.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies bla OXA-50 and crpP as key contributors to the development of difficult-to-treat resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa (DTR-PA) in bronchiectasis patients, highlighting their co-harborance as a significant factor in multidrug resistance.
full_output.methodology: Genomic epidemiology, MLST, and antimicrobial susceptibility testing were employed to analyze resistance profiles and sequence types of P. aeruginosa isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Inhibitory effects of benzyl isothiocyanate on widespread mcr-1-harbouring IncX4 plasmid transfer.
full_output.key_findings: The study characterizes the presence of mcr-1.1, mcr-3.5, blaCTX-M-55, and tet(X4) genes in clinical isolates of Enterobacterales from Thailand, highlighting their role in multidrug resistance and the potential for horizontal gene transfer.
full_output.methodology: The study utilized PCR, sequencing, and bioinformatics tools to identify and characterize AMR genes in clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Wastewater surveillance reveals patterns of antibiotic resistance across the United States.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified and quantified 11 clinically relevant antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) in wastewater across the United States, highlighting regional variations and associations with socioeconomic factors.
full_output.methodology: Digital droplet PCR was used to quantify the abundance of 11 ARGs in wastewater samples from 163 treatment plants.

full_output.paper_title: Genomic analysis and therapeutic efficacy evaluation of bacteriophage PK2420 for pneumonia caused by hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae (K20 serotype).
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies antibiotic resistance genes in the multidrug-resistant hypervirulent Klebsiella pneumoniae strain K2420, including baeR, KpnG, and msbA, which confer resistance to multiple antibiotics.
full_output.methodology: Metagenomic analysis using the Comprehensive Antibiotic Research Database (CARD) to identify antibiotic resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: Integrated multi-omics reveals metabolic determinants of CRAB ST2 airway infection progression.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies that the biosynthesis and degradation pathways of valine, leucine, and isoleucine are downregulated in CRAB ST2 infection strains compared to colonization strains, suggesting metabolic changes may contribute to the transition from colonization to infection.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing, metabolomics, and biofilm-forming ability assessments were used to analyze CRAB ST2 strains.

full_output.paper_title: Proteins of the SubB family provide multiple mechanisms of serum resistance in Yersinia pestis.

full_output.key_findings: The study identifies ypo0337 as a gene encoding an outer-membrane-associated lectin that confers resistance to all three complement pathways by recruiting factor H, C4BP, and hemopexin. The serine at position 12 of YPO0337 is crucial for this function.
full_output.methodology: Mutant generation, complementation, serum survival assays, Western blot, and pull-down experiments.

full_output.paper_title: Performance of disk diffusion, gradient test, and VITEK 2 for carbapenem susceptibility testing in OXA-48-like carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales: a comparative study.
full_output.key_findings: The study compared the performance of disk diffusion, gradient test (ETEST), and VITEK 2 for carbapenem susceptibility testing in OXA-48-like carbapenemase-producing Enterobacterales (CPE). It found that ETEST showed the highest essential agreement (EA) for meropenem and ertapenem, while VITEK 2 AST-N428 performed best for imipenem. The study highlights the variability in resistance frequencies, MICs, and agreement rates across different testing methods.
full_output.methodology: The study used broth microdilution (BMD) as the reference method and compared it with disk diffusion, gradient test (ETEST), and VITEK 2. Whole-genome sequencing (WGS) was used to molecularly characterize the isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Detection of Antibiotic-Resistance Genes in Drinking Water: A Study at a University in the Peruvian Amazon.
full_output.key_findings: The study detected the presence of antibiotic-resistance genes (ermC, amp, QEP, marA, and qEmarA) in all water samples analyzed, highlighting the widespread dissemination of resistance factors in drinking water.
full_output.methodology: Conventional PCR was used to detect antibiotic-resistance genes in water samples.

full_output.paper_title: Genotypic drug resistance and transmission clusters of Mycobacterium tuberculosis isolates among Ethiopian returnees from Saudi Arabia.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified 40 gene mutations conferring resistance to first- and second-line anti-TB drugs among M. tuberculosis isolates from Ethiopian returnees in Saudi Arabia, including mutations in katG, rpoB, gid, rpsL, rrs, embB, pncA, tlyA, ethA, and fbiC.
full_output.methodology: Whole genome sequencing (WGS) was used to analyze drug resistance and transmission clusters of M. tuberculosis isolates from 88 returnees.

full_output.paper_title: The ongoing antibiotic resistance and carbapenemase encoding genotypes surveillance. The first quarter report of the INVIFAR network for 2024.
full_output.key_findings: The study identifies bla NDM, bla KPC, bla OXA24, and bla GES as carbapenemase-encoding genes in various bacterial species, highlighting their role in carbapenem resistance.
full_output.methodology: Polymerase chain reaction tests were used to detect carbapenemase-encoding genes in clinical isolates.

full_output.paper_title: Genome-based assessment of antimicrobial resistance of Escherichia coli recovered from diseased swine in eastern China for a 12-year period.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified the emergence of plasmid-mediated colistin resistance genes mcr-1 and mcr-3 in animals and humans in China, highlighting the significance of these genes in the spread of colistin resistance. Additionally, the tet(X4) gene was detected, indicating tetracycline resistance.
full_output.methodology: Whole-genome sequencing and bioinformatics analysis were employed to identify and characterize the resistance genes.

full_output.paper_title: The Impact of Tetracycline on the Soil Microbiome and the Rhizosphere of Lettuce (Lactuca sativa L.).
full_output.key_findings: The study examined the impact of tetracycline on the soil and rhizosphere microbiome of lettuce, noting the presence of Mycobacterium tuberculosis and Mycobacterium holsaticum in tetracycline-treated soil, suggesting potential implications for antibiotic resistance and pathogen transmission.
full_output.methodology: Soil and rhizosphere samples were collected and analyzed using metagenomic sequencing to assess microbial community changes in response to tetracycline exposure.

full_output.paper_title: Transcriptomic Analysis of Campylobacter jejuni Following Exposure to Gaseous Chlorine Dioxide Reveals an Oxidative Stress Response.
full_output.key_findings: Exposure to gaseous ClO2 induces an oxidative stress response in Campylobacter jejuni, leading to upregulation of genes involved in ROS detoxification, iron transport, phosphate transport, and DNA repair.
full_output.methodology: RNA-Seq and qRT-PCR were used to analyze gene expression changes in C. jejuni following exposure to gaseous ClO2.

full_output.paper_title: A New Strategy to Prevent Emerging Lactococcus garvieae Infections by Using Organic Acids as Antimicrobials In Vitro and Ex Vivo.
full_output.key_findings: The study shows that the organic acid mixture Aq significantly inhibits L. garvieae growth, reduces EPS production, and downregulates virulence genes such as hly1, hly2, and hly3, thereby decreasing its pathogenicity.
full_output.methodology: The study used MIC/MBC assays, gene expression analysis, and haemolysis assays to evaluate the effect of Aq on L. garvieae.

full_output.paper_title: Verapamil and its metabolite norverapamil inhibit the Mycobacterium tuberculosis MmpS5L5 efflux pump to increase bedaquiline activity.
full_output.key_findings: Mutations in Rv0678 lead to increased resistance by upregulating the MmpS5L5 efflux pump, which can be inhibited by verapamil and norverapamil to enhance bedaquiline activity.
full_output.methodology: Genetic manipulation, MIC assays, and efflux pump inhibition studies.

full_output.paper_title: Prevalence, virulence factors, and antibiotic resistance of Staphylococcus aureus in seafood products.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified several antibiotic resistance genes in Staphylococcus aureus isolated from seafood products, including blaZ, mecA, tetM, and ermA. These genes were associated with resistance to penicillin G, ampicillin, tetracycline, and erythromycin, respectively.
full_output.methodology: PCR detection of resistance genes and virulence factors, along with antimicrobial susceptibility testing using the Kirby-Bauer disc diffusion method.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical and molecular characteristics of Staphylococcus aureus isolates from patients with COVID-19 in Southwest China.
full_output.key_findings: The study identified various Staphylococcus aureus isolates from patients with COVID-19 in Southwest China, highlighting differences in antimicrobial resistance patterns and virulence gene carriage among different sequence types (STs).
full_output.methodology: The study involved multilocus sequence typing, antimicrobial susceptibility testing, and PCR-based detection of virulence genes in S. aureus isolates from patients with COVID-19.

full_output.paper_title: Clinical burden of Acinetobacter baumannii, including carbapenem-resistant A. baumannii, in hospitalized adult patients in the USA between 2018 and 2022.
full_output.key_findings: The study highlights the significant clinical burden of Acinetobacter baumannii, particularly carbapenem-resistant A. baumannii (CRAB), in hospitalized adult patients in the USA between 2018 and 2022. It identifies regional variations in CRAB incidence and notes the association of CRAB with higher mortality and longer hospital stays.
full_output.methodology: Retrospective cohort study analyzing data from the PINC AI™ Database to determine the incidence and outcomes of A. baumannii and CRAB in hospitalized patients.

full_output.paper_title: Mycoplasma genitalium infection in Eswatini amid syndromic case management: prevalence, coinfections, diagnostic challenges and treatment gaps.
